Purge inactive deletes every inactive volunteer at once. You type the volunteer's id, or the count, to confirm. It can't be undone: their picks, notes, check-ins and ratings go with them, and their slots become empty.

Volunteers manage their own registration in the portal. They can change their shifts and some answers, cancel, and rejoin. A cancelled volunteer's slots show as needing a replacement.

docs.title: Assigning volunteers
docs.text:
On the Schedule tab, pick a day and a time, then click a slot. The dialog suggests volunteers in groups: those who requested that timeslot, those who said they're flexible, those who are available, and the rest. Anyone already working an overlapping shift that day is left out.

The banner above the schedule lists what needs attention:

  • Slots needing a replacement, because their volunteer cancelled or was made inactive. Open goes to the slot.
  • Dropped shifts: a volunteer changed their picks in the portal and no longer wants a shift they're assigned to. Unassign them, or Keep the assignment after you've talked to them.

docs.title: Sending schedules
docs.text:
1. Call for Volunteers → Schedule Email: write the message in Markdown, add images, and preview it for any volunteer with their real shifts and QR codes.
  2. Download package.
  3. Send with vol_mail from your own machine. See vol_mail and tools/vol_mail/README.md. Usually that's a draft round, then a final round to the people whose shifts changed.

vol_mail needs an export API key, made under Admin → API Keys with the volunteers:read, volunteers:email and checkin:codes scopes. A key is shown once, so save it straight away.

App Settings → Rotate key voids every check-in code already sent. Only use it if codes have leaked, and send the schedules again afterwards.

docs.title: At the event
docs.text:
Check-in. Check In Volunteer on the Schedule tab opens the scanner. Scan the QR code from the volunteer's schedule email, or type the code. If the volunteer is more than 45 minutes early or 10 minutes late, it asks first: Check in anyway records the check-in with the timing. A slot's dialog has a Check In button too.

Checked-in slots glow green. Past slots with nobody checked in pulse red.

Ratings and notes. A slot's dialog can rate the volunteer Good, Bad or No-Show, and holds notes for that slot.

Radios. On the Radios tab, Check Out a radio by scanning its barcode and choosing the volunteer, or typing a name. A radio registers itself the first time it's scanned. Scanning a radio someone else holds hands it over. To return radios, press Check In and scan each one. The tab lists what's out, what's available, and the full log.

docs.title: Security alerts
docs.text:
The site watches its own audit log and emails a security alert when something looks wrong or important, for example:

  • many failed sign-ins from one address, or for one account
  • someone trying lots of different usernames
  • an account created, or its role changed
  • another person's password, passkeys or reset address changed
  • the volunteer email key replaced, or an export API key created
  • an organizer signing in from a network they haven't used in the last 30 days
  • requests to the organizer site or the volunteer pages that look like an attack (SQL or script injection, scanning tools), or one address piling up errors
  • input to the volunteer pages that the pages themselves would never send, such as a name with digits or a field the form doesn't have. Someone is calling the portal directly.

Alerts go to the organizers ticked under Security alerts in Admin → Users who have an email address in Profile. At first that's only the first organizer account; any organizer can tick or untick anyone. If nobody qualifies, alerts are still recorded but not sent, and the Users and Audit Log screens say so in red. Each alert links to the audit log.

One kind of alert comes at most once an hour for the same cause. Anything more in that hour is counted and sent as a "(continued)" summary when the hour is up, so a sustained attack is a trickle of mail, not a flood, and nothing goes unreported because it stopped.

Treat what's in an alert as untrusted. Details such as a username can be whatever the attacker typed, and anything that looked like a link has been broken on purpose. Open the site yourself rather than following anything in the details.

docs.title: The audit log
docs.text:
Admin → Audit Log (for every organizer) lists everything the site has recorded, newest first: sign-ins and failed attempts, account and role changes, schedule and volunteer changes, export API calls, attack patterns noticed in requests, and every alert. Filter by kind of event, severity, who, address, which site, or words in the message, and open a row to see its details. Alert emails link straight here.

The card at the top shows who alerts reach, and warns if that's nobody. Send test alert emails everyone there now, to check the mail path end to end.

docs.title: Your own account
docs.text:
Profile, under your name in the top right, changes your own password and email. Both need your current password. It's also where you add a passkey, so you can sign in without a password.

If you forget your password, Send Reset Link on the sign-in page mails a link to the address on your account. An organizer can also set a new password for you under Admin → Users.

After 5 wrong passwords in 15 minutes, the sign-in page stops accepting that username from your network for a while and says how long to wait. Waiting more is the only fix; more attempts don't help. A passkey or a reset link still works in the meantime, and so does signing in from another network. Successful sign-ins never count, so a check-in desk full of laptops on the venue's network can't lock itself out.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Every setting comes from .env in the repo root. podman-compose reads it, and compose.yml passes each service the variables that service needs. Start from .env.example, which has the same settings with comments.

.env holds secrets. It's ignored by git and must never be committed. Secret settings are marked secret below, and Secrets covers how each one is generated and rotated.

docs.title: Not here: the conference's details
docs.text: The conference's name, contact email, website and code-of-conduct link are set in the app, not in .env: in the setup wizard, and later under Admin → App Settings. They're pushed to the portal with the logos, and the volunteer pages show them.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Setting Read by Default What it does POSTGRES_PASSWORD postgres, backend changeme Secret. The scheduler role's password. compose gives the backend the same value as DB_PASSWORD.

The backend also reads DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME and DB_USER. compose sets them to the postgres service, so they don't belong in .env. The portal's SQLite file is PORTAL_DB, set to /data/portal.db on the portal_data volume.

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text: Setting Read by Default What it does AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS backend 365 How many days the audit_events table keeps an event. It's pruned at startup and once a day. 0 keeps everything. logs/audit.jsonl is never pruned: it's the complete record (see Deployment for rotating it).

docs.title: Shared between the backend and the portal
docs.text:
These must be identical on both sides. The backend and the portal compare fingerprints on every sync heartbeat, and the admin site's Volunteer Portal dialog shows a mismatch.

Setting Default What it does EMAIL_HMAC_KEY none, required Secret. The key behind each volunteer's email_hmac, which is how an address is looked up without being stored readable. Never stored in either database. The portal refuses to start without it. Changing it locks every volunteer out. SYNC_KEY_ID none, required by the portal Names the signing secret, e.g. bsc-2026. Sent with every sync request. SYNC_SECRET none, required by the portal Secret. Signs every request from the scheduler to the portal. SYNC_SECRET_PREV empty Secret. During a rotation, the old secret, so the portal accepts both until the backend restarts with the new one.

docs.title: Where the services find each other
docs.text: Setting Read by Default What it does PORTAL_SYNC_URL backend http://portal:5001 in .env.example Where the backend reaches the portal's sync API, over the compose network. Empty runs the scheduler with no portal at all: the sync loop never starts. PORTAL_PUBLIC_URL backend, portal http://localhost:8080 The public site's origin, as volunteers see it. Sign-in links and early-access invite links are built on it. ADMIN_PUBLIC_URL backend, portal PORTAL_PUBLIC_URL The organizer site's origin: the base of admin invite and password-reset links, and the passkey relying party. Changing its hostname orphans every passkey. Leave it unset when one origin serves both, as in local development. PORTAL_SYNC_INTERVAL backend 30 Seconds between sync passes. A change calls for a push sooner, after a 2-second debounce. PORTAL_SYNC_VERIFY_TLS backend 1 Set to 0 only for a self-signed portal certificate in development.

docs.title: Portal mail
docs.text: Setting Read by Default What it does MAIL_BACKEND portal file file writes .eml files to logs/portal_mail/ and sends nothing. smtp sends through SMTP_HOST. relay hands plain text to the mail relay, which sends through Microsoft Graph. SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER portal empty, 587, empty The SMTP server, for MAIL_BACKEND=smtp. STARTTLS is always used. SMTP_PASS portal empty Secret. For MAIL_BACKEND=smtp. SMTP_FROM portal volunteers@example.org The From address, for MAIL_BACKEND=smtp. The relay sends as MAIL_SENDER instead.

docs.title: Mail relay
docs.text:
Used with MAIL_BACKEND=relay. Setup is in Graph mail setup.

Setting Read by Default What it does MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN portal, mailrelay none Secret. The bearer token the portal sends with each message. At least 32 characters. GRAPH_TENANT_ID mailrelay none The Entra tenant ID. GRAPH_CLIENT_ID mailrelay none The app registration's client ID. There is no client secret. RELAY_MAILBOX mailrelay none The account that signs in with a device code, and whose Sent Items keep a copy. It needs Send As on MAIL_SENDER. login refuses to save a sign-in for any other account. MAIL_SENDER mailrelay none The From address of everything the relay sends, e.g. volunteers@example.org, usually a Microsoft 365 group. Required: the relay won't start without it, or with anything but one plain address. Set here rather than in the app because it's tied to the tenant's Send As permission, and a request can never change it.

The relay also reads RELAY_PORT (5002), RELAY_STATE_DIR (/state), RELAY_RATE_PER_MIN (20) and RELAY_RATE_PER_HOUR (300). compose doesn't pass them, so they keep those defaults.

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does FRONTEND_PORT 8080 Host port for the full site, on 127.0.0.1. The tunnel sends the admin hostname here. PORTAL_SITE_PORT 8082 Host port for the public pages only, on 127.0.0.1. The tunnel sends the public hostname here.

Keep both above 1024, since rootless podman can't bind lower ports.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Setting Read by What it does DEPLOY_HOST you, for rsync The server to copy the repo to: rsync -aF BSides/ "$DEPLOY_HOST:Scheduler/". No container reads it. It lives in .env so the address isn't in the repo.

docs.title: Portal input validation
docs.text: Setting Read by Default What it does PORTAL_STRICT portal report How strictly the portal treats input the volunteer pages can't send (a name with digits, an unknown field, an invisible character). Either way it's recorded as a portal.anomaly event and the organizers ticked for security alerts are emailed. report then lets the request through as before; enforce refuses it with a bare 400. Start with report, check the audit log for anomalies from real volunteers, then switch to enforce. Anything else stops the portal at startup.

docs.title: Portal tuning
docs.text:
The portal reads these, but compose doesn't pass them, so they keep their defaults unless you add them to the portal service's environment.

Setting Default What it does PORTAL_TOKEN_TTL_MIN 15 How long a sign-in link works. PORTAL_SESSION_TTL_HOURS 12 A volunteer session's lifetime. PORTAL_REMEMBER_TTL_DAYS 90 A "Remember this browser" session's lifetime, rolled forward with use. PORTAL_RATE_PER_MIN, PORTAL_RATE_PER_HOUR 5, 30 Link requests per client address (IPv6 by /64) and per email address. PORTAL_RESPONSE_FLOOR_MS 250 The minimum time a link request takes, so timing doesn't tell whether an address is registered. SYNC_SKEW_SEC 300 How far a signed request's timestamp may be from the portal's clock.

docs.title: vol_mail
docs.text:
The schedule mailer runs on an organizer's machine and doesn't read .env. Export its settings in the shell first:

Setting What it is GRAPH_TENANT_ID, GRAPH_CLIENT_ID The same app registration as the relay. VOL_MAIL_MAILBOX The account that signs in. It needs Send As on MAIL_SENDER. MAIL_SENDER The From address, as for the relay. --from overrides it, and send stops without one.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The production site runs on one host under rootless podman-compose, reached only through a tunnel from an edge service that terminates TLS and gates the admin site. This page covers how it's laid out, how to ship a change, and the less routine jobs: the first install, upgrading PostgreSQL and backups.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    v([Volunteers]) --> cf[Edge<br/>TLS]
    o([Organizers]) --> cfa[Access gate] --> cf
    i([Integrators and<br/>tools/vol_mail]) -.->|"/api/export/*<br/>bypasses the gate, bearer key"| cf
    cf --> cfd[Tunnel client<br/>on the host]
    subgraph host [Host: podman-compose]
        cfd -->|127.0.0.1:8082| fe8082[frontend nginx<br/>public pages]
        cfd -->|127.0.0.1:8080| fe8080[frontend nginx<br/>full site]
        fe8082 -->|/api/portal/*| portal
        fe8080 -->|/api/portal/*| portal
        fe8080 -->|"/api/* (incl. /api/export/*)"| backend
        backend --> postgres[(postgres)]
        backend -->|signed sync API| portal
        portal --> pdb[(portal.db)]
        portal -->|mail_internal| mailrelay
    end
    mailrelay -->|mail_egress| msgraph[Microsoft Graph]
Hostname Host port Serves Gate public (PORTAL_PUBLIC_URL) PORTAL_SITE_PORT (8082) /, /apply/*, assets, /api/portal/*. Everything else is a 404. public admin (ADMIN_PUBLIC_URL) FRONTEND_PORT (8080) the full site: /admin and /api/* the access gate, bypassed for /api/export/*

The real hostnames are in .env, not in the repo.

  • Nothing else publishes a port. The portal, the backend, PostgreSQL and the relay are reachable only on the compose networks.
  • Both published ports are loopback-only. TLS ends at the edge, so nginx serves plain HTTP that must not be reachable from the LAN.
  • The export API bypasses the gate because the servers that call it carry a bearer key instead. See Export API.
  • nginx takes the client address from the edge's client-IP header, named in frontend/default.conf. The portal's rate limits depend on it, so a different edge has to send that header, or default.conf has to name the one it does send.
  • The mail relay is on two networks: mail_internal, shared only with the portal and with no route out, and mail_egress, its way to Microsoft.

The tunnel client runs on the host, not in compose, so the stack can be rebuilt without dropping the tunnel.

docs.title: Shipping a change
docs.text:
From the directory above the repo on your machine, copy it to the server:

set -a; . BSides/.env; set +a        # for DEPLOY_HOST
rsync -aF BSides/ "$DEPLOY_HOST:Scheduler/"

.rsync-filter keeps keys, development tooling, the docs, tools/ and the legacy app off the server. It also protects the server's own files, such as logs/, so --delete is safe to add. .env is copied, because the containers read it. Then, on the server:

cd ~/Scheduler
./maintenance.sh on        # stack down, "back soon" page up
podman-compose build
./maintenance.sh off       # maintenance page down, stack up

Restart the whole stack this way, not one service at a time. Migrations run by themselves when the backend and the portal start.

The maintenance page is a separate compose project (compose.maintenance.yml, project bsides-maintenance) with one nginx on the same two loopback ports, so the tunnel needs no change. Every page is a 503 with Retry-After, and every /api/* call is a JSON 503 that the apps can show. Everything it serves is in maintenance/, since nothing else is running. ./maintenance.sh status shows which stack is up. The two can't run at once because they want the same ports.

docs.title: Why the restarts work this way
docs.text:
podman-compose turns each depends_on into a hard podman --requires link. A required container can't be removed while a dependent exists, and down stops containers one at a time. So only backend → postgres keeps a depends_on. nginx resolves the backend and the portal on every request instead, and returns 502 until they're up.

Total stop time is the sum of every container's. That's why the frontend stops on SIGTERM and uvicorn has a 3-second graceful shutdown: without them, open /api/events streams held each container to podman's 10-second kill.

docs.title: First install
docs.text:
1. Install podman, podman-compose and your tunnel's client on the host. Create the tunnel, with the public hostname pointed at http://127.0.0.1:8082 and the admin hostname at http://127.0.0.1:8080.
  2. At the edge, put an access gate (organizer sign-in) on the admin hostname, with a bypass for the path /api/export/*. Check the edge sends the client-IP header that frontend/default.conf reads.
  3. Write .env on your machine from .env.example. Configuration describes every setting.
  4. Run rsync and the build as above, then podman-compose up -d.
  5. Open the admin hostname. The setup wizard creates the first organizer.
  6. Upload the organizers' public key (Admin → Email Key). Signup can't open without it.
  7. To send mail for real, set up the relay: Graph mail setup.

docs.title: Upgrading to 1.1 (audit log and alerts)
docs.text:
1.1 adds the audit log's table, security alerts, request watching and strict input checks on the volunteer pages. Ship it the usual way (above): it changes the backend, the portal and the frontend's nginx, so rebuild all three, and both databases migrate by themselves on start. Before and after:

  1. .env: add PORTAL_STRICT=report (the default if it's missing) and, if you want a retention other than a year, AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (see Configuration).
  2. Who gets alerts. Alerts are emailed to the organizers ticked under Security alerts in Admin → Users who have an address in Profile. On an upgraded database that starts as the earliest organizer account; tick others there.
  3. After the restart: open Admin → Audit Log and press Send test alert. The email should arrive within a minute, and its link should open the Audit Log.
  4. The old log: logs/audit.log stops growing; logs/audit.jsonl takes over. Keep or archive the old file. Set up rotation for the new one (Backups → Rotating the audit log).
  5. A few days later: if the Audit Log shows no portal.anomaly events from real volunteers (filter on Portal anomalies), set PORTAL_STRICT=enforce and restart the portal.

Rolling back is the 1.0 code on the same databases: neither app refuses a schema newer than its own, and 1.1 only adds a table and columns, which 1.0 ignores. Take the usual backup before upgrading anyway.

docs.title: Upgrading PostgreSQL
docs.text:
The official image keeps its data in a directory named for the major version, and refuses to start on an older major's data. The database is small, so a major upgrade is a dump and restore into a fresh volume, not pg_upgrade. The 16 → 18 upgrade was done on 2026-11-01.

For the next one, add a pgdata19 volume, point the postgres service's image and mount at it in compose.yml, and on the server:

cd ~/Scheduler
podman-compose stop backend                     # no writes during the dump
podman exec scheduler_postgres_1 pg_dump -U scheduler -Fc scheduler > ~/pg-old.dump
chmod 600 ~/pg-old.dump                         # outside ~/Scheduler: rsync --delete
COUNTS="select table_name, (xpath('/row/c/text()', query_to_xml(format('select count(*) as c from %I', table_name), false, true, '')))[1]::text::int from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public' and table_type='BASE TABLE' order by 1"
podman exec scheduler_postgres_1 psql -U scheduler -d scheduler -Atc "$COUNTS" > ~/pg-old-counts.txt
podman-compose down
# rsync the new compose.yml, then:
podman-compose up -d postgres                   # wait for (healthy)
podman exec -i scheduler_postgres_1 pg_restore -U scheduler -d scheduler --no-owner --exit-on-error < ~/pg-old.dump
podman exec scheduler_postgres_1 psql -U scheduler -d scheduler -Atc "$COUNTS" | diff ~/pg-old-counts.txt - && echo "row counts match"
podman-compose up -d

To roll back, put the old image and mount back in compose.yml: the old volume is never touched. Once the new version has settled, podman volume rm the old volume and shred -u the dump, which holds volunteer names and email ciphertext.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
What Where How Scheduler database pgdata18 volume podman exec scheduler_postgres_1 pg_dump -U scheduler -Fc scheduler > backup.dump Portal database portal_data volume, /data/portal.db sqlite3 /data/portal.db ".backup '/data/backups/portal-$(date +%F-%H%M).db'" inside the container. Never cp: with WAL, a copied file can be torn. Relay sign-in mailrelay_state volume Don't back it up. Run relay.py login again instead. Audit log logs/audit.jsonl (bind mount; audit.log before the JSON log) an ordinary file .env and private.pem your machine keep them in a password manager. See Secrets.

Both database dumps hold volunteer names and email ciphertext. Keep them owner-only (chmod 600), and don't leave them in ~/Scheduler, where an rsync with --delete would remove them.

docs.title: Rotating the audit log
docs.text:
logs/audit.jsonl grows for as long as the site runs; the backend never trims it (the audit_events table, which the admin site reads, is pruned separately by AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS). The backend opens the file for each line it writes, so an ordinary rename-based rotation is safe, with no restart and no copytruncate. For example, in /etc/logrotate.d/bsides (or a user crontab running logrotate with its own state file):

/home/<user>/Scheduler/logs/audit.jsonl {
    monthly
    rotate 24
    compress
    delaycompress
    missingok
    notifempty
    create 0640
}

Use the owner ls -ln logs/audit.jsonl shows: the container's :U mount maps it to the backend's uid.

docs.title: Sending portal mail through Microsoft Graph
docs.text:
The portal sends sign-in links as the conference's volunteer address (MAIL_SENDER in .env, e.g. volunteers@example.org) using the Microsoft Graph sendMail API over HTTPS. This works even though SMTP AUTH is disabled in the tenant.

The credential lives only in the mailrelay container, not in the portal. The portal hands the relay a plain-text {to, subject, body}, and the relay always sends as MAIL_SENDER. See Mail relay.

The relay uses delegated Mail.Send: it acts as a real account (RELAY_MAILBOX in .env), which signs in once with a device code. It needs no admin consent and no client secret. Here's how it works:

  • The sender is usually a Microsoft 365 group, and Graph can't send from a group directly.
  • So the relay sends from the relay mailbox with From set to MAIL_SENDER, and Exchange checks the relay mailbox's Send As right on the group.
  • The relay can send as the relay mailbox and as anything the relay mailbox has Send As on. It can't read mail.

docs.title: 0. Before you start
docs.text:
• Check that the relay mailbox has Send As on MAIL_SENDER. Being a member isn't enough. Check from Exchange Online PowerShell (see "Running Exchange PowerShell" at the end): 
    $RELAY_MAILBOX = '<RELAY_MAILBOX from .env>'
$MAIL_SENDER   = '<MAIL_SENDER from .env>'
# Expect AccessRights {SendAs}. The message then shows the sender address only.
Get-RecipientPermission $MAIL_SENDER | Where-Object Trustee -eq $RELAY_MAILBOX
# Send on Behalf only: still sends, but shows "<name> on behalf of <group>".
Get-UnifiedGroup $MAIL_SENDER | Format-List GrantSendOnBehalfTo
    To grant Send As: Exchange admin center → Groups → the group → Settings → Send As, or Add-RecipientPermission $MAIL_SENDER -Trustee $RELAY_MAILBOX -AccessRights SendAs.
  • Check that DKIM is on for the sender's domain. In the Defender portal (security.microsoft.com), go to Email & collaboration → Policies & rules → Threat policies → Email authentication settings → DKIM. The domain should show Enabled. If it doesn't, follow the prompts to publish the two CNAME records and then enable it. DKIM does more than anything else here to keep sign-in links out of spam.

docs.title: 1. Set up the app registration (Entra admin center)
docs.text:
As the app's owner you can do all of this without an admin.

  1. Go to entra.microsoft.com and open Identity → Applications → App registrations. Open BSides Volunteer Portal Mailer, or create it with New registration:
  2. Supported account types: this organizational directory only
  3. Redirect URI: leave it blank
  4. On the Overview page, copy these two values:
  5. Application (client) ID, which goes in GRAPH_CLIENT_ID
  6. Directory (tenant) ID, which goes in GRAPH_TENANT_ID
  7. Go to Authentication → Advanced settings and set Allow public client flows to Yes, then click Save. Device-code sign-in needs this setting.
  8. Go to API permissions. Add Microsoft Graph → Delegated permissions for:
  9. Mail.Send
  10. offline_access
  11. openid
  12. profile

Remove the Application Mail.Send permission if it's still listed. Nobody approved it, and if someone approves it later, it would let the app send as everyone in the tenant. 5. Go to Certificates & secrets and delete any client secrets. The relay doesn't use them, so there's no reason to keep a credential around.

docs.title: 2. Configure the portal and the relay
docs.text:
Add these to the deployment .env. Remove GRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET if it's still there.

MAIL_BACKEND=relay
MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN=<output of: openssl rand -hex 32>   # shared by portal and relay
GRAPH_TENANT_ID=<Directory (tenant) ID>              # relay only
GRAPH_CLIENT_ID=<Application (client) ID>            # relay only
RELAY_MAILBOX=<organizer>@example.org               # relay only: the account that signs in
MAIL_SENDER=volunteers@example.org                   # relay and vol_mail: the From address

The From address is always MAIL_SENDER. It's set here, once per deployment, never by a request, and the relay won't start without it. The relay needs outbound HTTPS access to login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com. The portal needs neither.

docs.title: 3. Start the relay and sign in
docs.text:
podman-compose up -d --build mailrelay
podman-compose logs mailrelay   # "ready ... through <RELAY_MAILBOX>" and "not signed in" (expected)
podman-compose exec mailrelay python relay.py login

login prints a code and a URL (microsoft.com/devicelogin):

  1. Open the URL in any browser and enter the code.
  2. Sign in as the RELAY_MAILBOX account and approve the permissions.
  3. The command finishes with Signed in as <RELAY_MAILBOX>.

If you sign in as a different account, it refuses to save anything.

The sign-in is saved on the mailrelay_state volume, and the running relay picks it up without a restart. To check:

podman-compose exec mailrelay python -c "import urllib.request; print(urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:5002/health').read())"
# b'{"ok": true, "signed_in": true}'

docs.title: 4. Test it
docs.text:
Restart the stack so the portal picks up MAIL_BACKEND=relay and joins the mail_internal network (see Deployment). Then send one message through the whole path, portal to relay to Graph:

./maintenance.sh on; podman-compose build; ./maintenance.sh off
podman-compose exec portal python mailer.py --test you@example.com

If it succeeds, it prints sent via relay: <id>, and podman-compose logs mailrelay shows send <id> ok. Check three things:

  • The message arrived and is not in spam. Gmail and Outlook.com are both worth trying.
  • From shows only the sender address, not " on behalf of …" (see step 0), and the headers show spf=pass, dkim=pass and dmarc=pass.
  • A copy appears in the relay mailbox's Sent Items.

    • Then try the real flow. Go to /apply/, enter the address of a volunteer who is already registered, and click the link you receive.

    Last, check that only the portal can reach the relay. Run this from the backend container. It should fail with a name-resolution or connection error:

    podman-compose exec backend python3 -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://mailrelay:5002/health', timeout=5)"

docs.title: Keeping it signed in
docs.text:
The sign-in stops working if the relay mailbox's password changes, if a Conditional Access policy asks for sign-in again, if the account is disabled, or if the relay goes 90 days without sending (likely between conferences). Sends then fail with sign-in expired, and the fix is to run login again:

podman-compose exec mailrelay python relay.py login

Nothing tells you automatically, so run the --test command before each event.

To revoke the sign-in on purpose, go to myaccount.microsoft.com → Apps & services, or delete the volume with podman volume rm <project>_mailrelay_state after stopping the relay.

docs.title: Common failures
docs.text: Error Usual cause mail relay unreachable The relay isn't running (see its logs; it exits if a setting is missing), or the portal wasn't recreated after mail_internal was added mail relay returned 401 MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN differs between the two containers; recreate both after changing it mail relay returned 503: not signed in Run relay.py login (step 3) mail relay returned 503: sign-in expired See "Keeping it signed in" login: AADSTS7000218 ... client_assertion or client_secret Allow public client flows isn't on (step 1.3) login: AADSTS65001 consent / AADSTS90094 admin approval The tenant doesn't let users consent to these delegated permissions; an admin has to approve them login: AADSTS50199 / AADSTS53003 Conditional Access blocks device-code sign-in login: signed in as X, but RELAY_MAILBOX is ... You signed in with the wrong account; run it again login: no refresh token returned offline_access is missing from the delegated permissions AADSTS700016 application not found Wrong tenant ID or client ID ErrorSendAsDenied the relay mailbox doesn't have Send As on MAIL_SENDER (see step 0) ErrorAccessDenied / 403 The delegated Mail.Send permission wasn't approved during login; run it again and accept

docs.title: If better access comes later
docs.text: With an admin's help, an app-only setup removes the dependence on the relay mailbox's sign-in: either Exchange RBAC for Applications scoped to one mailbox, or tenant-wide Mail.Send with admin consent. Switching means changing the relay's token code back to the client-credentials flow. The input checks, network layout and portal stay the same.

docs.title: Running Exchange PowerShell
docs.text:
Use any of these. Commands that change permissions need the Exchange Administrator role.

  • Azure Cloud Shell, if your tenant has it: shell.azure.com → PowerShell.
  • A container: podman run -it --rm mcr.microsoft.com/powershell, then Install-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement -Scope CurrentUser -Force.
  • PowerShell installed locally: on Fedora, sudo dnf install powershell after adding Microsoft's RHEL package repository.

Then connect. In a container, or anywhere else without a browser, add -Device; it prints a code to enter at microsoft.com/devicelogin:

$RELAY_MAILBOX = '<RELAY_MAILBOX from .env>'
Connect-ExchangeOnline -UserPrincipalName $RELAY_MAILBOX -Device

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
Each release is a git tag, plus a copy of these docs on GitHub Pages as they stood at that tag. mike publishes the docs: one folder per version on the gh-pages branch, a latest alias that follows the newest, and a version menu in the header.

URL Shows https://securgeek.github.io/volunteer-manager/ redirects to latest https://securgeek.github.io/volunteer-manager/latest/ the newest release https://securgeek.github.io/volunteer-manager/1.0/ the docs as of the 1.0 release, unchanged

Docs versions are MAJOR.MINOR. A patch release (1.0.1) republishes 1.0 in place, and a new minor or major version (1.1, 2.0) gets its own folder. Tag the release itself however you like, e.g. v1.0.0.

docs.title: Schema changes
docs.text:
Each release that changes a database schema has one file per app for it: backend/migrations/<release>.sql and portal/migrations/<release>.sql. 1.0 has none, since it's the baseline: the full schema files, backend/scheduler.sql and portal/portal.sql.

  • When the first schema change of a release goes in, add its file and an entry to SCHEMA_RELEASES in that app's db.py, marked in progress, for example ("1.1", 20, "1.1.sql", True). Every later schema change in that release goes into the same file. Make the same change to the full schema file too, since that's what a fresh install gets.
  • While it's in progress, the file re-runs every time the app starts, so a development database picks up each addition. Write it to be safe to run twice: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS (Postgres), ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. The portal skips an ADD COLUMN that's already there.
  • When you tag the release, set the entry's last field to False. Production then applies the file exactly once.

To check a database that got where it is by upgrades matches a fresh install, run tools/schema_check.sh. It compares tables, columns, defaults, indexes and constraints, and reads the live databases only. tools/ isn't on the server, so run it over ssh:

ssh "$DEPLOY_HOST" 'cd Scheduler && bash -s' < tools/schema_check.sh

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Run these from a clean checkout of the commit you're releasing, with the venv that has requirements-dev.txt installed activated (. .venv/bin/activate). mike starts the docs build as a separate command found on your PATH (mkdocs, or properdocs when that's installed, as the gen-files and literate-nav plugins now pull in). Without the venv first on PATH it finds a system copy that lacks mike's plugin, and fails with The "mike" plugin is not installed.

  1. Check it passes.

    ./run_tests.sh            # with TEST_PG_* set: see Getting started
./run_lint.sh             # pylint, bandit, and the strict docs build

  2. Finish the changelog. In CHANGELOG.md at the repo root, rename Unreleased to the version and date (## [1.1.0] — 2026-12-05), start a new empty Unreleased above it, and update the compare links at the bottom. If upgrading needs anything beyond the usual deploy (a setting, a manual step, a rebuild of something unusual), the section starts with Upgrade notes. The GitHub release notes can be that section.

  3. Close the release's schema changes, if it has any: set its SCHEMA_RELEASES entries to False (see Schema changes), and check production matches with tools/schema_check.sh.

  4. Make the SBOM for this release. The Security pages show it, and the published version keeps it.

    podman-compose build
tools/sbom.sh
git add docs/security/sbom/ && git commit -m "SBOM for 1.0.0"

  5. Tag it and push.

    git tag -a v1.0.0 -m "1.0.0"
git push origin master v1.0.0    # or main, whichever your default branch is

  6. Publish the docs from the tag. Build from the tag itself, so the commit shown on the Bandit page is the release's:

    git checkout v1.0.0
mike deploy --push --update-aliases 1.0 latest
git checkout master

    mike deploy builds the site, commits it to the gh-pages branch under 1.0/, points latest at it, and pushes that branch. Your working branch isn't touched.

  7. Deploy the server as usual: Deployment → Shipping a change.

docs.title: The first release only
docs.text:
After step 6, make latest the site's front door, and turn Pages on:

mike set-default --push latest

Then on GitHub: Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root). The site appears within a minute or two.

docs.title: Checking before you push
docs.text:
Leave out --push and mike commits to your local gh-pages branch only. mike serve then shows the versioned site at http://127.0.0.1:8000, version menu and all:

mike deploy --update-aliases 1.0 latest
mike serve

Push it with git push origin gh-pages once it looks right. Other commands:

mike list                       # published versions and their aliases
mike delete --push 1.0          # unpublish a version

docs.title: What each version freezes
docs.text:
A published version is a snapshot. Its pages won't change unless you deploy that version again:

  • The Bandit results are as of the build, so as of the release when built from its tag.
  • The SBOM and vulnerabilities are as of the tools/sbom.sh run committed in that release. New vulnerabilities in the same packages appear only in later scans. For a current view of a running release, rerun tools/sbom.sh against its images.
  • Everything else, from the organizer guide to the code reference, is the release's own.

mkdocs serve and mkdocs build still work for everyday writing. They build one unversioned site in site/, and the version menu stays empty until mike publishes.

docs.title: Secrets and keys
docs.text: This page lists each secret the system uses: where it lives, how to make it, and what happens when it changes. For how the design limits what any one of them gives away, see Quality & security → Security in the design.

docs.title: Never commit or publish these
docs.text:
File What it holds .env (and .env.*, .env_* backups) Every secret on this page except the private key. private.pem The key that decrypts every volunteer's email address. api_key* Export API keys saved for vol_mail. box.json, vol_mail_state/ Email ciphertext and check-in codes, from vol_mail. Database dumps Volunteer names and email ciphertext.

.gitignore covers all of these, and .rsync-filter keeps *.pem, *.key, api_key* and the vol_mail files off the server. .env is the exception: it's synced on purpose, because the containers need it.

Before pushing, check what git would add:

git add -n . | grep -Ei '\.env|\.pem|\.key|api_key|box\.json|\.db$'   # expect only .env.example
gitleaks detect --no-git          # if you have gitleaks

docs.title: The volunteer email key pair
docs.text:
Volunteer addresses are never stored readable. The portal encrypts each one to the organizers' RSA public key (RSA-OAEP with SHA-256) the moment it's submitted. Only private.pem can decrypt them, and it never goes to the server:

  • Admin → Volunteers decrypts in the organizer's browser, with the key chosen from disk. The server never sees a readable address.
  • vol_mail decrypts on the organizer's machine to send schedule emails.

Make a pair (3072-bit RSA):

openssl genpkey -algorithm RSA -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:3072 -out private.pem
openssl pkey -in private.pem -pubout -out public.pem
chmod 600 private.pem

Upload public.pem under Admin → Email Key. The scheduler pushes it to the portal on the next sync, and signup can't open until the portal has one.

Losing private.pem loses every address. Keep it in a password manager or another encrypted store, shared only with the organizers who send mail. Replacing the pair affects only new signups: addresses already stored stay encrypted to the old key, and only the old private key can read them.

docs.title: EMAIL_HMAC_KEY
docs.text:
HMAC-SHA256(key, lowercased address) is each volunteer's email_hmac. It's how the portal finds a registered address and refuses a duplicate signup without storing the address. The backend uses the same key to index volunteers added by hand.

  • Make it with openssl rand -hex 32. The backend and the portal must have the same value.
  • It's kept in the environment only, never in a database: portal.db holds the hashes, and keeping the key beside them would give away both halves.
  • The portal refuses to start without it, rather than make a new one.
  • Changing it locks every volunteer out. Their stored hashes stop matching, so nobody can sign in and duplicate detection stops working. Don't rotate it while volunteers exist.

docs.title: The sync secret
docs.text:
SYNC_SECRET signs every request from the scheduler to the portal (HMAC-SHA256 over the method, path, timestamp, nonce and body hash). SYNC_KEY_ID names it.

To rotate it without dropping sync:

  1. Generate a new secret with openssl rand -hex 32.
  2. In .env, move the old value to SYNC_SECRET_PREV and put the new one in SYNC_SECRET.
  3. Deploy. The portal accepts both while the backend switches to the new one.
  4. Once sync is healthy (Call for Volunteers → Volunteer Portal), empty SYNC_SECRET_PREV and deploy again.

docs.title: MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN
docs.text: The portal's bearer token for the mail relay. Make it with openssl rand -hex 32, at least 32 characters. To change it, update .env and restart the stack, so both containers get the new value together. A mismatch shows up as mail relay returned 401.

docs.title: The relay's Microsoft sign-in
docs.text:
The relay holds a delegated refresh token for RELAY_MAILBOX, on the mailrelay_state volume, mode 0600. It isn't in .env and isn't backed up. Microsoft issues a new one on every use, and the relay saves each atomically.

  • Create or renew it with podman-compose exec mailrelay python relay.py login.
  • It stops working after a password change, a Conditional Access prompt, or 90 days without sending. See Graph mail setup → Keeping it signed in.
  • Revoke it at myaccount.microsoft.com → Apps & services, or delete the volume.

vol_mail uses the same app registration, but keeps its sign-in in memory only.

docs.title: Keys kept in the database
docs.text:
The backend generates these on first use and keeps them in app_kv:

Key What it does Rotating it app_secret Signs the organizer session cookie. Not exposed in the UI. Changing it signs every organizer out. checkin_key Makes each shift's check-in QR code. App Settings → Rotate key. It voids every code already sent, so send the schedule emails again.

docs.title: Export API keys
docs.text: Made under Admin → API Keys, each with scopes, an expiry of up to 365 days and an optional IP allow-list. The key is shown once, and only its SHA-256 is stored. Keys can't be deleted, only revoked, so the audit log keeps saying which key did what. Save the key for vol_mail in a file named api_key*, which git and rsync both ignore.

docs.title: backend.alerts
docs.text:
Security alerts: rules over the audit log's events, and email through the portal.

Every audit record passes through observe() (registered with audit.add_observer by start()). Each rule in RULES names the events it watches and what it counts them by (the client's address, a username, a key id), and fires when it sees threshold of them — or that many distinct usernames, for a password spray — inside window_sec.

A fired alert:

  • is recorded as an alert.fired audit event, with the alert's own severity;
  • is queued for email to every organizer set to get alerts (users.audit_alerts, Admin → Users) who has an address in users.email, through the portal's send_admin_mail (kind alert), sent by a background task so no request waits on mail;
  • starts a cooldown for that rule and key (COOLDOWN_SEC). Matching events during it are only counted. When it ends, the count goes out: with the next alert for the same rule and key, or, if none comes, as a follow-up of its own (flush_held_back, every FLUSH_EVERY_SEC). So a flood is one email straight away and then at most one an hour, and no count is ever lost because the activity stopped.

At most MAX_MAILED_PER_HOUR alerts are emailed an hour in all; past that they are still recorded in the audit log, with mailed: false.

Two rules look back through audit_events rather than counting: a sign-in from a network the user hasn't signed in from in 30 days (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /64), and an export key used from a new one. Both stay quiet when there's no history yet, so turning alerts on isn't a burst of "new network" mail. They need the table, so they're skipped when it isn't in use.

Rules never see alert.* events, so an alert can't set off another. State is in memory, like the rate limits: the backend runs one worker.

def network(ip: str | None) -> str | None:
    """The network an address is judged by for "new network": IPv4 /24, IPv6 /64.

    Args:
        ip: An address, or anything else.

    Returns:
        The network in CIDR form, or `ip` itself when it isn't an address.
    """
    if not ip:
        return None
    try:
        addr = ipaddress.ip_address(ip)
    except ValueError:
        return ip
    if isinstance(addr, ipaddress.IPv6Address) and addr.ipv4_mapped:
        addr = addr.ipv4_mapped
    prefix = 24 if addr.version == 4 else 64
    return str(ipaddress.ip_network(f"{addr}/{prefix}", strict=False))

def observe(rec: dict) -> None:
    """Run every rule over one audit record. Registered with `audit.add_observer`.

    Args:
        rec: An audit record (audit.build_record, through JSON).
    """
    event = rec.get("event", "")
    if event.startswith("alert."):
        return
    for rule in RULES:
        if event in rule.events:
            _evaluate(rule, rec)
    if event not in _WATCHED and rec.get("severity") in ("high", "critical"):
        _evaluate(_FALLBACK, rec)

async def deliver(alert: Alert, retry: bool = True) -> int:
    """Email one alert to every recipient, retrying each once after MAIL_RETRY_SEC.

    Records `alert.mailed` (how many it reached) or `alert.mail_fail` (whom it didn't, by
    username, never address).

    Args:
        alert: The alert.
        retry: Retry a failed send once. Off for the test alert, whose caller is waiting.

    Returns:
        How many recipients it reached.
    """
    people = await asyncio.to_thread(recipients)
    if not people:
        log.warning("alerts: %s not mailed: no organizer set to get alerts has an email",
                    alert.rule_id)
        audit("alert.mail_fail", None, None, "No one to email the alert to",
              rule=alert.rule_id, reason="no_recipients")
        return 0
    fields = {"app_title": await asyncio.to_thread(_app_title), "rule": alert.rule_id,
              "title": alert.title, "severity": alert.severity,
              "facts": [list(f) for f in alert.facts], "held_back": alert.held_back}
    link = f"{portal_sync.site_origin()}/admin/audit"
    reached = 0
    for person in people:
        for attempt in ((1, 2) if retry else (2,)):
            try:
                await portal_sync.send_admin_mail("alert", person["email"], link, **fields)
                reached += 1
                break
            except Exception as exc:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
                # Deliberately broad: the portal, the network or the relay can each fail in
                # their own way, and one recipient's failure mustn't stop the others.
                if attempt == 1:
                    await asyncio.sleep(MAIL_RETRY_SEC)
                    continue
                log.error("alerts: %s not mailed to %s: %s", alert.rule_id,
                          person["username"], exc)
                audit("alert.mail_fail", None, None, "A security alert could not be emailed",
                      rule=alert.rule_id, recipient=person["username"], error=str(exc)[:200])
    if reached:
        audit("alert.mailed", None, None, "Security alert emailed", rule=alert.rule_id,
              recipients=reached)
    return reached

docs.title: flush_held_back() -> int
docs.text:
Send a follow-up for every rule and key whose cooldown has ended with events held back and no new alert to carry them. Each follow-up starts a new cooldown, so a flood that keeps going is a summary an hour.

Returns:

Type Description int

How many follow-ups fired.

Source code in backend/alerts.py 
def flush_held_back() -> int:
    """Send a follow-up for every rule and key whose cooldown has ended with events held
    back and no new alert to carry them. Each follow-up starts a new cooldown, so a flood
    that keeps going is a summary an hour.

    Returns:
        How many follow-ups fired.
    """
    now = _monotonic()
    due = []
    with _state.lock:
        for slot, count in list(_state.suppressed.items()):
            if count and _state.cooldown_until.get(slot, 0) <= now and slot[0] in _BY_ID:
                due.append((slot, count))
                del _state.suppressed[slot]
                _state.cooldown_until[slot] = now + COOLDOWN_SEC
    for (rule_id, key), count in due:
        rule = _BY_ID[rule_id]
        alert = Alert(rule.rule_id, f"{rule.title} (continued)", rule.severity,
                      [("Rule", rule.rule_id), ("For", str(key)[:FACT_MAX]),
                       ("Held back", f"{count} more in the last hour")], count)
        alert.mailed = _state.mailed.allow("all")
        audit("alert.fired", None, None, alert.title, severity=rule.severity, rule=rule_id,
              key=key, follow_up=True, held_back=count, mailed=alert.mailed)
        if alert.mailed:
            _queue(alert)
    return len(due)

def start(loop: asyncio.AbstractEventLoop) -> None:
    """Start watching audit events and mailing alerts. Called from main.lifespan.

    Args:
        loop: The running event loop, which the mail worker runs on.
    """
    _state.loop = loop
    _state.queue = asyncio.Queue()
    _state.worker = loop.create_task(_worker())
    _state.flusher = loop.create_task(_flusher())
    add_observer(observe)
    with _state.lock:
        pending, _state.unsent = _state.unsent, []
    for alert in pending:
        _state.queue.put_nowait(alert)

def stop() -> None:
    """Stop watching and cancel the mail worker (shutdown, tests)."""
    remove_observer(observe)
    for task in (_state.worker, _state.flusher):
        if task is not None:
            task.cancel()
    _state.loop = _state.queue = _state.worker = _state.flusher = None

docs.title: backend.api_auth
docs.text:
Bearer keys for the read-only export API (routers/export.py; managed in routers/api_tokens.py).

The admin hostname is behind an access gate at the edge, but /api/export/* bypasses it so servers can call it, so the export API is reachable from anywhere. Hence:

  • A key is bsc_ + 32 random bytes, shown once; only its SHA-256 is stored (api_tokens).
  • Every failure is the same bare 401 (no key, unknown, expired, revoked, wrong IP, missing scope), so a caller can't learn which check rejected it.
  • Failed attempts are limited per client IP in memory (one worker); over the limit is a 429 before the key is even looked at.
  • Every accepted call is audited under the key's label and id, never the key itself.

Scopes are additive. The other team's app needs schedule:read and volunteers:read; the mailer (tools/vol_mail) also needs volunteers:email and checkin:codes.

docs.title: rate_key(ip: str) -> str
docs.text:
The identity a client is rate limited under: an IPv6 address's /64, otherwise the address.

One IPv6 connection is normally handed a whole /64, so counting single addresses would let a caller take a fresh one per request. An IPv4-mapped address counts as its IPv4 address; a value that isn't an address passes through. Only for counting: allow-lists, audit and last_used_ip keep the exact address. routers/password_reset.py uses it too, and the portal has its own copy (portal/ratelimit.py), as the apps share no code.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ip str

The client address, as client_ip resolved it.

required

Returns:

Type Description str

The rate-limit key.

Source code in backend/api_auth.py 
def rate_key(ip: str) -> str:
    """The identity a client is rate limited under: an IPv6 address's /64, otherwise the address.

    One IPv6 connection is normally handed a whole /64, so counting single addresses would let
    a caller take a fresh one per request. An IPv4-mapped address counts as its IPv4 address; a
    value that isn't an address passes through. Only for counting: allow-lists, audit and
    ``last_used_ip`` keep the exact address. ``routers/password_reset.py`` uses it too, and
    the portal has its own copy (``portal/ratelimit.py``), as the apps share no code.

    Args:
        ip: The client address, as ``client_ip`` resolved it.

    Returns:
        The rate-limit key.
    """
    try:
        addr = ipaddress.ip_address(ip)
    except ValueError:
        return ip
    if isinstance(addr, ipaddress.IPv6Address):
        if addr.ipv4_mapped:
            return str(addr.ipv4_mapped)
        # From the integer, so a zone suffix (fe80::1%eth0) can't upset the parse.
        return str(ipaddress.IPv6Network((int(addr) >> 64 << 64, 64)))
    return str(addr)

    Returns:
        The networks as normalised CIDR strings. A bare address becomes a /32 or /128.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When any part isn't an address or network.
    """
    nets = []
    for part in (text or "").replace(",", " ").split():
        nets.append(str(ipaddress.ip_network(part, strict=False)))
    return nets

def ip_allowed(ip: str, allowed: str) -> bool:
    """True when allowed is empty (any address) or ip falls in one of its networks.

    Args:
        ip: The caller's address from `client_ip`.
        allowed: The key's stored allow-list, space-separated CIDRs.

    Returns:
        Whether the call may go ahead. An address that doesn't parse is refused.
    """
    nets = (allowed or "").split()
    if not nets:
        return True
    try:
        addr = ipaddress.ip_address(ip)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    return any(addr in ipaddress.ip_network(n) for n in nets)

docs.title: backend.audit
docs.text:
The audit log: one JSON object per line, one line per security-relevant action.

Every write, sign-in and refusal in the backend calls audit() with an event code from EVENTS. The line it appends to the file named by --audit (logs/audit.jsonl in the deployment) looks like:

{"ts": "2026-11-23T14:02:11.120Z", "event": "auth.login.fail", "severity": "low",
 "actor": null, "user_id": null, "ip": "203.0.113.9", "method": "POST",
 "path": "/api/login", "message": "Invalid login attempt", "data": {"username": "bob"}}

Each line is written with json.dumps, so text a caller controls (a username, a label, a note) can never break out of its field or forge a line of its own. The free-text audit.log this replaces wrote such text verbatim.

EVENTS is the registry of codes. test_audit.py checks that every audit() call in the code names a registered code as a string literal, so a typo fails a test rather than producing a code no alert rule or filter knows about. In production an unknown code is still recorded, flagged "unregistered": true, because losing an audit line would be worse.

Each event also becomes a row in audit_events (when configure(..., to_db=True), as in main.py), for the admin site's Audit Log and the alert rules. The row is written on its own pooled connection with its own commit, so a request that rolls back still leaves its row. The file is the complete record; the table is pruned to AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 365, 0 keeps everything) by prune(), which main.py runs at startup and daily.

A failure to write either is logged and swallowed: the audit log must never be the reason a request fails.

def prune(conn: "db.PgClient") -> int:
    """Delete `audit_events` rows older than `retention_days()`, and commit.

    Args:
        conn: A database connection.

        How many rows went.

    cur = conn.execute(_PRUNE_SQL, (days, days))
    conn.commit()
    return cur.rowcount

def client_ip(request: Request) -> str:
    """The caller's address, for the audit log, rate limits and API keys' IP allow-lists.

    nginx sends a single resolved X-Forwarded-For (frontend/CLAUDE.md → Reverse proxy), taken
    from the edge's client-address header, so the first hop is the real client.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request.

    Returns:
        The first `X-Forwarded-For` hop set by nginx, else the socket peer, else `""`.
    """
    fwd = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for", "")
    return fwd.split(",")[0].strip() if fwd else (request.client.host if request.client else "")

def build_record(event: str, request: Request | None, s_id: str | None, message: str,
                 who: str | None = None, *, severity: str | None = None, **data) -> dict:
    """The audit record for one event, before it's written. Separate from `audit()` so the
    record's shape can be tested without a file.

    Args:
        event: A code from `EVENTS`.
        request: The request, for the client IP, method and path. None for an event with no
            request behind it, such as an alert raised by a background task.
        s_id: The caller's session id; its cached username and user id go on the record.
        message: What happened, in words.
        who: A label for a caller with no session, such as an export API key. It wins over
            `s_id` as the actor.
        severity: Overrides the registry's severity for this one record (an `alert.fired`
            carries its alert's severity). Must be one of SEVERITIES.
        **data: Structured details (a target username, a key id, counts). Values must be
            JSON-serializable or have a useful `str()`.

    Returns:
        The record, ready for `json.dumps`.
    """
    if severity not in SEVERITIES:
        severity = EVENTS[event].severity if event in EVENTS else "info"
    actor, user_id = None, None
    if who:
        actor = who
    elif s_id:
        sess = _session_cache.get(s_id, {})
        actor = sess.get("username", "unknown")
        user_id = sess.get("user_id")
    record = {
        "ts": _now(),
        "event": event,
        "severity": severity,
        "source": "backend",
        "actor": _clip(actor),
        "user_id": user_id,
        "ip": (client_ip(request) or "unknown") if request else None,
        "method": request.method if request else None,
        "path": _clip(request.url.path) if request else None,
        "message": _clip(message),
        "data": {k: _clip(v) for k, v in data.items()},
    }
    if event not in EVENTS:
        record["unregistered"] = True
    return record

def audit(event: str, request: Request | None, s_id: str | None, message: str,
          who: str | None = None, *, severity: str | None = None, **data) -> None:
    """Append one event to the audit log. Never raises.

    Args:
        event: A code from `EVENTS`, as a string literal (test_audit.py checks).
        request: The request, for the client IP, method and path.
        s_id: The caller's session id, or None for an unauthenticated caller.
        message: What happened, in words. Caller-supplied text is safe here, but prefer
            putting it in `data` so it can be filtered on.
        who: A label for a caller with no session, such as an export API key.
        severity: Overrides the registry's severity; see `build_record`.
        **data: Structured details; see `build_record`.
    """
    if not (_config.path or _config.to_db or _config.observers):
        return
    if event not in EVENTS:
        log.warning("audit: unregistered event code %r", event)
    try:
        record = build_record(event, request, s_id, message, who, severity=severity, **data)
    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        log.error("audit: could not build %s event: %s", event, exc)
        return
    _emit(record)

def ingest(raw: dict, source: str) -> bool:
    """Record an event that happened elsewhere (the portal's security events, pulled by
    portal_sync), exactly as a local one: file, alert rules, table.

    Everything in `raw` is treated as untrusted: the timestamp must be ISO 8601 UTC, the
    severity one of SEVERITIES (else the registry's, else "info"), text is cut to MAX_TEXT,
    and `data` must be an object. An unknown event code is recorded and flagged, as locally.

    Args:
        raw: `{ts, event, severity, ip, method, path, message, data}`.
        source: Where it came from, e.g. `"portal"`.

    Returns:
        False when it was malformed and dropped, else True.
    """
    event, ts, data = raw.get("event"), raw.get("ts"), raw.get("data") or {}
    if not isinstance(event, str) or not event or not isinstance(ts, str) \
            or not _TS.match(ts) or not isinstance(data, dict):
        log.warning("audit: dropped a malformed %s event", source)
        return False
    if not (_config.path or _config.to_db or _config.observers):
        return True
    severity = raw.get("severity")
    if severity not in SEVERITIES:
        severity = EVENTS[event].severity if event in EVENTS else "info"
    record = {
        "ts": ts, "event": _clip(event), "severity": severity, "source": _clip(source),
        "actor": None, "user_id": None,
        "ip": _clip(raw.get("ip")) if isinstance(raw.get("ip"), str) else None,
        "method": _clip(raw.get("method")) if isinstance(raw.get("method"), str) else None,
        "path": _clip(raw.get("path")) if isinstance(raw.get("path"), str) else None,
        "message": _clip(str(raw.get("message") or "")),
        "data": {str(k)[:100]: _clip(v) for k, v in data.items()},
    }
    if event not in EVENTS:
        record["unregistered"] = True
        log.warning("audit: unregistered event code %r from %s", event, source)
    _emit(record)
    return True

docs.title: backend.checkin_codes
docs.text:
Shift check-in codes and the early/late rule. No database, so it can be unit-tested alone.

A code is BSC1.{slot_key}.{b64url(vol_id)}.{mac}, where mac is HMAC-SHA256 under app_kv.checkin_key, truncated to 128 bits. It is deterministic: the same volunteer and slot always give the same code, so a re-sent schedule email (draft, then final) doesn't void the first one. A valid code is not enough on its own to check in; routers/checkin.py also requires the volunteer to still be assigned to that slot, which is what voids a code on reassignment. Rotating the key voids every code at once.

Every way of failing (malformed, wrong key, tampered) returns the same None, so a caller can't be told which check rejected it.

required code str

def verify_code(key: bytes, code: str) -> Optional[tuple]:
    """Return (vol_id, slot_key) for a genuine code, or None.

    Every way of failing (malformed, wrong key, tampered) returns the same None, so a caller
    can't be told which check rejected it.

    Args:
        key: The current check-in HMAC key.
        code: What the scanner read or the organizer typed. Surrounding whitespace is ignored.
    """
    code = (code or "").strip()
    if not code or len(code) > MAX_CODE_LEN:
        return None
    parts = code.split(".")
    if len(parts) != 4 or parts[0] != PREFIX or not _SLOT_RE.match(parts[1]):
        return None
    _, slot_key, vol_b64, mac = parts
    try:
        vol_id = _unb64(vol_b64).decode()
    except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        return None
    if not vol_id or not hmac.compare_digest(mac, _mac(key, vol_id, slot_key)):
        return None
    return vol_id, slot_key

def shift_start(event_date: Optional[str], time_str: Optional[str], tz: str) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """When a shift starts, as an aware datetime, or None when it can't be told.

    event_date is ISO ``YYYY-MM-DD`` (days_table, optional); time_str is the
    ``'0800-1200'`` range from times_table, read the same way as routers/schedule.time_range.

    Args:
        event_date: The day's ISO date, or `None` when the day has none set.
        time_str: The shift's time range.
        tz: The event's IANA timezone name, from App Settings.
    """
    if not event_date:
        return None
    m = _RANGE.match(time_str or "")
    if not m:
        return None
    try:
        day = date.fromisoformat(event_date.strip())
        hhmm = m.group(1).zfill(4)
        hour, minute = int(hhmm[:2]), int(hhmm[2:])
        return datetime(day.year, day.month, day.day, hour, minute, tzinfo=ZoneInfo(tz))
    except (ValueError, KeyError):
        return None

def shift_end(start: Optional[datetime], time_str: Optional[str]) -> Optional[datetime]:
    """When a shift ends, given its start; a range like 2200-0200 runs past midnight.

    Args:
        start: The shift's start, from `shift_start`.
        time_str: The shift's time range, like `'0800-1200'`.

    Returns:
        The end as an aware datetime, or `None` without a start or a readable range.
    """
    m = _RANGE.match(time_str or "")
    if not start or not m:
        return None
    a, b = (int(x.zfill(4)[:2]) * 60 + int(x.zfill(4)[2:]) for x in m.groups())
    length = b - a if b > a else b - a + 24 * 60
    return start + timedelta(minutes=length)

def classify(now: datetime, start: Optional[datetime],
             early: int = EARLY_MINUTES, late: int = LATE_MINUTES) -> tuple:
    """('early' | 'late' | 'on_time' | 'unknown', minutes).

    minutes is how far before (early) or after (late) the start, rounded down; 0 otherwise.
    Exactly 45 minutes early or 10 minutes late still counts as on time.

    Args:
        now: The current time, aware.
        start: The shift's start from `shift_start`. `None` gives `'unknown'`.
        early: Minutes before the start that still count as on time.
        late: Minutes after the start that still count as on time.
    """
    if start is None:
        return "unknown", 0
    delta = (now - start).total_seconds() / 60
    if delta < -early:
        return "early", int(-delta)
    if delta > late:
        return "late", int(delta)
    return "on_time", 0

docs.title: backend.db
docs.text:
PostgreSQL access, schema migration and the session/role dependencies.

Every router talks to the database through PgClient, a small sqlite3-shaped wrapper over a pooled psycopg2 connection. It rewrites ? placeholders to %s, which is why the queries throughout the backend still use ?. Rows come back as dicts (RealDictCursor), so code reads row["col"], never row[0].

Connection settings come from the DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD environment variables. The schema is scheduler.sql for a fresh database, and one file per release after 1.0 (migrations/<release>.sql) for an existing one, as listed in SCHEMA_RELEASES.

def execute(self, sql: str, params: tuple = ()) -> _Cursor:
    """Run one statement with bound parameters.

    Args:
        sql: A complete literal statement using `?` placeholders.
        params: The values for the placeholders, in order.

    Returns:
        A cursor with `fetchone`, `fetchall` and `rowcount`. Fetching from a statement that
        returns no rows gives `None` or `[]` rather than raising.
    """
    pg_sql = sql.replace('?', '%s')
    cur = self._conn.cursor()
    cur.execute(pg_sql, params or None)
    return _Cursor(cur)

def migrate(conn):
    """Bring the schema up to `SCHEMA_VERSION`.

    A fresh database (version 0) gets `scheduler.sql`, which is the whole current schema. An
    existing one gets each release file in `SCHEMA_RELEASES` newer than its recorded version,
    in order, plus the file of a release still in progress (re-run on every start), and then
    records the new version.

    Args:
        conn: A raw psycopg2 connection (not a `PgClient`). Committed on success.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: A database from before 1.0 (older than `BASELINE_VERSION`), which the
            per-release files can't upgrade.
    """
    version = _schema_version(conn)
    if version == 0:
        _apply_sql_file(conn, os.path.join(_HERE, 'scheduler.sql'))
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "INSERT INTO schema_versions (version) VALUES (%s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;",
                (SCHEMA_VERSION,)
            )
        conn.commit()
        return
    if version < BASELINE_VERSION:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"This database is at schema version {version}, from before release 1.0 "
            f"(version {BASELINE_VERSION}). Upgrade it with a pre-1.0 build first, or dump and "
            "restore its data into a fresh 1.0 database.")
    for _release, release_version, path, in_progress in SCHEMA_RELEASES[1:]:
        if release_version > version or (in_progress and release_version == version):
            _apply_sql_file(conn, os.path.join(_HERE, 'migrations', path))
    if version < SCHEMA_VERSION:
        # Record the new version so the files above don't run again on the next start.
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(
                "INSERT INTO schema_versions (version) VALUES (%s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;",
                (SCHEMA_VERSION,)
            )
        conn.commit()

def get_db():
    """FastAPI dependency: borrow a pooled connection for one request.

    FastAPI caches the dependency per request, so `get_session_data` and the endpoint share the
    same connection. Anything left uncommitted when the request ends is rolled back before the
    connection goes back to the pool.

    Yields:
        A `PgClient` on the borrowed connection.
    """
    pool = _pool()
    conn = pool.getconn()
    try:
        yield PgClient(conn)
    finally:
        conn.rollback()
        pool.putconn(conn)

def put_conn(client: "PgClient") -> None:
    """Return a connection borrowed with get_conn, rolling back anything left open.

    Args:

def get_session_data(
    request: Request,
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
) -> Optional[dict]:
    """FastAPI dependency: the signed-in organizer for this request, if any.

    Looks the cookie's `session_id` up in `_session_cache` first and the `sessions` table second,
    caching what it finds. A session id with no row (expired or signed out elsewhere) is dropped
    from the cookie.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, whose session cookie holds `session_id`.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Returns:
        `{"user_id", "username", "role"}`, or `None` when nobody is signed in.
    """
    s_id = request.session.get("session_id")
    if not s_id:
        return None
    if s_id in _session_cache:
        return _session_cache[s_id]
    row = db.execute(
        "SELECT s.user_id, u.username, u.role FROM sessions s "
        "LEFT JOIN users u ON s.user_id = u.user_id WHERE s.session_id = ?;",
        (s_id,)
    ).fetchone()
    if row:
        s_data = {"user_id": row["user_id"], "username": row["username"],
                  "role": row["role"] or "organizer"}
        _session_cache[s_id] = s_data
        return s_data
    request.session.pop("session_id", None)
    return None

def get_app_kv(db: PgClient, key: str, default_factory=None) -> Optional[str]:
    """Read one value from the `app_kv` table, optionally creating it.

    Args:
        db: The database connection.
        key: The `app_key` to read.
        default_factory: Called to make the value when the key doesn't exist yet. The new value
            is stored and committed. Leave it out to just read.

    Returns:
        The stored value, the newly created one, or `None` when the key is missing and there
        is no factory.
    """
    row = db.execute("SELECT val FROM app_kv WHERE app_key = ?;", (key,)).fetchone()
    if row:
        return row["val"]
    if default_factory is not None:
        val = default_factory()
        db.execute("INSERT INTO app_kv (app_key, val) VALUES (?, ?);", (key, val))
        db.commit()
        return val
    return None

docs.title: backend.email_render
docs.text:
The schedule email template: Markdown in, the preview and the downloadable package out.

Organizers write the template on the site (routers/email_template.py); tools/vol_mail sends it from the package. To keep the preview and the sent mail from drifting, Markdown is converted here, once. The package carries HTML and text with {{placeholders}} still in them, and the tool only fills those in, by the rules in fill below, which it copies. Change one, change the other (tools/vol_mail/test_vol_mail.py checks they agree).

Placeholders, {{ name }} with optional spaces:

  • subject and body: name, first_name, handle, vol_id, event_title; the body also has shifts
  • shift block (repeated once per shift): day, date, time, position, category, qr

In HTML every value is escaped, except shifts (the filled shift blocks) and qr (an <img src="cid:…"> the filler makes), which the filler builds itself. Images are written ![alt](asset:logo.png) and stay src="asset:…" in the package; the tool attaches each asset inline, and the preview inlines it as a data URL.

Raw HTML in the template is escaped, not passed through (markdown-it html: False).

def check_template(subject: str, body_md: str, shift_md: str) -> list:
    """Problems that make a template unusable, as sentences; [] when it's fine.

    Args:
        subject: The subject line template.
        body_md: The body, in Markdown.
        shift_md: The block repeated once per shift, in Markdown.
    """
    problems = []
    for label, text, allowed in (("Subject", subject, SUBJECT_FIELDS),
                                 ("Body", body_md, BODY_FIELDS),
                                 ("Shift block", shift_md, SHIFT_FIELDS)):
        bad = unknown_placeholders(text, allowed)
        if bad:
            problems.append(f"{label} uses unknown placeholder(s): "
                            + ", ".join("{{%s}}" % b for b in bad)
                            + ". Available: " + ", ".join("{{%s}}" % a for a in allowed))
    if not (subject or "").strip():
        problems.append("The subject is empty.")
    if "\n" in (subject or ""):
        problems.append("The subject must be one line.")
    if "shifts" not in {m.group(1) for m in PLACEHOLDER.finditer(body_md or "")}:
        problems.append("The body doesn't include {{shifts}}, so no shifts would be listed.")
    if "qr" not in {m.group(1) for m in PLACEHOLDER.finditer(shift_md or "")}:
        problems.append("The shift block doesn't include {{qr}}, so no check-in codes would be sent.")
    return problems

def fill(template: str, values: dict, as_html: bool) -> str:
    """Replace each {{field}} with its value; an unknown field is left as it was.

    Args:
        template: Text containing `{{field}}` placeholders.
        values: Field name to value. Values are converted with `str`.
        as_html: Escape values for HTML, except the fields in `RAW_HTML_FIELDS`, which are
            markup already.
    """
    def sub(m):
        key = m.group(1)
        if key not in values:
            return m.group(0)
        val = str(values[key])
        return val if (not as_html or key in RAW_HTML_FIELDS) else html.escape(val)
    return PLACEHOLDER.sub(sub, template)

def human_date(iso: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """'April 25, 2027' from '2027-04-25'; '' when there's no date.

    Args:
        iso: An ISO date, or `None`. Anything that doesn't parse comes back unchanged.
    """
    if not iso:
        return ""
    try:
        d = date.fromisoformat(iso)
    except ValueError:
        return iso
    return f"{d:%B} {d.day}, {d.year}"

def render_message(parts: dict, vol: dict, event_title: str, qr_src) -> dict:
    """One volunteer's subject, HTML and text, from build_parts output.

    vol is an export-API volunteer (names, shifts with checkin_code). qr_src(i, shift) gives the
    image source for shift i: a data URL in the preview, ``cid:qr-{i}`` in the tool.

    Args:
        parts: The output of `build_parts`.
        vol: The volunteer, as the export API returns them.
        event_title: The value for `{{event_title}}`.
        qr_src: A callable `(index, shift) -> str` giving each QR image's source.

    Returns:
        `{"subject", "html", "text"}` for this volunteer.
    """
    who = {"name": vol["name"], "first_name": vol["first_name"], "handle": vol["handle"],
           "vol_id": vol["vol_id"], "event_title": event_title}
    blocks_html, blocks_txt = [], []
    for i, s in enumerate(vol["shifts"]):
        sv = {"day": s["day"], "date": human_date(s.get("date")), "time": s["time"],
              "position": s["position"], "category": s["category"]}
        blocks_html.append(fill(parts["shift_html"], {**sv, "qr": qr_img(qr_src(i, s), s)}, True))
        blocks_txt.append(fill(parts["shift_txt"], {**sv, "qr": f"Check-in code: {s['checkin_code']}"},
                               False))
    return {
        "subject": fill(parts["subject"], who, False),
        "html": fill(parts["body_html"], {**who, "shifts": "\n".join(blocks_html)}, True),
        "text": fill(parts["body_txt"], {**who, "shifts": "\n".join(blocks_txt).strip()}, False),
    }

def inline_assets(html_text: str, assets: dict) -> str:
    """Preview only: asset:name → a data URL, from {name: (content_type, bytes)}.

    Args:
        html_text: Rendered HTML containing `asset:name` references.
        assets: Asset name to `(content_type, data)`. A missing name is left as it was.
    """
    def sub(m):
        found = assets.get(m.group(1))
        if not found:
            return m.group(0)
        ctype, data = found
        return f"data:{ctype};base64,{base64.b64encode(data).decode()}"
    return ASSET_REF.sub(sub, html_text)

def build_package(subject: str, body_md: str, shift_md: str, assets: list, meta: dict) -> bytes:
    """The zip tools/vol_mail sends from. assets: dicts with name, content_type, data, sha256.

    Only assets the template refers to are included.

    Args:
        subject: The subject line template.
        body_md: The body, in Markdown.
        shift_md: The per-shift block, in Markdown.
        assets: The uploaded images, each a dict with `name`, `content_type`, `data` and
            `sha256`.
        meta: Extra manifest fields: when the package was made and by whom.

    Returns:
        The zip file's bytes: `manifest.json`, the four template files, `template.md` and the
        images used.
    """
    parts = build_parts(subject, body_md, shift_md)
    used = asset_refs(body_md, shift_md)
    files = {"body_html": "body.html", "body_txt": "body.txt",
             "shift_html": "shift.html", "shift_txt": "shift.txt"}
    manifest = {
        "format": FORMAT,
        "kind": "bsides-schedule-email",
        "subject": parts["subject"],
        **meta,
        "files": {**files, "source": "template.md"},
        "placeholders": {"subject": list(SUBJECT_FIELDS), "body": list(BODY_FIELDS),
                         "shift": list(SHIFT_FIELDS), "raw_html": list(RAW_HTML_FIELDS)},
        "assets": [{"name": a["name"], "file": f"assets/{a['name']}",
                    "content_type": a["content_type"], "sha256": a["sha256"],
                    "size": len(a["data"])}
                   for a in sorted(assets, key=lambda a: a["name"]) if a["name"] in used],
    }
    source = (f"Subject: {subject}\n\n<!-- body -->\n{body_md.rstrip()}\n\n"
              f"<!-- shift block -->\n{shift_md.rstrip()}\n")
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        z.writestr("manifest.json", json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n")
        for key, fname in files.items():
            z.writestr(fname, parts[key])
        z.writestr("template.md", source)
        for a in assets:
            if a["name"] in used:
                z.writestr(f"assets/{a['name']}", a["data"])
    return buf.getvalue()

    """Decide whether an access-log record is written.
