        record: One uvicorn access-log record. Its `args` are `(client, method, path,
            version, status)`.

        False for a successful GET of a healthcheck path, True for everything else.
    """
    try:
        _client, method, path, _ver, status = record.args
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return True
    return not (method == "GET" and path.split("?")[0] in self.PATHS and int(status) < 400)

def quiet_polls() -> None:

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    """Start the app's background parts, and stop them on shutdown.

    Args:
        app: The FastAPI app (unused; FastAPI passes it).

    Yields:
        Control to FastAPI while the app runs.
    """
    quiet_polls()
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    events.set_loop(loop)
    # No-op unless PORTAL_SYNC_URL and the sync keys are set, so a deployment without a
    # portal behaves exactly as it did before.
    portal_sync.start(loop)
    # Only when the audit table is in use (main below); tests start the app without it.
    pruner = None
    if audit.configured_to_db():
        pruner = loop.create_task(_prune_audit_daily())
        alerts.start(loop)
    yield
    if pruner:
        pruner.cancel()
        alerts.stop()

docs.text:
Taking a stored volunteer name apart, and the export API's name format.

The scheduler keeps one volunteers.name. All three ways in write it the same way: First L. plus an optional (handle) — add_vol, the CSV import (routers/setup.py), and portal signups (portal/routers/signup.display_name). The parts aren't stored separately, so the export API splits them back out here.

Read from the right, so a two-word first name survives: Mary Ann S. (zc) is first Mary Ann, initial S, handle zc. A name not in that shape (an older roster, typed by hand) still gives something sensible: a full last word becomes the initial, and a single word is a first name alone.

(first_name, last_initial, handle) from a stored name; any part may be ''.

def split_name(name: str) -> tuple:
    """(first_name, last_initial, handle) from a stored name; any part may be ''.

    Args:
        name: A stored name such as `"Ada L."`, `"Ada Lovelace"` or `"Ada L. (countess)"`.
            A full last name is cut to its initial.
    """
    rest, handle = (name or "").strip(), ""
    m = _HANDLE.match(rest)
    if m:
        rest, handle = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(2).strip()
    m = _INITIAL.match(rest)
    if m:
        return m.group(1), m.group(2).upper(), handle
    m = _LAST_WORD.match(rest)
    if m:
        return m.group(1), m.group(2)[0].upper(), handle
    return rest, "", handle

def __init__(self, alg: int = -7, synced: bool = False, aaguid: str = None):
    self.alg = alg
    # The authenticator model reported at registration; None sends all zeros.
    self.aaguid = uuid.UUID(aaguid).bytes if aaguid else b"\0" * 16
    self.credential_id = os.urandom(32)
    self.sign_count = 0 if synced else 1  # synced passkeys report 0 forever
    self.synced = synced
    self.user_handle = None
    if alg == -7:
        self._key = ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())
    elif alg in (-48, -49, -50):
        from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import mldsa
        cls = {-48: mldsa.MLDSA44PrivateKey, -49: mldsa.MLDSA65PrivateKey,
               -50: mldsa.MLDSA87PrivateKey}[alg]
        self._key = cls.generate()
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported test alg {alg}")

def register(self, options: dict, origin: str) -> str:
    """navigator.credentials.create() for these options, as the JSON a browser sends.

    Args:
        options: The server's `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions`, as JSON-decoded.
        origin: The page origin to sign into `clientDataJSON`.
    """
    rp_id = options["rp"]["id"]
    assert self.alg in [p["alg"] for p in options["pubKeyCredParams"]], "alg not offered"
    self.user_handle = b64url_decode(options["user"]["id"])
    cdj = self._client_data("webauthn.create", options["challenge"], origin)
    auth_data = (hashlib.sha256(rp_id.encode()).digest()
                 + bytes([self._flags(FLAG_AT)])
                 + struct.pack(">I", self.sign_count)
                 + self.aaguid
                 + struct.pack(">H", len(self.credential_id)) + self.credential_id
                 + self._cose_key())
    att_obj = cbor2.dumps({"fmt": "none", "attStmt": {}, "authData": auth_data})
    return json.dumps({
        "id": b64url(self.credential_id), "rawId": b64url(self.credential_id),
        "type": "public-key", "authenticatorAttachment": "platform",
        "clientExtensionResults": {},
        "response": {"clientDataJSON": b64url(cdj), "attestationObject": b64url(att_obj),
                     "transports": ["internal", "hybrid"]},
    })

def assert_(self, options: dict, origin: str, rp_id: str = None,
            user_handle: bytes = None, flags: int = None) -> str:
    """navigator.credentials.get() for these options, as the JSON a browser sends.

    Args:
        options: The server's `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions`, as JSON-decoded.
        origin: The page origin to sign into `clientDataJSON`.
        rp_id: Sign for this RP id instead of the one in `options`, to test a mismatch.
        user_handle: Send this user handle instead of the registered one.
        flags: Send these authenticator flags instead of the usual UP, UV and backup bits.
    """
    rp_id = rp_id or options["rpId"]
    if not self.synced:
        self.sign_count += 1
    cdj = self._client_data("webauthn.get", options["challenge"], origin)
    auth_data = (hashlib.sha256(rp_id.encode()).digest()
                 + bytes([self._flags() if flags is None else flags])
                 + struct.pack(">I", self.sign_count))
    sig = self._sign(auth_data + hashlib.sha256(cdj).digest())
    handle = self.user_handle if user_handle is None else user_handle
    return json.dumps({
        "id": b64url(self.credential_id), "rawId": b64url(self.credential_id),
        "type": "public-key", "authenticatorAttachment": "platform",
        "clientExtensionResults": {},
        "response": {"clientDataJSON": b64url(cdj), "authenticatorData": b64url(auth_data),
                     "signature": b64url(sig), "userHandle": b64url(handle)},
    })

docs.title: backend.portal_content
docs.text:
The volunteer portal's organizer-editable content: the scheduler's copy of the rules.

portal/content.py is the portal's copy, and the one that matters: it checks every push again and renders what volunteers see. This copy lets the scheduler refuse bad content when an organizer saves it, and render the editors' previews exactly as the portal will. Everything below this docstring must match the portal's file character for character; test_portal_content.py checks that, since the apps share no code. Edit both together.

What's here: the default landing page, questionnaire and invite email; the Jinja subset the templates may use (sandboxed: variables, {% if %}, comparisons and a few text filters); the Markdown renderer (no raw HTML, no images, web and email links only); and the checks on a questionnaire definition.

def render_template(source: str, values: dict, allowed: tuple, where: str) -> str:
    """Check a template, then render it in the sandbox.

    Args:
        source: The template text.
        values: A string for each allowed variable; missing ones render as "".
        allowed: The variable names it may use.
        where: What the template is, for errors.

    Returns:
        The rendered text.

    Raises:
        ContentError: The template isn't allowed, or fails to render.
    """
    _check_template(source, allowed, where)
    context = {name: str(values.get(name) or "") for name in allowed}
    try:
        return _ENV.from_string(source).render(context)
    except (TemplateError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise ContentError(f"{where}: {exc}") from None

def validate_landing(raw: Any) -> dict:
    """Check a landing page definition.

    Args:
        raw: ``intro``, ``main`` and ``sidebar`` (templated Markdown), ``roles_heading``, and
            ``roles``, each ``{icon, name, text}``.

    Returns:
        A clean copy.

    Raises:
        ContentError: For the first problem found.
    """
    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != set(DEFAULT_LANDING):
        raise ContentError("the landing page must have exactly: " + ", ".join(DEFAULT_LANDING))
    out: dict = {}
    for part in LANDING_PARTS:
        _check_template(raw[part], LANDING_VARS, f"Landing page {part}")
        out[part] = raw[part]
    out["roles_heading"] = _text(raw["roles_heading"], "The opportunities heading", 120,
                                 required=False)
    roles = raw["roles"]
    if not isinstance(roles, list) or len(roles) > MAX_ROLES:
        raise ContentError(f"opportunities must be a list of at most {MAX_ROLES}")
    out["roles"] = []
    for i, role in enumerate(roles, 1):
        if not isinstance(role, dict) or set(role) != {"icon", "name", "text"}:
            raise ContentError(f"opportunity {i} must have exactly icon, name and text")
        if role["icon"] not in ROLE_ICONS:
            raise ContentError(f"opportunity {i}: unknown icon {role['icon']!r}")
        out["roles"].append({"icon": role["icon"],
                             "name": _text(role["name"], f"Opportunity {i}'s name", 80),
                             "text": _text(role["text"], f"Opportunity {i}'s text", 200,
                                           required=False)})
    return out

def validate_fields(raw: Any) -> list:
    """Check a questionnaire definition.

    Args:
        raw: A list of questions, each ``key``, ``section``, ``type``, ``required``,
            ``editable`` and ``label``, plus ``options`` (choice, select) or ``max`` (text).

    Returns:
        A clean copy, in the same order.

    Raises:
        ContentError: For the first problem found.
    """
    if not isinstance(raw, list) or len(raw) > MAX_FIELDS:
        raise ContentError(f"the questionnaire must be a list of at most {MAX_FIELDS} questions")
    keys: set = set()
    out = []
    for i, field in enumerate(raw, 1):
        where = f"Question {i}"
        if not isinstance(field, dict) or not set(field) <= _FIELD_KEYS:
            raise ContentError(f"{where} has unknown settings")
        key = field.get("key")
        if not isinstance(key, str) or not _KEY.match(key):
            raise ContentError(f"{where}: its key must be lowercase letters, digits or _, "
                               "starting with a letter")
        if key in keys:
            raise ContentError(f"{where}: the key {key!r} is used twice")
        keys.add(key)
        kind = field.get("type")
        if kind not in FIELD_TYPES:
            raise ContentError(f"{where}: its type must be one of " + ", ".join(FIELD_TYPES))
        if field.get("section") not in SECTIONS:
            raise ContentError(f"{where}: its step must be one of " + ", ".join(SECTIONS))
        clean = {"key": key, "section": field["section"], "type": kind,
                 "required": _bool(field.get("required"), f"{where}'s required"),
                 "editable": _bool(field.get("editable", False), f"{where}'s editable"),
                 "label": _text(field.get("label"), f"{where}'s label", MAX_LABEL)}
        if kind == "ack" and not clean["required"]:
            raise ContentError(f"{where}: an acknowledgement is always required")
        if kind == "check" and clean["required"]:
            raise ContentError(f"{where}: a checkbox can't be required; use an acknowledgement")
        if key == FLEXIBLE_KEY and kind != "check":
            raise ContentError(f"{where}: {FLEXIBLE_KEY!r} is read by the assignment picker "
                               "and must stay a checkbox")
        if kind in ("choice", "select"):
            options = field.get("options")
            if not isinstance(options, list) or not 1 <= len(options) <= MAX_OPTIONS:
                raise ContentError(f"{where} needs 1 to {MAX_OPTIONS} options")
            clean["options"] = [_option(o, f"{where}, option {j}", keys)
                                for j, o in enumerate(options, 1)]
            values = [o["value"] for o in clean["options"]]
            if len(set(values)) != len(values):
                raise ContentError(f"{where}: two options have the same value")
            if kind == "select" and any("detail" in o for o in clean["options"]):
                raise ContentError(f"{where}: only a choice can ask a follow-up")
        elif "options" in field:
            raise ContentError(f"{where}: only a choice or a dropdown has options")
        if kind == "text":
            clean["max"] = _limit(field.get("max", 300), f"{where}'s length", 2000)
        elif "max" in field:
            raise ContentError(f"{where}: only a text question has a length")
        out.append(clean)
    return out

def validate_invite(raw: Any) -> dict:
    """Check an invite email template.

    Args:

        A clean copy.

        ContentError: For the first problem found, including a body without ``{{ link }}``.

    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != {"subject", "body"}:
        raise ContentError("the invite email must have exactly a subject and a body")
    subject = raw["subject"]
    _check_template(subject, INVITE_VARS, "The subject", MAX_INVITE_SUBJECT)
    if not isinstance(subject, str) or not subject.strip() or "\n" in subject:
        raise ContentError("The subject must be one line")
    _, used = _check_template(raw["body"], INVITE_VARS, "The body")
    if "link" not in used:
        raise ContentError("The body must include {{ link }}, or the invite can't be used")
    return {"subject": subject.strip(), "body": raw["body"]}

def validate_content(raw: Any) -> dict:
    """Check a content push: each part is a definition, or ``None`` for the default.

    Args:

docs.title: backend.portal_sync
docs.text:
Sync client: the scheduler's side of the portal API.

The scheduler is always the client. Nothing here listens, and the portal is never given a callback URL — which is why the portal can live on an internet-facing host while the scheduler does not, and why there is no inbound hole to punch. The price is that new signups arrive when we ask for them, so heartbeat is polled and is deliberately cheap (one row read).

Three jobs
  • poll heartbeat, pull only the streams whose rev moved
  • push the schedule snapshot, branding, settings, and volunteer changes
  • keep cursors and health in portal_sync_state, so the Admin UI can show sync is alive

If PORTAL_SYNC_URL is unset the task never starts, so an existing deployment with no portal behaves exactly as it did before.

def email_hmac(email: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """The portal's lookup index for an address (portal security.email_hmac), or None without
    a key. Normalisation must match the portal's exactly: strip and lowercase, nothing else.

    Args:
        email: The address, as typed.

    if not EMAIL_HMAC_KEY:

    return hmac.new(EMAIL_HMAC_KEY, email.strip().lower().encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()

A full replace rather than a diff: the portal holds a copy of our state, and reconciling a diff against a copy is how copies drift. content_hash makes an unchanged push free, so we can re-push whenever we are unsure rather than tracking what we already sent.

def build_snapshot(conn) -> dict:
    """Assemble the whole schedule as one payload.

    A full replace rather than a diff: the portal holds a copy of our state, and reconciling a
    diff against a copy is how copies drift. content_hash makes an unchanged push free, so we
    can re-push whenever we are unsure rather than tracking what we already sent.

    Args:
        conn: The database connection.

    Returns:
        Days, times, day_times (each with `remaining`), categories, positions and slots, plus
        a `content_hash` over all of them.
    """
    def rows(sql: str) -> list[dict]:
        return [dict(r) for r in conn.execute(sql).fetchall()]

    days = rows("SELECT day_key, day_str, event_date, 0 AS sort_order FROM days_table ORDER BY day_key")
    times = rows("SELECT time_key, time_str, 0 AS sort_order FROM times_table ORDER BY time_key")
    # Each timeslot carries `remaining`, which is what the signup form offers. Overage
    # changes it, so a new percentage changes the hash and is pushed like any other edit.
    remaining = compute_remaining(conn)
    day_times = rows("SELECT day_key, time_key FROM day_times ORDER BY day_key, time_key")
    for dt in day_times:
        dt["remaining"] = remaining.get((dt["day_key"], dt["time_key"]), 0)
    cats = rows("SELECT cat_name, sort_order, cat_color FROM categories ORDER BY sort_order")
    positions = rows("SELECT pos_key, pos_cat, pos_str FROM positions ORDER BY pos_key")
    slots = rows("SELECT day_key, time_key, pos_key, vol_id FROM schedule "
                 "ORDER BY day_key, time_key, pos_key")

    payload = {
        "days": days, "times": times, "day_times": day_times, "categories": cats,
        "positions": positions, "slots": slots,
    }
    payload["content_hash"] = hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()
    ).hexdigest()
    return payload

def overage_pct(conn) -> int:
    """The organizer's overbooking allowance, a whole percentage (app_kv portal_overage_pct).

    0 until set. Clamped, so a stray value can't open the floodgates.

    Args:
        conn: The database connection.

    Returns:
        The percentage, between 0 and `OVERAGE_MAX`.
    """
    row = conn.execute("SELECT val FROM app_kv WHERE app_key = 'portal_overage_pct'").fetchone()
    try:
        pct = int(row["val"]) if row else 0
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        pct = 0
    return max(0, min(OVERAGE_MAX, pct))

docs.title: compute_remaining(conn, pct: Optional[int] = None) -> dict
docs.text:
How many more volunteers the signup form may take for each timeslot.

capacity  = floor(slots in the timeslot x (1 + overage%))
remaining = capacity - assigned there - picked it but not yet assigned there

Overage is the deliberate overbooking against volunteers who drop out between signup and the event. Counting all slots in capacity, minus assigned ones, rather than open slots alone, keeps remaining steady when an organizer assigns a volunteer to the slot they picked: assigned goes up by one and "picked, not yet assigned" down by one.

A pick counts until that volunteer holds an assignment on the same day AND at the same start time; pending and approved volunteers count, cancelled or inactive ones don't. Returns {(day_key, time_key): remaining}, never below 0.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default conn

The database connection.

required pct Optional[int]

The overage percentage to use. None reads the stored one.

None Source code in backend/portal_sync.py 
def compute_remaining(conn, pct: Optional[int] = None) -> dict:
    """How many more volunteers the signup form may take for each timeslot.

        capacity  = floor(slots in the timeslot x (1 + overage%))
        remaining = capacity - assigned there - picked it but not yet assigned there

    Overage is the deliberate overbooking against volunteers who drop out between signup and
    the event. Counting *all* slots in capacity, minus assigned ones, rather than open slots
    alone, keeps remaining steady when an organizer assigns a volunteer to the slot they
    picked: assigned goes up by one and "picked, not yet assigned" down by one.

    A pick counts until that volunteer holds an assignment on the same day AND at the same
    start time; pending and approved volunteers count, cancelled or inactive ones don't. Returns
    {(day_key, time_key): remaining}, never below 0.

    Args:
        conn: The database connection.
        pct: The overage percentage to use. `None` reads the stored one.
    """
    pct = overage_pct(conn) if pct is None else pct
    out: dict = {}
    cells = {(r["day_key"], r["time_key"]): (r["total"], r["assigned"] or 0)
             for r in conn.execute(
                 "SELECT day_key, time_key, COUNT(*) AS total, "
                 "SUM(CASE WHEN vol_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS assigned "
                 "FROM schedule GROUP BY day_key, time_key").fetchall()}
    committed: dict = {}
    if _has_table(conn, "vol_picks"):
        for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT vp.day_key, vp.time_key, COUNT(*) AS n FROM vol_picks vp "
            "JOIN volunteers v ON v.vol_id = vp.vol_id "
            "WHERE vp.kind = 'pref' AND v.is_counted "
            "  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM schedule s WHERE s.vol_id = vp.vol_id "
            "                  AND s.day_key = vp.day_key AND s.time_key = vp.time_key) "
            "GROUP BY vp.day_key, vp.time_key"
        ).fetchall():
            committed[(r["day_key"], r["time_key"])] = r["n"]
    for cell, (total, assigned) in cells.items():
        capacity = (total * (100 + pct)) // 100
        out[cell] = max(0, capacity - assigned - committed.get(cell, 0))
    return out

def build_branding(conn) -> dict:
    """The site title, portal title and logos, as one payload for the portal.

    Args:
        conn: The database connection.

    Returns:
        `app_title`, `portal_title`, `logo`, `favicon` and `header_logo` (data URLs or `None`),
        `contact_email`, `conference_url` and `code_of_conduct_url`, plus a `content_hash`.
    """
    rows = {r["app_key"]: r["val"] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT app_key, val FROM app_kv "
        "WHERE app_key IN ('app_title', 'app_logo', 'app_favicon', 'app_header_logo', "
        "'portal_title', 'contact_email', 'conference_url', 'code_of_conduct_url')"
    ).fetchall()}
    # logo is the year's theme logo (the favicon is made from it); header_logo the smaller
    # one the volunteer pages show top left. A portal older than schema v4 ignores it.
    payload = {
        "app_title": rows.get("app_title"),
        "portal_title": rows.get("portal_title"),
        "logo": rows.get("app_logo"),
        "favicon": rows.get("app_favicon"),
        "header_logo": rows.get("app_header_logo"),
        # The conference's public contact address and links (setup wizard, App Settings).
        # A portal older than schema v6 ignores them.
        "contact_email": rows.get("contact_email"),
        "conference_url": rows.get("conference_url"),
        "code_of_conduct_url": rows.get("code_of_conduct_url"),
    }
    payload["content_hash"] = hashlib.sha256(
        json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()
    ).hexdigest()
    return payload

def build_invites(conn) -> dict:
    """Every early-access invite, as hashes, for the portal (POST /api/sync/signup_invites).

    The portal replaces its list with this one, keeping its own record of uses. Timestamps go
    as UTC with a Z, which the portal normalises.

    rows = conn.execute(

        "ORDER BY invite_id;").fetchall()

async def purge_volunteers(conn, vol_ids: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Delete volunteers on the portal, then here. Returns the ids deleted here.

    Portal first: deleted here first, the next pull would bring them straight back. Each
    volunteer's pending re-key id (portal_rekey_from) goes too, since the portal may still
    know them by it. Without a portal configured there's nothing to purge there.

    Here (_PURGE_LOCAL_SQL, one transaction with the delete): picks, notes (check-ins and
    ratings too) and shift flags are deleted, and schedule slots and radio checkouts keep
    their row with vol_id NULL (radio history keeps person_name).

    Args:
        conn: A PgClient.
        vol_ids: The scheduler ids to purge.

    Returns:
        The ids whose rows were deleted here.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: The portal call failed in any way; nothing was deleted here.
    """
    async with _state.lock:
        rows = conn.execute(
            "SELECT vol_id, portal_rekey_from FROM volunteers WHERE vol_id = ANY(?::text[])",
            (list(vol_ids),)).fetchall()
        conn.commit()
        if configured() and rows:
            portal_ids = sorted({r["vol_id"] for r in rows}
                                | {r["portal_rekey_from"] for r in rows if r["portal_rekey_from"]})
            try:
                await _request("POST", "/api/sync/purge_volunteers",
                               {"op_id": _op_id(), "vol_ids": portal_ids})
            # Deliberately broad: a refusal, a timeout and a connection error all mean the
            # same here (stop before deleting anything locally), and the caller reports it.
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
                raise RuntimeError(f"portal purge failed: {exc}") from exc
        for stmt in _PURGE_LOCAL_SQL:
            conn.execute(stmt, (list(vol_ids),))
        deleted = [r["vol_id"] for r in conn.execute(
            "DELETE FROM volunteers WHERE vol_id = ANY(?::text[]) RETURNING vol_id",
            (list(vol_ids),)).fetchall()]
        conn.commit()
    request_push()
    return sorted(deleted)

async def pull_security_events(conn) -> int:
    """Copy the portal's security events (its SecuritySignals findings) into the audit log.

    Each becomes an audit event with source "portal", written to logs/audit.jsonl and
    audit_events and run through the alert rules, exactly like one of ours. The cursor is
    the portal's row id, kept as stream "security_events_pull".

    Args:
        conn: The database connection, for the cursor.

    Returns:
        How many events were taken.
    """
    cursor = cursor_of(_get_state(conn, "security_events_pull"))
    taken = 0
    while True:
        data = await _request("GET", f"/api/sync/security_events?since={cursor}&limit=500")
        events = data.get("events") or []
        for e in events:
            if audit.ingest(e, "portal"):
                taken += 1
        nxt = data.get("next", cursor)
        if not isinstance(nxt, int) or nxt <= cursor:
            break
        cursor = nxt
        _mark_ok(conn, "security_events_pull", cursor)
        if len(events) < 500:
            break
    return taken

async def pull_volunteers(conn) -> int:
    """Mirror changed volunteers, and their timeslot picks, into our own tables.

    Volunteer-owned columns and picks are always taken. Scheduler-owned ones (status, name)
    are skipped while the row is portal_dirty: it holds a local decision the portal hasn't
    accepted yet, and the portal's older status must not undo it; the portal echoes the
    decision back once the push lands. The old id of a pending badge-number re-key is skipped
    entirely, or it would resurrect the pending row beside its renamed copy.

    A pick naming a timeslot we no longer run is dropped (vol_picks has a foreign key to
    day_times). Dropping a timeslot the volunteer is assigned to raises a shift flag
    (_flag_dropped_assignments) for the banner in the organizer app.

    Returns how many rows were written.

    Args:
        conn: The database connection. Committed after each page of 500.
    """
    state = _get_state(conn, "volunteers_pull")
    cursor = cursor_of(state)
    written = 0
    known = {(r["day_key"], r["time_key"])
             for r in conn.execute("SELECT day_key, time_key FROM day_times").fetchall()}
    while True:
        data = await _request("GET", f"/api/sync/volunteers?since={cursor}&limit=500")
        rows = data.get("volunteers") or []
        for v in rows:
            if conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM volunteers WHERE portal_rekey_from = ? "
                            "AND portal_dirty", (v["vol_id"],)).fetchone():
                continue
            local = conn.execute("SELECT portal_dirty FROM volunteers WHERE vol_id = ?",
                                 (v["vol_id"],)).fetchone()
            answers = (json.dumps(v["answers"]) if isinstance(v.get("answers"), (dict, list))
                       else v.get("answers"))
            owned = (v.get("time_pref") or "", v.get("add_time") or "",
                     bool(v.get("add_any")), answers, v.get("cancelled_at") or None)
            if local and local["portal_dirty"]:
                conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE volunteers SET time_pref = ?, add_time = ?, add_any = ?, answers = ?, "
                    "cancelled_at = ? WHERE vol_id = ?", (*owned, v["vol_id"]))
            else:
                # inactive_at is ours, so it's never taken from the portal.
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO volunteers (vol_id, name, status, time_pref, add_time, add_any, "
                    "answers, cancelled_at, email_enc, email_hmac, email_key_fp, "
                    "possible_duplicate_of) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) "
                    "ON CONFLICT(vol_id) DO UPDATE SET name = excluded.name, "
                    "status = excluded.status, time_pref = excluded.time_pref, "
                    "add_time = excluded.add_time, add_any = excluded.add_any, "
                    "answers = excluded.answers, cancelled_at = excluded.cancelled_at, "
                    "email_enc = excluded.email_enc, "
                    "email_hmac = excluded.email_hmac, email_key_fp = excluded.email_key_fp, "
                    "possible_duplicate_of = excluded.possible_duplicate_of",
                    (v["vol_id"], v.get("name") or "", v.get("status") or "pending", *owned,
                     v.get("email_enc"), v.get("email_hmac"), v.get("email_key_fp"),
                     json.dumps(v["possible_duplicate_of"])
                     if isinstance(v.get("possible_duplicate_of"), (dict, list))
                     else v.get("possible_duplicate_of")),
                )
            if v.get("invite_id"):
                # The early-access invite this signup used. Keep the first use; the portal
                # already refuses a second.
                conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE signup_invites SET used_at = NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', used_by = ? "
                    "WHERE invite_id = ? AND used_at IS NULL",
                    (v.get("name") or v["vol_id"], v["invite_id"]))
            if "picks" in v:
                incoming = [p for p in v.get("picks") or []
                            if (p.get("day_key"), p.get("time_key")) in known]
                _flag_dropped_assignments(conn, v["vol_id"],
                                          {(p["day_key"], p["time_key"]) for p in incoming})
                conn.execute("DELETE FROM vol_picks WHERE vol_id = ?", (v["vol_id"],))
                for p in incoming:
                    conn.execute(
                        "INSERT INTO vol_picks (vol_id, day_key, time_key, kind, rank) "
                        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
                        (v["vol_id"], p["day_key"], p["time_key"], p.get("kind") or "pref",
                         p.get("rank")),
                    )
            written += 1
        conn.commit()
        cursor = data.get("cursor", cursor)
        if not data.get("more"):
            break
    _mark_ok(conn, "volunteers_pull", cursor)
    if written:
        # Open organizer browsers refresh the shift-flag banner and volunteer lists. Lazy, as
        # routers.events imports this module lazily too.
        from routers.events import broadcast
        broadcast("volunteers")
    return written

def build_volunteer_push(conn) -> tuple[list, list]:
    """Every volunteer owed to the portal, and the re-keys to apply first.

    Only SCHEDULER_OWNED columns are sent. Picks, answers and the name parts are the
    volunteer's (the portal's upsert updates only the columns a push carries), so a push can't
    overwrite an edit the volunteer made while an approval was waiting to go out.

    Args:
        conn: The database connection.

    Returns:
        `(volunteers, rekeys)`: the `portal_dirty` rows, and the renames they need.
    """
    vols, rekeys = [], []
    for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT vol_id, name, status, inactive_at, portal_rekey_from FROM volunteers "
        "WHERE portal_dirty ORDER BY vol_id"
    ).fetchall():
        rec = {"vol_id": r["vol_id"], **{c: r[c] for c in SCHEDULER_OWNED}}
        if rec["inactive_at"]:
            rec["inactive_at"] = rec["inactive_at"].isoformat() + "Z"
        vols.append(rec)
        if r["portal_rekey_from"]:
            rekeys.append({"vol_id": r["portal_rekey_from"], "new_vol_id": r["vol_id"]})
    return vols, rekeys

async def push_dirty_volunteers(conn) -> int:
    """Push owed volunteer changes; clear the flag on what the portal accepted.

    The clear matches on status too, so a second decision made while this push was in flight
    stays dirty and goes on the next tick instead of being marked sent.

    Args:
        conn: The database connection.

    Returns:
        How many volunteers were pushed.
    """
    vols, rekeys = build_volunteer_push(conn)
    if not vols:
        return 0
    await push_volunteers(conn, vols, rekeys)
    for v in vols:
        conn.execute(
            "UPDATE volunteers SET portal_dirty = FALSE, portal_rekey_from = NULL "
            "WHERE vol_id = ? AND status = ? AND portal_dirty",
            (v["vol_id"], v["status"]),
        )
    conn.commit()
    return len(vols)

def pubkey_fingerprint(pem: str) -> str:
    """The portal's security.pubkey_fingerprint, reimplemented: ``SHA256:<b64>`` of the SPKI
    DER, padding stripped. Compared against the heartbeat's pubkey_fp.

    Args:
        pem: A PEM public key.

    Returns:
        The fingerprint, as `SHA256:<base64>`.
    """
    der = base64.b64decode("".join(
        line.strip() for line in pem.strip().splitlines()
        if line.strip() and not line.strip().startswith("-----")))
    return "SHA256:" + base64.b64encode(hashlib.sha256(der).digest()).decode().rstrip("=")

async def sync_settings(conn, heartbeat: dict) -> Optional[list]:
    """Push signup-open and the email public key when the portal's differ. Returns what was
    pushed, or None.

    The public key matters most: the portal encrypts every signup's address to it and refuses
    to open signup without one, so a key uploaded here must reach the portal unprompted.

    Args:
        conn: The database connection.
        heartbeat: The portal's latest heartbeat, for the fingerprint of the key it holds.
    """
    want = local_settings(conn)
    remote = await _request("GET", "/api/sync/config")
    diff = {}
    if (remote.get("settings") or {}).get("portal_signup_open") != want["portal_signup_open"]:
        diff["portal_signup_open"] = want["portal_signup_open"]
    want_fp = pubkey_fingerprint(want["email_pubkey"]) if want["email_pubkey"] else None
    if heartbeat.get("pubkey_fp") != want_fp:
        diff["email_pubkey"] = want["email_pubkey"]  # None clears it there too
    if not diff:
        return None
    await push_settings(conn, diff)
    return sorted(diff)

In-memory sliding-window limits, for the backend's single worker.

SlidingWindow counts events per key over a window and says whether a key is over its limit. Password sign-in (routers/auth.py) and password reset (routers/password_reset.py) use it. Counts live in process memory: a restart forgets them, which is fine for limits measured in minutes, and correct only because the backend runs one uvicorn worker.

Keys are whatever the caller builds ("ip:…", "user:…", "user-ip:…"). Pass an IP through api_auth.rate_key first, so an IPv6 client counts by its /64.

def over(self, *keys: str) -> bool:
    """Whether any of `keys` is already at its limit. Records nothing.

    Args:

    with self._lock:

def allow(self, *keys: str) -> bool:
    """Check and record in one step: count against every key only if none is over.

    Args:
        *keys: The keys to check and count against.

    Returns:
        False if any key is at its limit (nothing recorded), else True.
    """
    now = _monotonic()
    with self._lock:
        if any(len(self._trim(k, now)) >= self.limit for k in keys):
            return False
        for k in keys:
            self._hits[k].append(now)
    return True

def retry_after(self, *keys: str) -> int:
    """Seconds until every one of `keys` is under its limit again (0 if already).

    Args:
        *keys: The keys to check.

    Returns:
        Whole seconds, rounded up.
    """
    now = _monotonic()
    wait = 0.0
    with self._lock:
        for k in keys:
            q = self._trim(k, now)
            if len(q) >= self.limit:
                # The oldest event that must expire to bring the count under the limit.
                wait = max(wait, q[len(q) - self.limit] + self.window_sec - now)
    return int(wait) + (1 if wait % 1 else 0)

docs.title: backend.security_signals
docs.text:
Request signals: malformed input, attack patterns and probing, noticed for alerting.

SecuritySignals is an ASGI middleware that watches every request and response and reports what looks hostile. It never refuses a client: the one request it answers itself is one carrying a NUL character, which no browser sends and the database can't take (a 400). Everything else goes through untouched; this only watches.

This file is identical in backend/ and portal/ (the apps share no code, so each has a copy; backend/test_security_signals.py fails if they differ). Each app passes in what differs: how to read the client's address, where findings go, and which paths to skip.

What it looks at, before the route runs:

  • Signatures (SIGNATURES, SCANNER_AGENT, PROBE_PATH): SQL injection, path traversal, script injection, template and command injection, scanner user agents and the paths scanners try. Checked in the path, the query string, the User-Agent and form fields (urlencoded or multipart, up to BODY_LIMIT; file parts and any field named like a password are skipped). Deliberately narrow, so O'Brien, "Rock & Roll" or a note saying "drop off at the desk" never match.
  • A NUL anywhere in those: refused with a 400.
  • Cross-site writes: a POST (PUT, PATCH, DELETE) the browser marks Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site, or whose Origin isn't one of the app's own.
  • A session cookie whose signature fails (when the app passes cookie_check).

and after it, the response status: 404 under the API prefix (probing), 422 and 400 (malformed input), 401, 403 (reaching above a role), 405, 413, 415.

Each signal has a weight (WEIGHTS). A client's weights add up over WINDOW_SEC; crossing SCORE_ALERT is a suspicious_client finding. Any signature is an attack_signature finding at once. A 401 under critical_prefix (the portal's signed sync API, which no browser calls) is a sync_auth_fail. Each finding is reported at most once per client per NOTE_COOLDOWN_SEC; the ones in between are counted and the next report carries the count. So a scanner's thousand requests are a handful of rows, not a thousand, and single 404s or 422s are never rows at all, only counts in memory.

Clients are counted by address, an IPv6 one by its /64. State is in memory, capped at MAX_CLIENTS (oldest dropped), for the one worker each app runs.

def client_key(ip: str) -> str:
    """What a client is counted by: an IPv6 address's /64, otherwise the address.

    Args:
        ip: The client's address, or anything else.

    Returns:
        The key.
    """
    try:
        addr = ipaddress.ip_address(ip)
    except ValueError:
        return ip
    if isinstance(addr, ipaddress.IPv6Address):
        if addr.ipv4_mapped:
            return str(addr.ipv4_mapped)
        return str(ipaddress.ip_network(f"{addr}/64", strict=False))
    return str(addr)

def inspect_text(where: str, text: str) -> list:
    """The signature hits (and a NUL) in one piece of text.

    Args:
        where: What the text is, for the report.
        text: The text.

    Returns:
        A list of Hit.
    """
    hits = []
    if "\x00" in text:
        i = text.index("\x00")
        hits.append(Hit("nul", "nul", where, _snippet(text, i, i + 1)))
    for name, pattern in SIGNATURES:
        m = pattern.search(text)
        if m:
            hits.append(Hit("signature", name, where, _snippet(text, m.start(), m.end())))
    return hits

def inspect_head(request: Request) -> list:
    """Hits in what every request has: path, query string, User-Agent.

    Args:
        request: The request.

    Returns:
        A list of Hit.
    """
    path = request.url.path
    hits = inspect_text("path", path)
    raw = request.scope.get("raw_path") or b""
    if b"%00" in raw.lower() or b"%2500" in raw.lower():
        hits.append(Hit("nul", "nul", "path", path[:SNIPPET]))
    if PROBE_PATH.search(path):
        hits.append(Hit("probe_path", "probe_path", "path", path[:SNIPPET]))
    for name, value in request.query_params.multi_items():
        if not _SECRET_FIELD.search(name):
            hits += inspect_text(f"query:{name[:40]}", value)
            hits += inspect_text("query", name)
    agent = request.headers.get("user-agent", "")
    if SCANNER_AGENT.search(agent):
        hits.append(Hit("scanner", "scanner_agent", "user-agent", agent[:SNIPPET]))
    hits += inspect_text("user-agent", agent)
    return hits

@router.get("/api/api_tokens")
def list_tokens(
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Every key, newest first, with whether it still works. Never the key or its hash.

    Args:
        s_data: The organizer's session.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Returns:
        dict with ``tokens`` (list) and ``scopes`` (name → description) for the create form.
    """
    rows = db.execute(
        "SELECT token_id, label, scopes, allowed_ips, created_by, created_at, expires_at, "
        "revoked_at, last_used_at, last_used_ip, "
        "(revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS active "
        "FROM api_tokens ORDER BY created_at DESC;"
    ).fetchall()
    tokens = [{
        **dict(r),
        "scopes": r["scopes"].split(),
        "allowed_ips": r["allowed_ips"].split(),
        **{k: _iso(r[k]) for k in ("created_at", "expires_at", "revoked_at", "last_used_at")},
    } for r in rows]
    return {"tokens": tokens, "scopes": api_auth.SCOPES}

@router.post("/api/api_tokens")
def create_token(
    request: Request,
    label: str = Form(default=""),
    scopes: str = Form(default=""),
    expires_days: int = Form(default=DEFAULT_DAYS),
    allowed_ips: str = Form(default=""),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Create a key.

    Args:
        label: Who or what it's for, e.g. "Badge app – Sam"; shown in the list and audit log.
        scopes: Space- or comma-separated names from api_auth.SCOPES; at least one.
        expires_days: 1 to MAX_DAYS.
        allowed_ips: Optional space- or comma-separated addresses / CIDRs; blank for any.

    Returns:
        dict with ``token_id``, ``key`` (shown once; never retrievable later) and ``expires_at``.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Blank or over-long label, unknown or no scopes, bad expiry or IP.
    """
    label = " ".join(label.split())
    if not label or len(label) > MAX_LABEL:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"A label of 1-{MAX_LABEL} characters is required")
    wanted = sorted(set(scopes.replace(",", " ").split()))
    unknown = [s for s in wanted if s not in api_auth.SCOPES]
    if not wanted or unknown:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Pick at least one scope" if not wanted
                            else f"Unknown scope: {', '.join(unknown)}")
    if not 1 <= expires_days <= MAX_DAYS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Expiry must be 1-{MAX_DAYS} days")
    try:
        nets = api_auth.parse_allowed_ips(allowed_ips)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Not an IP address or network: {exc}") \
            from exc

    key = api_auth.new_key()
    token_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    row = db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO api_tokens (token_id, token_hash, label, scopes, allowed_ips, created_by, "
        "expires_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, "
        "NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' + make_interval(days => ?)) RETURNING expires_at;",
        (token_id, api_auth.key_hash(key), label, " ".join(wanted), " ".join(nets),
         s_data["username"], expires_days),
    ).fetchone()
    db.commit()
    audit("api_key.create", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Created API key {label!r} ({token_id}) with {' '.join(wanted)}")
    return {"token_id": token_id, "key": key, "expires_at": _iso(row["expires_at"])}

@router.post("/api/api_tokens/revoke")
def revoke_token(
    request: Request,
    token_id: str = Form(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Revoke a key at once. Revoking one already revoked or expired changes nothing.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, for the session id and the audit log.
        token_id: The key to revoke.
        s_data: The organizer's session.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 404: No such key.
    """
    row = db.execute("SELECT label FROM api_tokens WHERE token_id = ?;", (token_id,)).fetchone()
    if not row:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="No such key")
    db.execute("UPDATE api_tokens SET revoked_at = NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' "
               "WHERE token_id = ? AND revoked_at IS NULL;", (token_id,))
    db.commit()
    audit("api_key.revoke", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Revoked API key {row['label']!r} ({token_id})")
    return {"ok": True}

@router.get("/api/admin/audit")
def list_events(
    request: Request,
    event: str = Query(default="", max_length=64, description="Event code prefix, e.g. auth."),
    min_severity: str = Query(default="info", description="info, low, medium, high, critical"),
    actor: str = Query(default="", max_length=100),
    ip: str = Query(default="", max_length=64, description="Address prefix"),
    source: str = Query(default="", description="backend or portal; blank for both"),
    q: str = Query(default="", max_length=100, description="Text in the message"),
    before_id: int | None = Query(default=None, ge=1),
    limit: int = Query(default=100, ge=1, le=PAGE_MAX),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Audit events, newest first.

    Args:
        request: The request, for auditing the read itself.
        event: Only codes starting with this.
        min_severity: Only this severity and above.
        actor: Only actors containing this (case-insensitive).
        ip: Only addresses starting with this.
        source: Only this source.
        q: Only messages containing this (case-insensitive).
        before_id: Only events older than this id (the previous page's `next_before_id`).
        limit: At most this many.
        s_data: The caller's session; organizers only.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Returns:
        `{"events": [...], "next_before_id": id or None}`.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: An unknown severity or source.
    """
    if min_severity not in SEVERITY_ORDER:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Unknown severity")
    if source not in ("", "backend", "portal"):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Unknown source")
    levels = list(SEVERITY_ORDER[SEVERITY_ORDER.index(min_severity):])
    rows = db.execute(_EVENTS_SQL, (
        event, _like(event, prefix_only=True), levels, actor, _like(actor),
        ip, _like(ip, prefix_only=True), source, source, q, _like(q),
        before_id, before_id, limit)).fetchall()
    if before_id is None:
        audit("audit.view", request, request.session.get("session_id"), "Opened the audit log",
              filters={k: v for k, v in (("event", event), ("min_severity", min_severity),
                                         ("actor", actor), ("ip", ip), ("source", source),
                                         ("q", q)) if v and v != "info"})
    return {"events": rows,
            "next_before_id": rows[-1]["id"] if len(rows) == limit else None,
            "viewer": s_data["username"]}

        "you": s_data["username"],

@router.post("/api/admin/audit/test_alert")
async def test_alert(request: Request, s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer"))):
    """Mail a test alert to everyone alerts go to, now, and say how many it reached.

    Goes the whole way a real alert does (portal, relay, inbox), without the retry, and at
    most once a minute.

    Args:
        request: The request, for the audit log.
        s_data: The caller's session; organizers only.

    Returns:
        `{"reached": n, "recipients": n}`.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 429: Another test in the last minute.
    """
    if not _test_alerts.allow("test"):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail="One test alert a minute. Try again shortly.",
                            headers={"Retry-After": str(_test_alerts.retry_after("test"))})
    audit("alert.test", request, request.session.get("session_id"), "Sent a test alert")
    alert = alerts.Alert("test", "Test alert from the audit log page", "low", [
        ("Sent by", s_data["username"]),
        ("Why", "Checking that security alerts reach you. Nothing has happened."),
    ])
    people = len(await asyncio.to_thread(alerts.recipients))
    reached = await alerts.deliver(alert, retry=False)
    return {"reached": reached, "recipients": people}

docs.title: backend.routers.auth
docs.text:
Organizer sign-in with a password, and sign-out.

Passwords are Argon2 hashes. A successful sign-in creates a sessions row and puts its id in the signed session cookie. start_session is shared with the passkey and invite routers, so every way in produces the same session.

Failed sign-ins are rate limited (LOGIN_LIMITS), checked before the password is: a refused request is a 429 with Retry-After and never tests a password. Only failures count, because at the event every check-in laptop shares the venue's one address. The limits are per username from one address, per address, and a much higher per-username ceiling across all addresses, so a stranger who knows a username can't lock its owner out from elsewhere while a spread-out guessing run still hits a wall (and the alerts fire long before it). A successful sign-in clears its username-and-address count. An unknown username is checked against a dummy hash, so its reply takes as long as a wrong password's.

@router.post("/api/login")
def login(
    request: Request,
    username: str = Form(...),
    password: str = Form(...),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Verify credentials, create a session record, and set the session cookie.

    Passwords are hashed with Argon2

    Session IDs are generated with UUID4

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; client IP and user-agent stored in the sessions table.
        username: Login username; lowercased before lookup.
        password: Plaintext password verified against the stored Argon2 hash.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        dict with keys ``username`` and ``role``.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 401: User not found or password mismatch.
        HTTPException 429: Too many failed sign-ins for this username or from this address
            (`LOGIN_LIMITS`); `Retry-After` says when to try again.
    """
    username = username.lower()
    keys = _login_keys(username, request)
    refused = _throttled(request, username, keys)
    if refused:
        raise refused

    # Postgres can't take a NUL in a query parameter (psycopg2 raises, which was a 500). No
    # username has one, so it's simply an unknown user.
    row = None if "\x00" in username else db.execute(
        "SELECT user_id, username, password_hash, failed_login_cnt, role FROM users "
        "WHERE username = ?;",
        (username,)
    ).fetchone()
    if not row:
        with suppress(VerifyMismatchError):          # for the time it takes; never matches
            _hasher.verify(_DUMMY_HASH, password)
        raise _failed(request, username, keys, "unknown_user")

    try:
        _hasher.verify(row["password_hash"], password)
    except VerifyMismatchError:
        new_failed = row["failed_login_cnt"] + 1
        db.execute("UPDATE users SET failed_login_cnt = ? WHERE username = ?;",
                   (new_failed, username))
        db.commit()
        raise _failed(request, username, keys, "bad_password") from None

    _login_fails["user_ip"].clear(keys["user_ip"])
    result = start_session(request, db, row)
    audit("auth.login.ok", request, request.session.get("session_id"), "Signed in with a password")
    return result

def start_session(request: Request, db: PgClient, row: dict) -> dict:
    """Create a session for an authenticated user and set the cookie.

    Shared by the password login and the passkey login (routers/passkeys.py), so both
    produce exactly the same session.

    Args:
        row: A ``users`` row with at least ``user_id``, ``username`` and ``role``.

    Returns:
        dict with keys ``username`` and ``role``.
    """
    session_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    user_id = row["user_id"]
    role = row["role"] or "organizer"

    db.execute(
        "UPDATE users SET last_login_at = NOW(), failed_login_cnt = 0 WHERE user_id = ?;",
        (user_id,)
    )
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO sessions (session_id, user_id, ip_addr, user_agent) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?);",
        (session_id, user_id, client_ip(request),
         request.headers.get("user-agent", ""))
    )
    db.commit()

    request.session["session_id"] = session_id
    _session_cache[session_id] = {"user_id": user_id, "username": row["username"], "role": role}

    return {"username": row["username"], "role": role}

        HTTP 200 with an empty body.
    """
    s_id = request.session.pop("session_id", None)
    if s_id:
        audit("auth.logout", request, s_id, "Signed out")
        _session_cache.pop(s_id, None)
        db.execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE session_id = ?;", (s_id,))
        db.commit()
    return Response(status_code=200)

def record_checkin(request: Request, db: PgClient, s_data: dict,
                   vol_id: str, slot_key: str, force: bool) -> dict:
    """Check a volunteer in to a slot, unless they're early or late and force isn't set.

    Shared by the scanner (POST /api/checkin/scan) and the slot dialog's button
    (POST /api/checkin_vol), so both apply the same rule.

    More than EARLY_MINUTES before the start, or more than LATE_MINUTES after it, returns
    ``needs_confirm`` and writes nothing; the caller asks the operator and resends with force.
    A forced early or late check-in also records a ``[CheckInTiming]`` note, which the notes
    report shows and reset_vol_status clears. A shift with no event_date, or a time_str that
    isn't a range, can't be judged: it checks in with timing ``unknown``.

    Args:
        request: The request, for the audit log.
        db: The database connection. Committed on a check-in.
        s_data: The operator's session. Their username goes on the note.
        vol_id: The volunteer being checked in.
        slot_key: The shift, `{day_key}_{time_key}_{pos_key}`.
        force: Check in even when early or late, after the operator confirmed.

    Returns:
        The volunteer and shift, `timing` and `minutes`, and three flags: `checked_in`,
        `already` (checked in before) and `needs_confirm`.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 409: The volunteer isn't (or is no longer) assigned to that slot.
    """
    slot = _slot(db, slot_key)
    if not slot or slot["vol_id"] != vol_id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409,
                            detail="That volunteer isn't assigned to this shift any more.")

    start = checkin_codes.shift_start(slot["event_date"], slot["time_str"], event_tz(db))
    timing, minutes = checkin_codes.classify(datetime.now(timezone.utc), start)
    result = {
        "vol_id": vol_id, "name": slot["vol_name"], "slot_key": slot_key,
        "day": slot["day_str"], "time": slot["time_str"],
        "position": slot["pos_str"], "category": slot["pos_cat"],
        "start": start.isoformat() if start else None,
        "timing": timing, "minutes": minutes,
        "checked_in": False, "already": False, "needs_confirm": False,
    }

    note = f"[CheckIn] | {slot_key}"
    if db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM vol_notes WHERE vol_id = ? AND note = ?;",
                  (vol_id, note)).fetchone():
        return {**result, "checked_in": True, "already": True}

    if timing in ("early", "late") and not force:
        return {**result, "needs_confirm": True}

    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO vol_notes (vol_id, note, username, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, NOW());",
        (vol_id, note, s_data["username"])
    )
    if timing in ("early", "late"):
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO vol_notes (vol_id, note, username, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, NOW());",
            (vol_id, f"[CheckInTiming] {timing.capitalize()} {minutes} min | {slot_key}",
             s_data["username"])
        )
    db.commit()
    broadcast("checkin")
    extra = f" ({timing} {minutes} min, confirmed)" if timing in ("early", "late") else ""
    audit("checkin.ok", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Checked in vol_id={vol_id} for {slot_key}{extra}.")
    return {**result, "checked_in": True}

@router.post("/api/checkin/scan")
def scan_checkin(
    request: Request,
    code: str = Form(...),
    force: bool = Form(default=False),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer", "checkin")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Check a volunteer in from the code on their schedule email.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        code: The scanned or typed check-in code.
        force: Check in even when early or late (the operator's "Check in anyway").
        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer or checkin role.
        db: Injected PgClient.

    Returns:
        The record_checkin result: who, which shift, timing, and whether it was written.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Not a genuine check-in code (or one from before a key rotation).
        HTTPException 409: The volunteer is no longer assigned to that shift.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    found = checkin_codes.verify_code(checkin_key(db), code)
    if not found:
        audit("checkin.code_rejected", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
              "Rejected a check-in code.")
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="That isn't a valid check-in code.")
    vol_id, slot_key = found
    return record_checkin(request, db, s_data, vol_id, slot_key, force)

@router.post("/api/email_pubkey")
def set_email_pubkey(
    request: Request,
    pubkey: str = Form(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Store or replace the RSA public key used to encrypt volunteer email addresses.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        pubkey: SPKI PEM string for an RSA-OAEP key; validated client-side before submission.
        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer role.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        dict ``{"ok": True}``.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: pubkey is empty after stripping whitespace.

          "Updated email public key")
    # The portal encrypts signups to this key and keeps signup shut without one.
    portal_sync.request_push()
    return {"ok": True}

@router.post("/api/email_template")
def save_template(
    request: Request,
    subject: str = Form(default=""),
    body_md: str = Form(default=""),
    shift_md: str = Form(default=""),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Save the template. Problems that would break sending are refused; images the template
    refers to but that aren't uploaded yet are allowed (upload them next) and listed.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, for the session id and the audit log.
        subject: The subject line template.
        body_md: The body, in Markdown.
        shift_md: The block repeated once per shift, in Markdown.
        s_data: The organizer's session. Their username is recorded as `updated_by`.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: An unknown placeholder, no {{shifts}} or {{qr}}, a blank subject.
        HTTPException 413: Over MAX_TEXT.
    """
    if max(len(subject), len(body_md), len(shift_md)) > MAX_TEXT:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail="The template is too long")
    problems = email_render.check_template(subject, body_md, shift_md)
    if problems:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=" ".join(problems))
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO email_template (template_key, subject, body_md, shift_md, updated_by, "
        "updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') "
        "ON CONFLICT (template_key) DO UPDATE SET subject = excluded.subject, "
        "body_md = excluded.body_md, shift_md = excluded.shift_md, "
        "updated_by = excluded.updated_by, updated_at = excluded.updated_at;",
        (TEMPLATE_KEY, subject.strip(), body_md, shift_md, s_data["username"]))
    db.commit()
    audit("email_template.change", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          "Saved the schedule email template")
    return {"ok": True, "missing_assets": _missing_assets(db, body_md, shift_md)}

async def upload_asset(
    request: Request,
    file: UploadFile = File(...),
    name: str = Form(default=""),

    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),

    """Upload (or replace, by name) a PNG, JPEG or GIF for the template.

        name: Optional name to use in ``asset:<name>``; defaults to the file's name. The
            extension is always the image's real type.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Not a PNG, JPEG or GIF; or an unusable name.
        HTTPException 413: Over 1 MB, or over 5 MB for all images together.
    """
    data = await file.read(MAX_ASSET + 1)
    found = _sniff(data)
    if not found:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Only PNG, JPEG and GIF images can be used "
                            "(many mail apps won't show SVG)")
    ctype, ext = found
    stored = _store_asset(db, _asset_name(name or file.filename or "", ext), ctype, data,
                          s_data["username"])
    audit("email_template.change", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Uploaded email image {stored['name']}")
    return stored

@router.post("/api/email_template/assets/site_logo")
def add_site_logo(
    request: Request,
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Copy the App Settings logo into the template's images as ``site-logo.<ext>``.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, for the session id and the audit log.
        s_data: The organizer's session.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 404: No logo is set.
        HTTPException 400: The logo is an SVG (or otherwise not PNG, JPEG or GIF).
    """
    logo = get_app_kv(db, "app_logo")
    if not logo:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="No site logo is set (Admin → App Settings)")
    try:
        data = base64.b64decode(logo.split(",", 1)[1])
    except (IndexError, ValueError):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="The site logo couldn't be read") from None
    found = _sniff(data)
    if not found:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="The site logo isn't a PNG, JPEG or GIF "
                            "(an SVG won't show in many mail apps). Upload a PNG version instead.")
    ctype, ext = found
    stored = _store_asset(db, f"site-logo.{ext}", ctype, data, s_data["username"])
    audit("email_template.change", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          "Copied the site logo into the email images")
    return stored

@router.get("/api/email_template/package")
def package(
    request: Request,
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """The saved template as a zip for tools/vol_mail: manifest, HTML and text, images.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, for the session id and the audit log.
        s_data: The organizer's session. Their username goes in the manifest.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 409: The saved template has problems, or refers to images not uploaded.
    """
    t = _load(db)
    problems = email_render.check_template(t["subject"], t["body_md"], t["shift_md"])
    missing = _missing_assets(db, t["body_md"], t["shift_md"])
    if missing:
        problems.append("Images not uploaded yet: " + ", ".join(missing))
    if problems:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=" ".join(problems))
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    meta = {"created_at": now.isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z"), "created_by": s_data["username"],
            "event_title": get_app_kv(db, "app_title") or "",
            "template_updated_at": t["updated_at"]}
    data = email_render.build_package(t["subject"], t["body_md"], t["shift_md"],
                                      _assets(db, with_data=True), meta)
    audit("email_template.download", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          "Downloaded the schedule email package")
    fname = f"schedule-email-{now:%Y%m%d-%H%M}.zip"
    return Response(content=data, media_type="application/zip",
                    headers={"Content-Disposition": f'attachment; filename="{fname}"'})

GET /api/events is an SSE stream. Endpoints call broadcast("schedule"), "volunteers", "checkin" and so on after a change, and each browser refetches what it shows. Events that change what the portal holds also trigger a portal push.

def broadcast(event: str = "schedule"):
    """Push a named event to all connected SSE clients. Safe to call from sync endpoints.

    This is also where the portal push is triggered. Hooking it here rather than at each of
    the twenty-odd mutation sites means a new mutation cannot forget to push: if it tells open
    browsers that something changed, it tells the portal too.

    Args:
        event: The event name the browsers listen for.
    """
    if event in _PORTAL_EVENTS:
        # Imported lazily so this module stays importable without the sync client, and
        # debounced on the other side, so applying a grid of forty slot edits pushes once.
        import portal_sync
        portal_sync.request_push()
    if _state.loop is None:
        return
    with _lock:
        for q in list(_subscribers):
            _state.loop.call_soon_threadsafe(q.put_nowait, event)

@router.get("/api/events")
async def sse_events():
    """SSE endpoint; each connected client receives a push whenever schedule state changes."""
    queue: asyncio.Queue = asyncio.Queue()
    with _lock:
        _subscribers.add(queue)

    async def generator():
        try:
            while True:
                event = await queue.get()
                yield {"event": event, "data": ""}
        finally:
            # Runs on disconnect too: the CancelledError that ends the stream passes through.
            with _lock:
                _subscribers.discard(queue)

    return EventSourceResponse(generator())

The read-only export API, for other servers and tools/vol_mail. Keys: api_auth.py.

Both endpoints are built from one slot query, so a volunteer's shifts and the schedule can't disagree. Shift times are given in the event timezone (App Settings) with its offset; start/end are null for a day with no date or a time that isn't a range.

Names come from names.export_name: First L., or Handle [First L.] with the parts alongside.

The response models below are the contract. docs/api/export.md (the caller's guide) is built from them by docs/gen_export_api.py, so a field's description and examples are what callers read. Field order is the JSON key order. Optional fields carry x-scope, and both routes use response_model_exclude_unset, so a field the handler didn't set (email_enc without volunteers:email) is left out, while one set to None is sent as null.

            response_model_exclude_unset=True)
def export_schedule(
    assigned: bool = Query(default=False, description="Only slots with a volunteer."),
    day: Optional[str] = Query(default=None, description="Only one day, by `day_key`, for "
                               "example `sat`. An unknown `day_key` returns an empty list, "
                               "not an error."),
    key: dict = Depends(TokenChecker("schedule:read")),

    tz = event_tz(db)
    slots = []

def volunteer_records(db: PgClient, status: str = "active", assigned: bool = False,
                      with_email: bool = False, with_codes: bool = False) -> dict:
    """The volunteers export, shared with the email template preview (routers/email_template),
    so the preview shows exactly what tools/vol_mail will be sent.

    Args:
        db: The database connection.
        status: `active` for assignable volunteers only, anything else for everyone.
        assigned: Only volunteers with at least one shift.
        with_email: Include each volunteer's `email_enc`.
        with_codes: Include each shift's `checkin_code`.

    Returns:
        The export header plus `volunteers`.
    """
    tz = event_tz(db)
    code_key = checkin_key(db) if with_codes else None

    shifts: dict = {}
    for s in _slots(db, tz):
        if not s["vol_id"]:
            continue
        s.pop("vol_name")
        vol_id = s.pop("vol_id")
        if with_codes:
            s["checkin_code"] = checkin_codes.make_code(code_key, vol_id, s["slot_key"])
        shifts.setdefault(vol_id, []).append(s)

    rows = db.execute(
        "SELECT v.vol_id, v.name, v.status, v.email_enc, "
        "(v.cancelled_at IS NOT NULL) AS cancelled, (v.inactive_at IS NOT NULL) AS inactive "
        "FROM volunteers v WHERE (? OR v.is_assignable) ORDER BY v.name, v.vol_id;",
        (status != "active",),
    ).fetchall()
    vols = []
    for r in rows:
        mine = shifts.get(r["vol_id"], [])
        if assigned and not mine:
            continue
        v = {"vol_id": r["vol_id"], **_name_fields(r["name"]), "status": r["status"],
             "cancelled": r["cancelled"], "inactive": r["inactive"], "shifts": mine}
        if with_email:
            v["email_enc"] = r["email_enc"]
        vols.append(v)
    return {**_header(db, tz), "volunteers": vols}

docs.text:
Inviting someone to create their own admin account, instead of an organizer making it.

An organizer creates an invite for a role, optionally with an email address; the link is mailed through the portal (portal_sync.send_admin_mail) and shown once to copy as well. The invitee opens /admin/invite?t=…, picks a username and password, and is signed in.

  • Only the token's hash is stored (32 random bytes, SHA-256): a copy of user_invites can't accept anything, and the link can't be shown again after creation.
  • Opening the link does nothing. GET check is read-only, because mail and chat previews fetch links; accept is a POST that consumes the token in one conditional UPDATE, inside the same transaction as the new user, so two submissions resolve to one account.
  • 72 hours, single use, revocable.

def clean_email(raw: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
    """A plausible address, lowercased, or None for blank. 400 for anything else.

    Args:
        raw: The address as typed, or `None`.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Too long, or not shaped like an address.
    """
    email = (raw or "").strip().lower()
    if not email:
        return None
    if len(email) > 254 or not EMAIL.match(email):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="That doesn't look like an email address")
    return email

@router.post("/api/invites")
async def create_invite(
    request: Request,
    role: str = Form(...),
    email: str = Form(default=""),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Create an invite, and mail it if an address is given.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, for the session id and the audit log.
        role: The new account's role: `organizer`, `checkin` or `view`.
        email: Where to mail the link. Blank means the organizer sends it by hand.
        s_data: The organizer's session.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Returns:
        dict with ``invite_id``, ``link`` (shown once; never retrievable later),
        ``expires_at``, ``emailed`` and, when mailing failed, ``email_error`` — the invite
        stands either way, so the link can be sent by hand.
    """
    if role not in ROLES:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid role")
    email = clean_email(email)
    site = portal_sync.site_origin()
    if not site:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="ADMIN_PUBLIC_URL is unset, so there's "
                            "no address to put in the link")
    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    invite_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    row = db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO user_invites (invite_id, token_hash, role, email, created_by, expires_at) "
        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' + ? * INTERVAL '1 hour') "
        "RETURNING expires_at;",
        (invite_id, token_hash(token), role, email, s_data["username"], INVITE_HOURS),
    ).fetchone()
    db.commit()
    link = f"{site}/admin/invite?t={token}"
    audit("invite.create", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Created a {role} invite {invite_id}")

    out = {"invite_id": invite_id, "link": link, "expires_at": _iso(row["expires_at"]),
           "emailed": False}
    if email:
        try:
            await portal_sync.send_admin_mail(
                "invite", email, link, role=role, inviter=s_data["username"],
                app_title=get_app_kv(db, "app_title") or "the conference",
                hours=INVITE_HOURS)
            out["emailed"] = True
        # Deliberately broad: a failed mail mustn't undo the invite. The link is still
        # usable. The organizer is told it didn't send; the reason (which can carry the
        # portal's reply) goes to the server log, not the page (CodeQL #7).
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
            logging.getLogger(__name__).warning("invite %s: mail not sent: %s", invite_id, exc)
            out["email_error"] = ("The invite was created, but the email couldn't be sent. "
                                  "Copy the link and send it yourself; Admin → Volunteer "
                                  "Portal shows any mail problems.")
    return out

@router.post("/api/invites/accept")
def accept_invite(
    request: Request,
    t: str = Form(...),
    username: str = Form(...),
    password: str = Form(...),
    email: str = Form(default=""),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Create the invited account and sign it in.

    Everything is checked before the token is spent, so a taken username or short password
    leaves the link usable; the consume and the insert commit together.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, for the new session and the audit log.
        t: The token from the link.
        username: The new account's username.
        password: The new account's password, at least 8 characters.
        email: An optional address for password resets.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Returns:
        dict with ``username`` and ``role``, as POST /api/login.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Expired, used or revoked link; bad username, password or email.
        HTTPException 409: Username taken.
    """
    username = username.lower().strip()
    if not re.match(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{1,31}$", username):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Username: 2-32 letters, digits, dots, "
                            "dashes or underscores")
    if len(password) < 8:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Password must be at least 8 characters")
    email = clean_email(email)
    if db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE username = ?;", (username,)).fetchone():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=f"Username '{username}' is taken")

    user_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    invite = db.execute(
        "UPDATE user_invites SET used_at = NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', used_by = ?, email = NULL "
        "WHERE token_hash = ? AND used_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL "
        "AND expires_at > NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' RETURNING invite_id, role;",
        (username, token_hash(t))).fetchone()
    if not invite:
        db.commit()
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="This invite link has expired, was "
                            "already used, or was revoked. Ask an organizer for a new one.")
    try:
        db.execute("INSERT INTO users (user_id, username, password_hash, role, email) "
                   "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?);",
                   (user_id, username, PasswordHasher().hash(password), invite["role"], email))
    except Exception:
        # Someone took the username in the moment since the check; the invite isn't spent.
        db._conn.rollback()
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=f"Username '{username}' is taken") from None
    # start_session commits, so the consume, the new user and the session land together.
    result = start_session(request, db, {"user_id": user_id, "username": username,
                                         "role": invite["role"]})
    audit("invite.accept", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Accepted invite {invite['invite_id']} as {invite['role']}",
          invite_id=invite["invite_id"], role=invite["role"])
    return result

docs.title: backend.routers.passkeys
docs.text:
Passkeys (WebAuthn) for organizer accounts — an alternative to the password.

Passwords keep working; a passkey is a second way in. Three properties this file exists to keep:

  • Nothing stored here can sign anyone in. The server holds public keys, which only check signatures, and challenges, stored as SHA-256.
  • Each challenge verifies once. It's consumed by one conditional UPDATE before the response is checked, so two submissions of the same response resolve by rowcount and a captured response can't be replayed.
  • Adding a passkey needs the password again. A stolen session cookie must not be enough to plant a permanent way back in.

The relying party is the organizer site's origin: ADMIN_PUBLIC_URL, or PORTAL_PUBLIC_URL when the two are served from one origin (local dev). Passkeys are bound to that hostname for good: change it and every passkey stops working, though passwords still do.
