@router.post("/api/schedule/build")
def build_schedule_structure(
    request: Request,
    config: str = Form(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Create a whole schedule — days, times, categories, positions and slots — in one write.

    Backs the setup wizard's schedule builder. The counts grid is what the flat
    ``bulk_add_slots`` cross-product cannot express: a category may need ten registration
    desks at one timeslot and four at the next, so each (day, time) cell carries its own
    count and gets slots for the first N positions of that category.

    Everything is inserted with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING under a single commit, so a re-run
    adds what is missing and leaves existing rows — including any volunteer assignments —
    untouched.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        config: JSON object as a form field (the API takes no JSON request bodies) with keys:

            ``days``: list of ``{"key", "title", "date"}`` — date is ISO ``YYYY-MM-DD`` or "".
            ``times``: list of ``{"key", "title", "day_keys": [...]}`` — day_keys declares
                which days run that time. Two days running different-length shifts from the
                same start are two entries with different keys.
            ``categories``: list of ``{"name", "prefix", "label", "names", "counts", "color"}``
                in display order. ``names`` (optional) makes the category named rather than
                numbered. ``counts`` maps ``"{day_key}|{time_key}"`` to how many of that
                category's positions are scheduled in that cell; 0 or absent means none.
                ``color`` (optional) is the ``#rrggbb`` chip color; omitted, a new category
                takes the next default and an existing one keeps the color it has.

        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer role.
        db: Injected PgClient from get_db().

    Returns:
        dict with keys ``days``, ``times``, ``categories``, ``positions_created``,
        ``slots_created``.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Malformed JSON, a missing or duplicate key, a key with characters
            that would break slot parsing, a count referencing an undeclared day/time pair,
            or any list exceeding its size cap.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    try:
        cfg = json.loads(config)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="config must be a JSON object") from None
    if not isinstance(cfg, dict):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="config must be a JSON object")

    days  = cfg.get("days")       or []
    times = cfg.get("times")      or []
    cats  = cfg.get("categories") or []
    if not days:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="At least one day is required")
    if not times:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="At least one time is required")
    for label, seq, cap in (("days", days, BUILD_MAX_DAYS), ("times", times, BUILD_MAX_TIMES),
                            ("categories", cats, BUILD_MAX_CATEGORIES)):
        if len(seq) > cap:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Too many {label} (max {cap})")

    # ── days ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    day_keys = []
    for i, d in enumerate(days):
        key   = str(d.get("key") or "").strip().lower()
        title = str(d.get("title") or "").strip()
        date  = str(d.get("date") or "").strip() or None
        if not key or not title:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Day {i + 1} needs a key and a title")
        _validate_key(key, "day_key")
        if key in day_keys:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Duplicate day key {key!r}")
        day_keys.append(key)
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO days_table (day_key, day_str, event_date) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
            "ON CONFLICT (day_key) DO NOTHING;",
            (key, title, date),
        )

    # ── times, and the day/time pairs they run ────────────────────────────────
    pairs = set()
    time_keys = []
    for i, t in enumerate(times):
        key   = str(t.get("key") or "").strip()
        title = str(t.get("title") or "").strip()
        if not key or not title:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Time {i + 1} needs a key and a title")
        _validate_key(key, "time_key")
        if key in time_keys:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Duplicate time key {key!r}")
        time_keys.append(key)
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO times_table (time_key, time_str) VALUES (?, ?) "
            "ON CONFLICT (time_key) DO NOTHING;",
            (key, title),
        )
        for dk in (t.get("day_keys") or []):
            dk = str(dk).strip().lower()
            if dk not in day_keys:
                raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Time {key!r} names unknown day {dk!r}")
            pairs.add((dk, key))
            db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO day_times (day_key, time_key) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;",
                (dk, key),
            )

    # ── categories, positions, slots ──────────────────────────────────────────
    positions_created = 0
    slots_created     = 0

    for idx, cat in enumerate(cats):
        name  = str(cat.get("name") or "").strip()
        color = _norm_color(cat.get("color") or "", f"category {name!r} color")
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO categories (cat_name, sort_order, cat_color) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
            "ON CONFLICT (cat_name) DO UPDATE SET sort_order = excluded.sort_order, "
            "cat_color = COALESCE(?, categories.cat_color);",
            (name, idx, color or _DEFAULT_CAT_COLORS[idx % len(_DEFAULT_CAT_COLORS)], color),
        )

        prefix, labels = _build_labels(cat, idx)
        pos_keys = [f"{prefix}{n}" for n in range(1, len(labels) + 1)]
        for pos_key, pos_str in zip(pos_keys, labels):
            cur = db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO positions (pos_key, pos_cat, pos_str) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
                "ON CONFLICT (pos_key) DO NOTHING;",
                (pos_key, name, pos_str),
            )
            positions_created += cur.rowcount

        for cell, raw in (cat.get("counts") or {}).items():
            try:
                count = int(raw)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                raise HTTPException(
                    status_code=400,
                    detail=f"Category {name!r} has a non-numeric count at {cell!r}") from None
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            dk, _, tk = str(cell).partition("|")
            if (dk, tk) not in pairs:
                raise HTTPException(
                    status_code=400,
                    detail=f"Category {name!r} schedules {cell!r}, which is not a declared day/time",
                )
            # A cell may ask for more than the category defines (a named list is finite);
            # take what exists rather than failing the whole build.
            slots_created += _fill_slots(db, [(dk, tk)], pos_keys[:count])

    db.commit()
    broadcast("schedule")
    audit("schedule.structure", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Built schedule: {len(day_keys)} day(s), {len(time_keys)} time(s), "
          f"{len(cats)} categor(ies), {positions_created} position(s), {slots_created} slot(s)")
    return {
        "days":              len(day_keys),
        "times":             len(time_keys),
        "categories":        len(cats),
        "positions_created": positions_created,
        "slots_created":     slots_created,
    }

docs.text:
Reconcile the live schedule against a counts grid: add what is missing, remove the surplus.

This is the editor's counterpart to /api/schedule/build. Build is additive and runs against an empty database; this one diffs against a schedule that already has volunteers in it, so it can also take slots away.

Assignments are never discarded. Lowering a count removes only unassigned slots, highest-numbered position first; a slot with a volunteer is left alone and reported in blocked. This matches set_day_time and remove_slot, which refuse rather than drop an assignment.

Positions are matched to counts by how many, not by which: raising a cell from 2 to 4 schedules the two lowest-numbered positions of that category not already there, rather than forcing the cell to hold exactly positions 1-4. That leaves existing assignments where they are instead of churning them.

Display names are only written for positions this call creates, except in a named category, where the supplied list is the point and is applied to positions 1…len(names). A numbered category never renames a position that already exists, so a hand-edited pos_str survives.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default request Request

Starlette Request; used for audit logging.

required config str

JSON object as a form field (the API takes no JSON request bodies) with keys:

cells: list of "{day_key}|{time_key}" — every cell the grid displayed. Reconciliation is confined to these, so a stale grid cannot clear a cell it never showed. @router.post("/api/schedule/apply_grid")
def apply_grid(
    request: Request,
    config: str = Form(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Reconcile the live schedule against a counts grid: add what is missing, remove the surplus.

    This is the editor's counterpart to ``/api/schedule/build``. Build is additive and runs
    against an empty database; this one diffs against a schedule that already has volunteers
    in it, so it can also take slots away.

    **Assignments are never discarded.** Lowering a count removes only unassigned slots,
    highest-numbered position first; a slot with a volunteer is left alone and reported in
    ``blocked``. This matches ``set_day_time`` and ``remove_slot``, which refuse rather than
    drop an assignment.

    Positions are matched to counts by *how many*, not by which: raising a cell from 2 to 4
    schedules the two lowest-numbered positions of that category not already there, rather
    than forcing the cell to hold exactly positions 1-4. That leaves existing assignments
    where they are instead of churning them.

    Display names are only written for positions this call creates, except in a *named*
    category, where the supplied list is the point and is applied to positions 1…len(names).
    A numbered category never renames a position that already exists, so a hand-edited
    ``pos_str`` survives.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        config: JSON object as a form field (the API takes no JSON request bodies) with keys:

            ``cells``: list of ``"{day_key}|{time_key}"`` — every cell the grid displayed.
                Reconciliation is confined to these, so a stale grid cannot clear a cell it
                never showed. Each must be a pair declared in ``day_times``.
            ``categories``: list of ``{"name", "mode", "names", "counts"}``. ``mode`` is
                ``"numbered"`` (default) or ``"named"``; ``names`` is the display-name list
                for a named category. ``counts`` maps a cell key to how many of that
                category's positions belong there; a listed cell missing from ``counts``
                means zero.

        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer role.
        db: Injected PgClient from get_db().

    Returns:
        dict with ``ok``, ``positions_created``, ``positions_deleted``, ``slots_created``,
        ``slots_removed``, and ``blocked`` — a list of
        ``{"category", "cell", "kept"}`` for cells that could not shrink all the way.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Malformed JSON, an unknown category, a cell that is not a declared
            day/time pair, a non-numeric or out-of-range count.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    try:
        cfg = json.loads(config)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="config must be a JSON object") from None
    if not isinstance(cfg, dict):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="config must be a JSON object")

    cells = cfg.get("cells") or []
    cats  = cfg.get("categories") or []
    if len(cats) > BUILD_MAX_CATEGORIES:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Too many categories (max {BUILD_MAX_CATEGORIES})")

    # Confine every write to cells the grid actually displayed, and only real day/time pairs.
    pairs = set(_day_time_pairs(db))
    grid_cells = []
    for cell in cells:
        dk, _, tk = str(cell).partition("|")
        if (dk, tk) not in pairs:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"{cell!r} is not a declared day/time")
        grid_cells.append((dk, tk))
    if not grid_cells:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="No cells to apply")

    known_cats = {r["cat_name"] for r in db.execute("SELECT cat_name FROM categories;").fetchall()}
    all_keys   = set(_all_keys(db, "positions", "pos_key"))

    positions_created = positions_deleted = 0
    slots_created     = slots_removed     = 0
    blocked           = []

    for cat in cats:
        name = str(cat.get("name") or "").strip()
        if name not in known_cats:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Unknown category {name!r}")

        raw_counts = cat.get("counts") or {}
        counts     = {}
        for (dk, tk) in grid_cells:
            try:
                n = int(raw_counts.get(f"{dk}|{tk}", 0) or 0)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                raise HTTPException(
                    status_code=400,
                    detail=f"Category {name!r} has a non-numeric count at {dk}|{tk}") from None
            if n < 0 or n > GRID_MAX_PER_CELL:
                raise HTTPException(
                    status_code=400,
                    detail=f"Category {name!r} count at {dk}|{tk} must be 0…{GRID_MAX_PER_CELL}")
            counts[(dk, tk)] = n

        rows    = _cat_positions(db, name)
        ordered = [r["pos_key"] for r in rows]
        labels  = {r["pos_key"]: r["pos_str"] for r in rows}
        prefix  = _infer_prefix(ordered, name)

        named = str(cat.get("mode") or "numbered") == "named"
        names = [str(n).strip() for n in (cat.get("names") or []) if str(n).strip()] if named else []
        if named and not names:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Category {name!r} is named but has no names")

        # How many positions this category must be able to offer.
        needed = len(names) if named else max(counts.values(), default=0)
        if needed > BUILD_MAX_POSITIONS:
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=400,
                detail=f"Category {name!r} needs {needed} positions (max {BUILD_MAX_POSITIONS})")

        # ── grow the position list to fit ────────────────────────────────────
        next_n = len(ordered) + 1
        while len(ordered) < needed:
            key, next_n = _new_pos_key(prefix, next_n, all_keys)
            label = names[len(ordered)] if named else f"{name} {len(ordered) + 1}"
            db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO positions (pos_key, pos_cat, pos_str) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
                "ON CONFLICT (pos_key) DO NOTHING;",
                (key, name, label),
            )
            all_keys.add(key)
            ordered.append(key)
            labels[key] = label
            positions_created += 1
            next_n += 1

        # A named list is the point of naming — apply it. A numbered category leaves
        # existing display names alone, so a hand-edited one is not overwritten.
        if named:
            for i, label in enumerate(names):
                key = ordered[i]
                if labels.get(key) != label:
                    db.execute("UPDATE positions SET pos_str = ? WHERE pos_key = ?;", (label, key))

        # ── reconcile each cell ──────────────────────────────────────────────
        placed = {}
        for r in db.execute(
            "SELECT s.day_key, s.time_key, s.pos_key, s.vol_id FROM schedule s "
            "JOIN positions p ON s.pos_key = p.pos_key WHERE p.pos_cat = ?;",
            (name,),
        ).fetchall():
            placed.setdefault((r["day_key"], r["time_key"]), {})[r["pos_key"]] = r["vol_id"]

        for (dk, tk) in grid_cells:
            here = placed.get((dk, tk), {})
            to_add, to_remove, short = _reconcile_cell(ordered, here, counts[(dk, tk)])

            for key in to_add:
                db.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO schedule (day_key, time_key, pos_key) VALUES (?, ?, ?) "
                    "ON CONFLICT (day_key, time_key, pos_key) DO NOTHING;",
                    (dk, tk, key),
                )
                slots_created += 1

            for key in to_remove:
                db.execute(
                    "DELETE FROM schedule WHERE day_key = ? AND time_key = ? AND pos_key = ?;",
                    (dk, tk, key),
                )
                db.execute(
                    "DELETE FROM schedule_notes WHERE day_key = ? AND time_key = ? AND pos_key = ?;",
                    (dk, tk, key),
                )
                slots_removed += 1

            if short:
                blocked.append({"category": name, "cell": f"{dk}|{tk}", "kept": short})

        # ── tidy positions the grid no longer needs ──────────────────────────
        # Only ones left with no slots anywhere: invisible either way, and recreating one
        # is a keystroke. Anything still scheduled, or assigned, is left alone.
        for key in ordered[needed:]:
            if db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM schedule WHERE pos_key = ?;", (key,)).fetchone():
                continue
            db.execute("DELETE FROM schedule_notes WHERE pos_key = ?;", (key,))
            db.execute("DELETE FROM positions WHERE pos_key = ?;", (key,))
            positions_deleted += 1

    db.commit()
    broadcast("schedule")
    audit("schedule.structure", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Applied grid: +{slots_created}/-{slots_removed} slot(s), "
          f"+{positions_created}/-{positions_deleted} position(s), {len(blocked)} blocked")
    return {
        "ok":                True,
        "positions_created": positions_created,
        "positions_deleted": positions_deleted,
        "slots_created":     slots_created,
        "slots_removed":     slots_removed,
        "blocked":           blocked,
    }

docs.text:
First-run setup and App Settings.

On a fresh database the setup wizard creates the first organizer (setup/create_admin, refused once any user exists), then imports or builds the schedule and imports the volunteer roster from CSV. The CSV imports are safe to run again: each row is in its own savepoint, so a bad row is reported and skipped while the rest are kept.

App Settings live here too: the site title, the event timezone, and the two logos, which are stored as data URLs in app_kv and pushed to the portal for the volunteer pages.

@router.get("/api/setup_status")
def setup_status(
    request: Request,
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Return the current setup wizard state and the authenticated user's identity.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; session cookie checked to determine auth state.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        dict with keys ``has_users``, ``has_title``, ``has_schedule``, ``has_volunteers``
        (booleans), ``authenticated`` (bool), ``username`` (str or None), ``role`` (str or None).
    """
    has_users      = bool(db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM users LIMIT 1;").fetchone())
    has_title      = bool(db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM app_kv WHERE app_key = 'app_title';").fetchone())
    has_schedule   = bool(db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM schedule LIMIT 1;").fetchone())
    has_volunteers = bool(db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM volunteers LIMIT 1;").fetchone())
    s_id           = request.session.get("session_id")
    s_data         = _session_cache.get(s_id) if s_id else None
    if s_data is None and s_id:
        row = db.execute(
            "SELECT s.user_id, u.username, u.role FROM sessions s "
            "LEFT JOIN users u ON s.user_id = u.user_id WHERE s.session_id = ?;",
            (s_id,)
        ).fetchone()
        if row:
            s_data = {"user_id": row["user_id"], "username": row["username"],
                      "role": row["role"] or "organizer"}
            _session_cache[s_id] = s_data
    return {
        "has_users":      has_users,
        "has_title":      has_title,
        "has_schedule":   has_schedule,
        "has_volunteers": has_volunteers,
        "authenticated":  s_data is not None,
        "username":       s_data["username"] if s_data else None,
        "role":           s_data["role"]     if s_data else None,
    }

@router.post("/api/setup/create_admin")
def setup_create_admin(
    request: Request,
    username: str = Form(...),
    password: str = Form(...),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Create the first organizer account; rejects with 403 once any user exists.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, for the audit log.
        username: Desired admin username; lowercased and stripped before storage.
        password: Plaintext password; must be at least 8 characters.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        dict with keys ``username`` and ``role`` (always ``"organizer"``).

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Password shorter than 8 characters.
        HTTPException 403: A user account already exists.
    """
    from argon2 import PasswordHasher
    if db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM users LIMIT 1;").fetchone():
        audit("setup.create_admin.refused", request, None,
              "First-admin setup called after setup was complete", username=username)
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Setup already complete — admin already exists")
    if len(password) < 8:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Password must be at least 8 characters")

    user_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    ph      = PasswordHasher()
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO users (user_id, username, password_hash, role, audit_alerts) "
        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'organizer', TRUE);",
        (user_id, username.lower().strip(), ph.hash(password))
    )
    db.commit()
    audit("setup.create_admin", request, None, "Created the first admin account",
          who=username.lower().strip(), user_id=user_id)
    return {"username": username.lower().strip(), "role": "organizer"}

@router.post("/api/setup/import_schedule")
def setup_import_schedule(
    request: Request,
    file: UploadFile = File(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Import schedule slots from CSV; every insert is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so re-importing is safe.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        file: UTF-8 CSV with required columns ``day_key``, ``day_str``, ``time_key``,
              ``time_str``, ``pos_key``, ``pos_cat``, ``pos_str``; optional column ``date``
              (ISO ``YYYY-MM-DD``) stored as ``event_date`` in days_table.
        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer role.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        dict with keys ``inserted_slots``, ``days``, ``times``, ``positions``,
        ``skipped``, and ``errors`` (list of per-row error messages).

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: File is not UTF-8, or required CSV columns are missing.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    content = file.file.read()
    try:
        text = content.decode("utf-8-sig")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="File must be UTF-8 encoded") from None

    reader   = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text))
    required = {"day_key", "day_str", "time_key", "time_str", "pos_key", "pos_cat", "pos_str"}
    if not required.issubset(set(reader.fieldnames or [])):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="CSV must have columns: day_key, day_str, time_key, time_str, pos_key, pos_cat, pos_str"
        )

    inserted  = 0
    skipped   = 0
    errors    = []
    seen_days = {}
    seen_times = {}
    seen_pos   = {}

    for row_num, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
        day_key    = (row.get("day_key")  or "").strip()
        day_str    = (row.get("day_str")  or "").strip()
        time_key   = (row.get("time_key") or "").strip()
        time_str   = (row.get("time_str") or "").strip()
        pos_key    = (row.get("pos_key")  or "").strip()
        pos_cat    = (row.get("pos_cat")  or "").strip()
        pos_str    = (row.get("pos_str")  or "").strip()
        event_date = (row.get("date")     or "").strip() or None

        if not all([day_key, day_str, time_key, time_str, pos_key, pos_cat, pos_str]):
            errors.append(f"Row {row_num}: missing required field — skipped")
            skipped += 1
            continue

        try:
            with _row_savepoint(db):
                if day_key not in seen_days:
                    db.execute("INSERT INTO days_table VALUES (?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (day_key) DO NOTHING;", (day_key, day_str, event_date))
                if time_key not in seen_times:
                    db.execute("INSERT INTO times_table VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT (time_key) DO NOTHING;", (time_key, time_str))
                if pos_key not in seen_pos:
                    db.execute("INSERT INTO positions VALUES (?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (pos_key) DO UPDATE SET pos_cat = EXCLUDED.pos_cat, pos_str = EXCLUDED.pos_str;", (pos_key, pos_cat, pos_str))
                db.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO day_times (day_key, time_key) VALUES (?, ?) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;",
                    (day_key, time_key)
                )
                db.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO schedule (day_key, time_key, pos_key) VALUES (?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (day_key, time_key, pos_key) DO NOTHING;",
                    (day_key, time_key, pos_key)
                )
        except psycopg2.Error as e:
            errors.append(f"Row {row_num} ({day_key}/{time_key}/{pos_key}): "
                          f"{_row_problem(e, f'schedule row {row_num}')}")
            skipped += 1
            continue
        # Only once the row is saved: a rolled-back row's day must still be inserted by the
        # next row that uses it.
        seen_days.setdefault(day_key, day_str)
        seen_times.setdefault(time_key, time_str)
        seen_pos.setdefault(pos_key, (pos_cat, pos_str))
        inserted += 1

    db.commit()
    audit("setup.import_schedule", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Imported schedule: {inserted} slots, {len(seen_days)} days, "
          f"{len(seen_times)} times, {len(seen_pos)} positions ({skipped} skipped).")
    return {
        "inserted_slots": inserted,
        "days":           len(seen_days),
        "times":          len(seen_times),
        "positions":      len(seen_pos),
        "skipped":        skipped,
        "errors":         errors,
    }

@router.post("/api/setup/import_volunteers")
def setup_import_volunteers(
    request: Request,
    file: UploadFile = File(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Import volunteers from CSV; re-importing updates the imported columns of existing records.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        file: UTF-8 CSV with required columns ``vol_id``, ``first_name``, ``last_name``;
              optional columns ``nickname``, ``time_pref``, ``add_time``.
        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer role.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        dict with keys ``inserted``, ``skipped``, and ``errors`` (list of per-row messages).

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: File is not UTF-8, or required CSV columns are missing.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    content = file.file.read()
    try:
        text = content.decode("utf-8-sig")
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="File must be UTF-8 encoded") from None

    reader   = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text))
    required = {"vol_id", "first_name", "last_name"}
    if not required.issubset(set(reader.fieldnames or [])):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail=f"CSV must have columns: vol_id, first_name, last_name, nickname, time_pref, add_time"
        )

    inserted = 0
    skipped  = 0
    errors   = []

    for row_num, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
        vol_id     = (row.get("vol_id")     or "").strip()
        first_name = (row.get("first_name") or "").strip()
        last_name  = (row.get("last_name")  or "").strip()
        nickname   = (row.get("nickname")   or "").strip()
        time_pref  = (row.get("time_pref")  or "").strip()
        add_time   = (row.get("add_time")   or "").strip()

        if not vol_id or not first_name or not last_name:
            errors.append(f"Row {row_num}: missing vol_id, first_name, or last_name — skipped")
            skipped += 1
            continue

        vol_name = f"{first_name} {last_name[0]}."
        if nickname:
            vol_name += f" ({nickname})"

        try:
            # Re-importing updates the imported columns only. (This was SQLite's INSERT OR
            # REPLACE, a syntax error on Postgres; it would also have deleted the row and lost
            # every column the CSV doesn't carry.)
            with _row_savepoint(db):
                db.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO volunteers (vol_id, name, time_pref, add_time) "
                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT (vol_id) DO UPDATE SET "
                    "name = EXCLUDED.name, time_pref = EXCLUDED.time_pref, "
                    "add_time = EXCLUDED.add_time;",
                    (vol_id, vol_name, time_pref, add_time)
                )
            inserted += 1
        except psycopg2.Error as e:
            errors.append(f"Row {row_num} (id={vol_id}): "
                          f"{_row_problem(e, f'volunteer row {row_num}')}")
            skipped += 1

    db.commit()
    audit("setup.import_volunteers", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Imported {inserted} volunteers via CSV ({skipped} skipped).")
    return {"inserted": inserted, "skipped": skipped, "errors": errors}

def clean_public_link(raw: Optional[str], what: str) -> str:
    """Check a link the volunteer pages will show.

    Only ``http(s)`` links with a host pass. Anything else, a ``javascript:`` URL above all,
    would run script on a public page when clicked.

    Args:
        raw: What the organizer typed. Surrounding whitespace is ignored.
        what: The field's name, for the error message.

    Returns:
        The link, or ``""`` for blank.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Not an http(s) link with a host, contains whitespace, or too long.
    """
    link = (raw or "").strip()
    if not link:
        return ""
    parts = urlsplit(link)
    if (len(link) > MAX_CONFERENCE_FIELD or parts.scheme not in ("http", "https")
            or not parts.netloc or any(c.isspace() for c in link)):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400,
                            detail=f"The {what} must be a web address starting with https://")
    return link

@router.post("/api/setup/set_title")
def setup_set_title(
    request: Request,
    title: str = Form(...),
    with_contact: bool = Form(default=False),
    contact_email: Optional[str] = Form(default=None),
    conference_url: Optional[str] = Form(default=None),
    code_of_conduct_url: Optional[str] = Form(default=None),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Store the conference's title, and optionally its public contact address and links.

    The setup wizard and App Settings both use this. With ``with_contact`` set, the three
    conference fields are all taken as sent, and a blank or missing one is removed, so the
    volunteer pages leave that line out. Without it (the wizard's Skip) they keep their stored
    values. A flag rather than "missing means unchanged", because FastAPI reads an empty form
    field as missing. Everything is checked before anything is stored.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        title: Display title for the application; must be non-empty.
        with_contact: Replace the three conference fields with what this request sends.
        contact_email: The address the volunteer pages give for questions.
        conference_url: The conference's website, linked from the volunteer pages.
        code_of_conduct_url: The code of conduct, linked from the volunteer pages.
        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer role.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        dict with keys ``ok``, ``title`` and each conference field as now stored.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: title is blank, or a conference field fails its check.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    title = title.strip()
    if not title:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Title is required")
    given: dict[str, str] = {}
    if with_contact:
        given = {"contact_email": clean_contact_email(contact_email),
                 "conference_url": clean_public_link(conference_url, "website"),
                 "code_of_conduct_url": clean_public_link(code_of_conduct_url,
                                                          "code of conduct link")}
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO app_kv (app_key, val) VALUES ('app_title', ?) "
        "ON CONFLICT(app_key) DO UPDATE SET val = excluded.val;",
        (title,)
    )
    for key, value in given.items():
        if value:
            db.execute("INSERT INTO app_kv (app_key, val) VALUES (?, ?) "
                       "ON CONFLICT(app_key) DO UPDATE SET val = excluded.val;", (key, value))
        else:
            db.execute("DELETE FROM app_kv WHERE app_key = ?;", (key,))
    db.commit()
    changed = ", ".join(given)
    audit("settings.change", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Set app title to {title!r}" + (f" and {changed}" if changed else ""))
    _queue_branding_push()
    stored = {r["app_key"]: r["val"] for r in db.execute(
        "SELECT app_key, val FROM app_kv WHERE app_key = ANY(?::text[]);",
        (list(CONFERENCE_FIELDS),)).fetchall()}
    return {"ok": True, "title": title, **{k: stored.get(k, "") for k in CONFERENCE_FIELDS}}

@router.post("/api/app_logo")
def set_app_logo(
    request: Request,
    logo:    Optional[UploadFile] = File(default=None),
    favicon: str = Form(default=""),
    remove:  bool = Form(default=False),
    s_data:  dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db:      PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Store or remove the year's theme logo and its auto-generated 32x32 favicon.

    The theme logo is the conference's primary one: the favicon is made from it, and the
    volunteer pages show it large on the landing page and faintly behind every page. The
    smaller logo in their upper left is the header logo (``set_header_logo``).

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        logo: The image file, up to MAX_LOGO_BYTES. Stored as a data URL.
        favicon: 32x32 PNG as a base64 data URL drawn from the logo in the browser.
        remove: True removes the logo and favicon; ``logo`` is then ignored.

        HTTPException 413: Logo over 2 MB.

    if remove:
        db.execute("DELETE FROM app_kv WHERE app_key IN ('app_logo', 'app_favicon');")
    else:
        url = _logo_data_url(logo)
        if favicon and (not favicon.startswith("data:image/png;base64,")
                        or len(favicon) > MAX_FAVICON_CHARS):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="The favicon must be a small PNG")
        for key, val in [("app_logo", url), ("app_favicon", favicon)]:
            db.execute(
                "INSERT INTO app_kv (app_key, val) VALUES (?, ?) "
                "ON CONFLICT(app_key) DO UPDATE SET val = excluded.val;",
                (key, val)
            )
    db.commit()
    audit("settings.change", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          "Removed app logo" if remove else "Updated app logo and favicon")
    _queue_branding_push()
    return {"ok": True}

@router.post("/api/users/add")
def add_user(
    request: Request,
    username: str = Form(...),
    password: str = Form(...),
    role:     str = Form(default="view"),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Create a new user account.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        username: Desired username; lowercased and stripped before storage.
        password: Plaintext password; must be at least 8 characters.
        role: One of ``"organizer"``, ``"checkin"``, ``"view"``; defaults to ``"view"``.
        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer role.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        HTTP 201 with the new user dict: ``user_id``, ``username``, ``role``,
        ``created_at``, ``last_login_at``, ``failed_login_cnt``, ``passkey_count``.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: Password too short, username blank, or invalid role.
        HTTPException 409: Username already exists.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    username = username.lower().strip()
    if not username or not password:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Username and password are required")
    if len(password) < 8:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Password must be at least 8 characters")
    if role not in ("organizer", "checkin", "view"):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid role")
    if db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE username = ?;", (username,)).fetchone():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=f"Username '{username}' already exists")
    user_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    ph = PasswordHasher()
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO users (user_id, username, password_hash, role) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?);",
        (user_id, username, ph.hash(password), role)
    )
    db.commit()
    audit("user.create", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Added user {username!r} with role {role!r}", target=username, role=role)
    return JSONResponse(status_code=201, content=jsonable_encoder(db.execute(
        _GET_USER_SQL, (user_id,)
    ).fetchone()))

def set_user_role(
    request: Request,
    user_id: str = Form(...),
    role:    str = Form(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Change a user's role; self-modification is blocked to prevent accidental lockout.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        user_id: UUID of the user to update.

        HTTPException 404: User not found.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    if user_id == s_data["user_id"]:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Cannot change your own role")
    if role not in ("organizer", "checkin", "view"):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Invalid role")
    if not db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM users WHERE user_id = ?;", (user_id,)).fetchone():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
    db.execute(_SET_ROLE_SQL, (role, role, user_id))
    db.commit()
    audit("user.role_change", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Set role of {user_id!r} to {role!r}", target_user_id=user_id, role=role)
    return {"ok": True}

def change_own_password(
    request: Request,
    current_password: str = Form(...),
    new_password: str = Form(...),
    s_data: Optional[dict] = Depends(get_session_data),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Change the signed-in user's own password. Any role. Backs the Profile dialog.

    Requires the current password, so a borrowed session can't lock the owner out. Bumps
    password_version, as set_password does.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, for the session id and the audit log.
        current_password: Their current password.
        new_password: The new one, at least 8 characters.
        s_data: The caller's session, or `None` when signed out.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: New password shorter than 8 characters.
        HTTPException 401: Not signed in.
        HTTPException 403: Current password incorrect.
    """
    if not s_data:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Unauthorized")
    row = db.execute("SELECT password_hash FROM users WHERE user_id = ?;",
                     (s_data["user_id"],)).fetchone()
    if not row:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Unauthorized")
    ph = PasswordHasher()
    try:
        ph.verify(row["password_hash"], current_password)
    except (VerificationError, InvalidHashError):
        audit("password.change.fail", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
              "Password change refused: wrong current password")
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Current password is incorrect") from None
    if len(new_password) < 8:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Password must be at least 8 characters")
    db.execute(
        "UPDATE users SET password_hash = ?, password_version = password_version + 1, "
        "updated_at = NOW(), failed_login_cnt = 0 WHERE user_id = ?;",
        (ph.hash(new_password), s_data["user_id"]))
    db.commit()
    audit("password.change", request, request.session.get("session_id"), "Changed own password")
    return {"ok": True}

@router.post("/api/users/set_audit_alerts")
def set_audit_alerts(
    request: Request,
    user_id: str = Form(...),
    enabled: str = Form(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Turn security alert emails on or off for an organizer (alerts.py sends them).

    Any organizer may change anyone's. Only organizers can have them on; it may be nobody,
    and the Audit Log then says so in red. Every change is audited, and raises an alert.

    Args:
        request: The request, for the audit log.
        user_id: The user to change.
        enabled: `1` to send them alerts, `0` to stop.
        s_data: The caller's session; organizers only.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Returns:
        `{"ok": True, "audit_alerts": bool}`.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: `enabled` isn't 0 or 1, or turning alerts on for a non-organizer.
        HTTPException 404: No such user.
    """
    if enabled not in ("0", "1"):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="enabled must be 0 or 1")
    target = db.execute("SELECT username, role FROM users WHERE user_id = ?;",
                        (user_id,)).fetchone()
    if not target:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="User not found")
    if enabled == "1" and target["role"] != "organizer":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400,
                            detail="Only organizers can get security alerts.")
    db.execute("UPDATE users SET audit_alerts = ?, updated_at = NOW() WHERE user_id = ?;",
               (enabled == "1", user_id))
    db.commit()
    who = "themselves" if user_id == s_data["user_id"] else repr(target["username"])
    audit("user.audit_alerts", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Turned security alerts {'on' if enabled == '1' else 'off'} for {who}",
          target=target["username"], target_user_id=user_id, enabled=enabled == "1")
    return {"ok": True, "audit_alerts": enabled == "1"}

@router.post("/api/add_vol")
def add_vol(
    request: Request,
    vol_id: str = Form(...),
    first_name: str = Form(...),
    last_name: str = Form(...),
    nickname: str = Form(default=""),
    time_pref: str = Form(default=""),
    add_time: str = Form(default=""),
    email_enc: str = Form(default=""),
    email: str = Form(default=""),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Add a new volunteer record.

    The address arrives twice: encrypted in the browser (``email_enc``, the only form stored)
    and plain (``email``), solely so ``email_hmac`` can be computed here, as the portal does at
    signup. The HMAC key is in this process's environment, so the browser can't do it. The plain
    address is never stored or logged. Without EMAIL_HMAC_KEY the volunteer is still added,
    unindexed, and ``email_indexed`` says so.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        vol_id: Unique volunteer identifier (e.g. a badge number).
        first_name: Volunteer's first name.
        last_name: Volunteer's last name; only the initial is stored in the display name.
        nickname: Optional handle appended to display name as ``(nickname)``.
        time_pref: Semicolon-delimited preferred shift strings.
        add_time: Availability notes.
        email_enc: RSA-OAEP ciphertext of the volunteer's email (base64); empty → NULL.
        email: The same address in plain text, for email_hmac only; ignored without email_enc.
        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer role.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        HTTP 201 with a volunteer dict: ``key``, ``name``, ``requested``, ``additional``,
        ``sched_list``, ``slot_count``, ``email_indexed``.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: vol_id, first_name, or last_name is blank.
        HTTPException 409: vol_id already exists, or the address already belongs to someone.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    vol_id     = vol_id.strip()
    first_name = first_name.strip()
    last_name  = last_name.strip()
    nickname   = nickname.strip()
    email_enc  = email_enc.strip() or None

    if not vol_id or not first_name or not last_name:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Volunteer ID, first name, and last name are required")

    if db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM volunteers WHERE vol_id = ?;", (vol_id,)).fetchone():
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail=f"Volunteer ID '{vol_id}' already exists")

    addr_hash = email_hmac(email) if email_enc and email.strip() else None
    _check_email_free(db, addr_hash)

    vol_name = f"{first_name} {last_name[0]}."
    if nickname:
        vol_name += f" ({nickname})"

    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO volunteers (vol_id, name, time_pref, add_time, email_enc, email_hmac) "
        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?);",
        (vol_id, vol_name, time_pref, add_time, email_enc, addr_hash)
    )
    db.commit()
    audit("volunteer.add", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Added volunteer {vol_id}: {vol_name}")

    return JSONResponse(status_code=201, content={
        "key": vol_id, "name": vol_name, "requested": time_pref,
        "additional": add_time, "sched_list": [], "slot_count": 0,
        "email_indexed": addr_hash is not None,
    })

@router.post("/api/admin/volunteers/email_hmac")
def fill_email_hmac(
    request: Request,
    vol_id: str = Form(...),
    email: str = Form(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Fill in a missing email_hmac for a volunteer added by hand before add_vol computed it.

    The Volunteers tab decrypts the address in the browser with the private key and sends it
    here; it's hashed and dropped, never stored or logged. Only fills a gap: a volunteer who
    already has an email_hmac (every portal signup) is left alone.

    Args:
        request: The incoming request, for the session id and the audit log.
        vol_id: The volunteer.
        email: Their address, decrypted in the browser. Hashed, never stored or logged.
        s_data: The organizer's session.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Returns:
        dict ``{"ok": True}``.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 404: No such volunteer, or it has no encrypted email.
        HTTPException 409: Already indexed, or the address belongs to someone else.
        HTTPException 503: EMAIL_HMAC_KEY isn't set.
    """
    row = db.execute("SELECT email_enc, email_hmac FROM volunteers WHERE vol_id = ?;",
                     (vol_id,)).fetchone()
    if not row or not row["email_enc"]:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="No such volunteer with an email")
    if row["email_hmac"]:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="That volunteer's email is already indexed")
    addr_hash = email_hmac(email)
    if not addr_hash:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="EMAIL_HMAC_KEY isn't set on the scheduler")
    _check_email_free(db, addr_hash, vol_id)
    db.execute("UPDATE volunteers SET email_hmac = ? WHERE vol_id = ? AND email_hmac IS NULL;",
               (addr_hash, vol_id))
    db.commit()
    audit("volunteer.email_index", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Indexed the email of volunteer {vol_id}")
    return {"ok": True}

    request: Request,

    slot_key: str = Form(...),
    rating: str = Form(...),
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer", "checkin")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Record a rating note; checkin role is restricted to No-Show only.

    Args:
        request: Starlette Request; used for audit logging.
        vol_id: Volunteer being rated.
        slot_key: Composite slot key ``day_time_poskey``.
        rating: One of ``"Good"``, ``"Bad"``, ``"No-Show"``.
        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer or checkin role.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        HTTP 201 with a dict: ``rating``, ``username``, ``created_at``.

    Raises:
        HTTPException 400: rating is not a valid value.
        HTTPException 403: checkin role attempted a rating other than No-Show.
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    if rating not in VALID_RATINGS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f"Invalid rating. Must be one of: {', '.join(VALID_RATINGS)}")
    if s_data["role"] == "checkin" and rating != "No-Show":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Forbidden")

    note_id  = str(uuid.uuid4())
    note     = f"[Rating] {rating} | {slot_key}"
    db.execute("INSERT INTO vol_notes (note_id, vol_id, note, username) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?);",
               (note_id, vol_id, note, s_data["username"]))
    db.commit()
    broadcast("rating")
    audit("volunteer.rate", request, request.session.get("session_id"),
          f"Rated volunteer {vol_id} at {slot_key}: {rating}")

    row = db.execute(
        "SELECT note, username, created_at FROM vol_notes WHERE note_id = ?;", (note_id,)
    ).fetchone()
    return JSONResponse(status_code=201, content={
        "rating": rating, "username": row["username"], "created_at": row["created_at"]
    })

@router.post("/api/vol_notes_report")
def vol_notes_report(
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Return all organizer notes per volunteer, excluding [Rating] and [CheckIn] system notes.

    Args:
        s_data: Injected session dict; requires organizer role.
        db: Injected database connection.

    Returns:
        list of volunteer dicts, each with keys ``vol_id``, ``name``, ``pos_keys``,
        and ``notes`` (list of ``{note, username, created_at}``).

    Raises:
        HTTPException 401/403: Insufficient role.
    """
    rows = db.execute("""
        SELECT v.vol_id, v.name,
               (SELECT STRING_AGG(s.day_key || '_' || s.time_key || '_' || s.pos_key, ', ')
                FROM schedule s WHERE s.vol_id = v.vol_id) as pos_keys,
               vn.note, vn.username, vn.created_at
        FROM volunteers v
        LEFT JOIN vol_notes vn ON v.vol_id = vn.vol_id
            AND vn.note NOT LIKE '[Rating]%'
            AND vn.note NOT LIKE '[CheckIn]%'
        ORDER BY v.name, vn.created_at DESC;
    """).fetchall()

    vols      = {}
    vol_order = []
    for row in rows:
        vid = row["vol_id"]
        if vid not in vols:
            vols[vid] = {"vol_id": vid, "name": row["name"],
                         "pos_keys": row["pos_keys"] or "", "notes": []}
            vol_order.append(vid)
        if row["note"] is not None:
            vols[vid]["notes"].append({
                "note": row["note"], "username": row["username"], "created_at": row["created_at"],
            })

    return [vols[vid] for vid in vol_order]

@router.get("/api/admin/volunteers")
def list_all_volunteers(
    s_data: dict = Depends(RoleChecker("organizer")),
    db: PgClient = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Every volunteer, whatever their status, with their picks, answers, and schedule.

    Backs Admin → Volunteers. Unlike get_vols, which feeds the assignment pickers and so lists
    assignable volunteers only, this includes pending, cancelled and inactive ones.

    Three queries for the whole roster, grouped here, rather than one per volunteer.
    Check-ins are the `[CheckIn] | {day}_{time}_{pos}` notes, matched exactly as
    _build_schedule matches them.

    Args:
        s_data: The organizer's session.
        db: The request's database connection.

    Returns:
        dict ``{"volunteers": [...]}``, each with ``vol_id``, ``name``, ``status``,
        ``created_at``, ``time_pref``, ``add_time``, ``add_any``, ``answers``,
        ``possible_duplicate_of``, ``email_enc`` (ciphertext), ``picks`` (with labels),
        ``shifts`` (in schedule order, with ``checked_in``), and ``shift_count``.
    """
    vols = db.execute(
        "SELECT vol_id, name, status, created_at, time_pref, add_time, add_any, answers, "
        "possible_duplicate_of, cancelled_at, inactive_at, email_enc, "
        "(email_hmac IS NOT NULL) AS email_indexed FROM volunteers "
        "ORDER BY LOWER(name), vol_id;"
    ).fetchall()

    picks: dict = {}
    for p in db.execute(
        "SELECT vp.vol_id, vp.day_key, vp.time_key, vp.kind, vp.rank, "
        "d.day_str || ' ' || t.time_str AS label FROM vol_picks vp "
        "LEFT JOIN days_table d ON d.day_key = vp.day_key "
        "LEFT JOIN times_table t ON t.time_key = vp.time_key "
        "ORDER BY vp.vol_id, vp.kind DESC, vp.rank, vp.day_key, vp.time_key;"
    ).fetchall():
        picks.setdefault(p["vol_id"], []).append(
            {k: p[k] for k in ("day_key", "time_key", "kind", "rank", "label")})

    shifts: dict = {}
    for s in db.execute("""
        SELECT s.vol_id, s.day_key, d.day_str, s.time_key, t.time_str,
               s.pos_key, p.pos_str, p.pos_cat,
               EXISTS (
                   SELECT 1 FROM vol_notes vn
                   WHERE vn.vol_id = s.vol_id
                   AND vn.note = '[CheckIn] | ' || s.day_key || '_' || s.time_key || '_' || s.pos_key
               ) AS checked_in
        FROM schedule s
        LEFT JOIN days_table d  ON d.day_key  = s.day_key
        LEFT JOIN times_table t ON t.time_key = s.time_key
        LEFT JOIN positions p   ON p.pos_key  = s.pos_key
        WHERE s.vol_id IS NOT NULL
        ORDER BY s.vol_id, s.day_key, s.time_key, s.pos_key;
    """).fetchall():
        shifts.setdefault(s["vol_id"], []).append(
            {k: s[k] for k in ("day_key", "day_str", "time_key", "time_str",
                               "pos_key", "pos_str", "pos_cat", "checked_in")})

    out = []
    for v in vols:
        mine = shifts.get(v["vol_id"], [])
        out.append({
            "vol_id": v["vol_id"], "name": v["name"], "status": v["status"],
            "cancelled": v["cancelled_at"] is not None, "inactive": v["inactive_at"] is not None,
            # Ciphertext only; the Volunteers tab decrypts it in the browser with a private key
            # the organizer supplies (frontend lib/email_crypto.js). Never readable here.
            "email_enc": v["email_enc"],
            # False for a volunteer added by hand before add_vol computed the HMAC; the
            # Volunteers tab offers to fill these in once emails are decrypted.
            "email_indexed": bool(v["email_indexed"]),
            "created_at": v["created_at"].isoformat() + "Z" if v["created_at"] else None,
            "time_pref": v["time_pref"] or "", "add_time": v["add_time"] or "",
            "add_any": bool(v["add_any"]), "answers": v["answers"] or {},
            "possible_duplicate_of": v["possible_duplicate_of"] or [],
            "picks": picks.get(v["vol_id"], []),
            "shifts": mine, "shift_count": len(mine),
        })
    return {"volunteers": out}

docs.title: mailrelay.relay
docs.text:
Mail relay — the only process that holds a Microsoft Graph credential.

It sends as RELAY_MAILBOX's account using a delegated Mail.Send sign-in: one device-code login (python relay.py login) stores a refresh token, and every send exchanges it for a short-lived access token. That refresh token is a credential for a real person's account, so it's kept out of the internet-facing portal and lives only here. The relay does one thing: send a plain-text message as MAIL_SENDER, which the operator sets at startup. A caller supplies exactly to, subject and body; it can't choose the sender, add headers, send HTML or attach anything.

Messages go to Graph as structured JSON with contentType "Text", not as MIME, so Microsoft builds every header and there is nothing for a caller to inject into.

Standard library only, on purpose: the smaller this process, the less there is to attack in the one container that holds the credential.

python relay.py             # serve; needs MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN, GRAPH_*, RELAY_MAILBOX
python relay.py login       # one-time device-code sign-in as RELAY_MAILBOX
pytest test_relay.py -v     # no network needed

def __init__(self):
    self.tenant_id     = os.getenv("GRAPH_TENANT_ID", "").strip()
    self.client_id     = os.getenv("GRAPH_CLIENT_ID", "").strip()
    self.token         = os.getenv("MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN", "").strip()
    # The account that signs in and the mailbox mail goes through, not the From address.
    self.mailbox       = os.getenv("RELAY_MAILBOX", "").strip()
    # The From address of every message, the conference's own (e.g. volunteers@...).
    self.sender        = os.getenv("MAIL_SENDER", "").strip()
    # Holds the refresh token. The only writable path in the container.
    self.state_dir     = os.getenv("RELAY_STATE_DIR", "/state")
    self.port          = int(os.getenv("RELAY_PORT", "5002"))
    # Graph allows 30 messages a minute per mailbox; stay under it.
    self.rate_per_min  = int(os.getenv("RELAY_RATE_PER_MIN", "20"))
    self.rate_per_hour = int(os.getenv("RELAY_RATE_PER_HOUR", "300"))

    missing = [n for n, v in (("GRAPH_TENANT_ID", self.tenant_id),
                              ("GRAPH_CLIENT_ID", self.client_id),
                              ("MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN", self.token),
                              ("RELAY_MAILBOX", self.mailbox),
                              ("MAIL_SENDER", self.sender)) if not v]
    if missing:
        raise ConfigError(f"missing {', '.join(missing)}")
    if len(self.token) < 32:
        raise ConfigError("MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN must be at least 32 characters "
                          "(generate one with `openssl rand -hex 32`)")
    if len(self.sender) > 254 or not _ADDR.match(self.sender):
        raise ConfigError("MAIL_SENDER must be one plain address, e.g. volunteers@example.org")

def allow(self, now: float) -> bool:
    """Count one send, if the limits allow it.

    Args:
        now: The current time, in seconds (`time.time()`).

    Returns:
        True when the send may go ahead and has been counted; False when either window is full.
    """
    with self.lock:
        while self.sent and self.sent[0] <= now - 3600:
            self.sent.popleft()
        last_min = sum(1 for t in self.sent if t > now - 60)
        if last_min >= self.per_min or len(self.sent) >= self.per_hour:
            return False
        self.sent.append(now)
        return True

def read(self):
    """The stored refresh token, read fresh each time.

    Returns:
        The token, or `None` before the first `login`.

def write(self, token: str) -> None:
    """Replace the refresh token atomically, with mode 0600.

    Args:
        token: The new refresh token.
    """
    tmp = f"{self.path}.tmp"
    fd = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
    with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as f:
        f.write(token)
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())
    os.replace(tmp, self.path)

def send(self, to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> None:
    """Send one plain-text message from `MAIL_SENDER` through `/me/sendMail`.

    Args:
        to: The one recipient.
        subject: The subject line.
        body: The plain-text body.

    Raises:
        SignInRequired: When there is no usable sign-in.
        MailError: When Graph refuses the token refresh or the send.
    """
    payload = {
        "message": {
            "from": {"emailAddress": {"address": self.cfg.sender}},
            "subject": subject,
            "body": {"contentType": "Text", "content": body},
            "toRecipients": [{"emailAddress": {"address": to}}],
        },
        "saveToSentItems": True,
    }
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{GRAPH_API}/me/sendMail",
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method="POST",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self._token()}",
                 "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    try:
        with _urlopen(req, timeout=20):
            pass  # 202 Accepted, empty body
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        if exc.code == 401:
            self.token = None  # revoked mid-hour; the next send refreshes
        raise MailError(f"Graph sendMail failed: {_describe(exc.code, _error_body(exc))}") from None

def authorized(self, header: str) -> bool:
    """Check the caller's bearer token, in constant time.

    Args:
        header: The `Authorization` header, or blank.

    Returns:
        Whether it is `Bearer` with the relay's token.
    """
    scheme, _, presented = (header or "").partition(" ")
    return scheme == "Bearer" and hmac.compare_digest(presented.encode(),
                                                      self.cfg.token.encode())

def send(self, auth_header: str, raw: bytes) -> tuple[int, dict]:
    """Handle one `POST /send`: check auth, validate, rate limit, send.

    Args:
        auth_header: The `Authorization` header.
        raw: The request body.

    Returns:
        `(status, body)`: 202 sent, 400 invalid, 401 unauthorized, 429 rate limited, 502
        Graph or network failure, 503 not signed in.
    """
    if not self.authorized(auth_header):
        return 401, {"error": "unauthorized"}
    try:
        to, subject, body = validate(json.loads(raw))
    except ValueError as exc:  # json.JSONDecodeError is a ValueError too
        return 400, {"error": str(exc) if not isinstance(exc, json.JSONDecodeError)
                     else "body must be JSON"}
    if not self.limiter.allow(self.clock()):
        log.warning("send refused: rate limit")
        return 429, {"error": "rate limit exceeded"}
    mid = uuid.uuid4().hex
    try:
        self.graph.send(to, subject, body)
    except SignInRequired as exc:
        log.error("send %s failed: %s", mid, exc)
        return 503, {"error": str(exc), "id": mid}
    except MailError as exc:
        log.error("send %s failed: %s", mid, exc)
        return 502, {"error": str(exc), "id": mid}
    except OSError as exc:  # DNS, connection refused, timeout
        log.error("send %s failed: %s", mid, type(exc).__name__)
        return 502, {"error": f"could not reach Microsoft: {type(exc).__name__}", "id": mid}
    # Logs carry an id, never the address — the same rule as the portal's audit log.
    log.info("send %s ok", mid)
    return 202, {"sent": True, "id": mid}

def do_POST(self):
    """Check the transport (path, JSON content type, length) and pass `/send` to `Relay`."""
    if self.path != "/send":
        return self._reply(404, {"error": "not found"})
    if self.headers.get_content_type() != "application/json":
        return self._reply(415, {"error": "Content-Type must be application/json"})
    try:
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", ""))
    except ValueError:
        return self._reply(411, {"error": "Content-Length required"})
    if length < 0 or length > MAX_REQUEST_BYTES:
        return self._reply(413, {"error": "request too large"})
    raw = self.rfile.read(length)
    self._reply(*self.server.relay.send(self.headers.get("Authorization", ""), raw))

def login(cfg: Config, out=print, sleep=time.sleep, clock=time.time) -> str:
    """Device-code sign-in as RELAY_MAILBOX. Saves the refresh token; returns who signed in.

    Args:
        cfg: The relay's settings.
        out: Where to print the device-code instructions.
        sleep: Waits between polls. Tests pass a fake.
        clock: The time source. Tests pass a fake.

    Raises:
        MailError: When sign-in fails, times out, or signs in as an account other than
            `RELAY_MAILBOX`.
    """
    base = f"{GRAPH_LOGIN}/{urllib.parse.quote(cfg.tenant_id)}/oauth2/v2.0"
    try:
        dc = _post_form(f"{base}/devicecode", {"client_id": cfg.client_id, "scope": SCOPES})
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        raise MailError(f"device code request failed: {_describe(exc.code, _error_body(exc))}") from None
    out(dc["message"])
    interval = int(dc.get("interval", 5))
    deadline = clock() + int(dc.get("expires_in", 900))
    while clock() < deadline:
        sleep(interval)
        try:
            tok = _post_form(f"{base}/token", {"client_id": cfg.client_id,
                                               "grant_type": DEVICE_CODE_GRANT,
                                               "device_code": dc["device_code"]})
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            err = _error_body(exc)
            if err.get("error") == "authorization_pending":
                continue
            if err.get("error") == "slow_down":
                interval += 5
                continue
            raise MailError(f"sign-in failed: {_describe(exc.code, err)}") from None
        user = _id_token_user(tok.get("id_token"))
        if user.lower() != cfg.mailbox.lower():
            raise MailError(f"signed in as {user or 'an unknown account'}, but RELAY_MAILBOX "
                            f"is {cfg.mailbox}; nothing was saved")
        if not tok.get("refresh_token"):
            raise MailError("no refresh token returned; is offline_access on the app's "
                            "API permissions?")
        TokenStore(cfg).write(tok["refresh_token"])
        return user
    raise MailError("the device code expired before sign-in finished; run login again")

def validate(payload) -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    """Return (to, subject, body) or raise ValueError with a reason safe to send back.

    Args:
        payload: The decoded JSON body.
    """
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise ValueError("body must be a JSON object")
    extra = set(payload) - {"to", "subject", "body"}
    if extra:
        raise ValueError(f"unexpected field(s): {', '.join(sorted(extra))}")
    to, subject, body = payload.get("to"), payload.get("subject"), payload.get("body")
    if not all(isinstance(v, str) for v in (to, subject, body)):
        raise ValueError("to, subject and body are required strings")
    to = to.strip()
    if len(to) > 254 or not _ADDR.match(to):
        raise ValueError("to must be a single plain email address")
    if not subject or len(subject) > MAX_SUBJECT or _CTRL.search(subject):
        raise ValueError(f"subject must be 1-{MAX_SUBJECT} characters on one line")
    if not body or len(body) > MAX_BODY or _BODY_CTRL.search(body):
        raise ValueError(f"body must be 1-{MAX_BODY} characters of plain text")
    return to, subject, body

def make_server(relay: Relay, host: str = "0.0.0.0",  # nosec B104
                port: int = 5002) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
    """Build the threaded HTTP server for a relay.

    Args:
        relay: The relay to serve.
        host: Address to listen on. All interfaces inside the container.
        port: Port to listen on.

    Returns:
        The server, not yet started.
    """
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), Handler)
    server.relay = relay
    return server

def main() -> None:
    """Run the relay, or `relay.py login` to sign in. Exits 2 on bad configuration."""
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
    try:
        cfg = Config()
    except ConfigError as exc:
        print(f"mailrelay: refusing to start — {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)

    if sys.argv[1:] == ["login"]:
        print(f"Sign in as {cfg.mailbox}.")
        try:
            user = login(cfg)
        except MailError as exc:
            sys.exit(f"login failed: {exc}")
        print(f"Signed in as {user}. The relay will use this sign-in from its next send.")
        return
    if sys.argv[1:]:
        sys.exit("usage: relay.py [login]")

    relay = Relay(cfg)
    server = make_server(relay, port=cfg.port)
    log.info("mailrelay ready on :%d, sending as %s through %s", cfg.port, cfg.sender,
             cfg.mailbox)
    if not relay.graph.signed_in():
        # Starts anyway, so `login` can be run inside the running container.
        log.warning("not signed in: sends will fail until `python relay.py login` is run")
    server.serve_forever()

docs.title: portal.config
docs.text:
Portal configuration, read from the environment at import time.

The one rule worth stating: EMAIL_HMAC_KEY is required and has no default. If the portal generated a fresh key when the variable was missing, every stored email_hmac would be orphaned — nobody could sign in, and the partial-unique index would stop deduplicating against existing rows. That failure is silent at boot and disastrous a week later, so a missing key is a hard startup failure instead.

def __init__(self, require_secrets: bool = True):
    self.db_path      = os.getenv("PORTAL_DB", "/data/portal.db")
    # The public URL volunteers see in a magic link. Deliberately NOT the same variable
    # the scheduler uses to reach the sync API: that one is often an internal address
    # (http://portal:5001) while this one must be the address a browser can open.
    self.base_url     = (os.getenv("PORTAL_PUBLIC_URL")
                         or os.getenv("PORTAL_BASE_URL")
                         or "http://localhost:5001").rstrip("/")
    # The organizer site's origin, which admin invite and reset links must start with
    # (routers/sync.py, send_admin_mail). A separate hostname in the deployment, so the
    # public portal host never serves /admin; unset, it is the same origin as base_url.
    self.admin_url    = (os.getenv("ADMIN_PUBLIC_URL", "").strip()
                         or self.base_url).rstrip("/")
    self.mail_backend = os.getenv("MAIL_BACKEND", "file")
    self.mail_dir     = os.getenv("MAIL_DIR", "/app/logs/portal_mail")
    self.smtp_host    = os.getenv("SMTP_HOST", "")
    self.smtp_port    = _int("SMTP_PORT", 587)
    self.smtp_user    = os.getenv("SMTP_USER", "")
    self.smtp_pass    = os.getenv("SMTP_PASS", "")
    self.smtp_from    = os.getenv("SMTP_FROM", "volunteers@example.org")
    # MAIL_BACKEND=relay sends through the mailrelay container. The Graph credentials live
    # there, never here; this process only holds the token that lets it ask.
    self.relay_url    = os.getenv("MAIL_RELAY_URL", "http://mailrelay:5002").rstrip("/")
    self.relay_token  = os.getenv("MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN", "").strip()
    if self.mail_backend == "relay" and not self.relay_token:
        raise ConfigError("MAIL_BACKEND=relay needs MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN")
    # mailer.py hands this to urlopen, which also opens file:// and other schemes.
    if self.mail_backend == "relay" and not self.relay_url.startswith(("http://",
                                                                        "https://")):
        raise ConfigError(f"MAIL_RELAY_URL must be http:// or https://, got "
                          f"{self.relay_url!r}")

    # Login link and session lifetimes.
    self.token_ttl_min      = _int("PORTAL_TOKEN_TTL_MIN", 15)
    self.session_ttl_hours  = _int("PORTAL_SESSION_TTL_HOURS", 12)
    self.remember_ttl_days  = _int("PORTAL_REMEMBER_TTL_DAYS", 90)

    # Rate limits, per IP and per address hash (§10).
    self.rate_per_min  = _int("PORTAL_RATE_PER_MIN", 5)
    self.rate_per_hour = _int("PORTAL_RATE_PER_HOUR", 30)
    # A response floor, so timing doesn't leak what the copy doesn't.
    self.response_floor_ms = _int("PORTAL_RESPONSE_FLOOR_MS", 250)

    # Strict input validation (validation.py): "report" records anomalies and lets the
    # request through as before; "enforce" refuses them too.
    self.strict = os.getenv("PORTAL_STRICT", "report").strip().lower() or "report"
    if self.strict not in ("report", "enforce"):
        raise ConfigError(f"PORTAL_STRICT must be report or enforce, got {self.strict!r}")

    # Sync request signing (§2). SYNC_SECRET_PREV lets a rotation land without
    # restarting both services at the same moment.
    self.sync_skew_sec = _int("SYNC_SKEW_SEC", 300)
    if require_secrets:
        self.email_hmac_key = _req("EMAIL_HMAC_KEY").encode()
        self.sync_key_id    = _req("SYNC_KEY_ID")
        self.sync_secret    = _req("SYNC_SECRET").encode()
    else:
        self.email_hmac_key = b""
        self.sync_key_id    = ""
        self.sync_secret    = b""
    prev = os.getenv("SYNC_SECRET_PREV", "").strip()
    self.sync_secret_prev = prev.encode() if prev else None

def secrets_for(self, key_id: str) -> list[bytes]:
    """Candidate signing secrets for a key id — current, plus the previous during rotation.

    Args:
        key_id: The key id from the request's signature header.

    Returns:
        The secrets to try, or `[]` for an unknown key id.
    """
    if key_id != self.sync_key_id:
        return []
    return [s for s in (self.sync_secret, self.sync_secret_prev) if s]

docs.title: portal.content
docs.text:
The portal's organizer-editable content: the landing page, the questionnaire, the invite.

Organizers edit all three in the scheduler (Volunteer Portal → Landing page / Questionnaire / Invite email), which pushes them here (POST /api/sync/content). Until a part has been saved, the default below is used, which is what the site said before any of this was editable.

This module is the portal's own copy of the rules. The scheduler has the same rules in backend/portal_content.py, so it can check and preview before saving, and backend/test_portal_content.py holds the two to each other. The apps share no code. Every push is checked here again, because a page volunteers load must not trust what arrives over the wire:

  • Templates (the landing page's Markdown and the invite email) are Jinja, rendered in the sandbox and limited to a small subset: variables from a fixed list, {% if %} with comparisons and and/or/not, and a few text filters. No loops, no {% set %}, no includes, calls, attribute or item access, so a template can't read anything it wasn't given or keep the portal busy.
  • Markdown is rendered with raw HTML off and images off, and links only to http(s), mailto: or this site's own paths. The result goes into the page as HTML, so this is what keeps script out of it.
  • The questionnaire must be the shape the form and signup_fields validation expect.

def render_template(source: str, values: dict, allowed: tuple, where: str) -> str:
    """Check a template, then render it in the sandbox.

    Args:
        source: The template text.
        values: A string for each allowed variable; missing ones render as "".
        allowed: The variable names it may use.
        where: What the template is, for errors.

    Returns:
        The rendered text.

    Raises:
        ContentError: The template isn't allowed, or fails to render.
    """
    _check_template(source, allowed, where)
    context = {name: str(values.get(name) or "") for name in allowed}
    try:
        return _ENV.from_string(source).render(context)
    except (TemplateError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise ContentError(f"{where}: {exc}") from None

def validate_landing(raw: Any) -> dict:
    """Check a landing page definition.

    Args:
        raw: ``intro``, ``main`` and ``sidebar`` (templated Markdown), ``roles_heading``, and
            ``roles``, each ``{icon, name, text}``.

    Returns:
        A clean copy.

    Raises:
        ContentError: For the first problem found.
    """
    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != set(DEFAULT_LANDING):
        raise ContentError("the landing page must have exactly: " + ", ".join(DEFAULT_LANDING))
    out: dict = {}
    for part in LANDING_PARTS:
        _check_template(raw[part], LANDING_VARS, f"Landing page {part}")
        out[part] = raw[part]
    out["roles_heading"] = _text(raw["roles_heading"], "The opportunities heading", 120,
                                 required=False)
    roles = raw["roles"]
    if not isinstance(roles, list) or len(roles) > MAX_ROLES:
        raise ContentError(f"opportunities must be a list of at most {MAX_ROLES}")
    out["roles"] = []
    for i, role in enumerate(roles, 1):
        if not isinstance(role, dict) or set(role) != {"icon", "name", "text"}:
            raise ContentError(f"opportunity {i} must have exactly icon, name and text")
        if role["icon"] not in ROLE_ICONS:
            raise ContentError(f"opportunity {i}: unknown icon {role['icon']!r}")
        out["roles"].append({"icon": role["icon"],
                             "name": _text(role["name"], f"Opportunity {i}'s name", 80),
                             "text": _text(role["text"], f"Opportunity {i}'s text", 200,
                                           required=False)})
    return out
