    cols = PUSH_COLUMNS
    # These columns are NOT NULL in the schema. A SQLite DEFAULT only fills a column that is
    # *omitted*, not one explicitly given NULL — so a push that leaves out first_name would
    # fail on the constraint unless we substitute here.
    non_null = {"first_name": "", "last_name": "", "nickname": "", "name": "",
                "status": "pending", "time_pref": "", "add_time": "", "add_any": 0}

    def _val(v: dict, col: str):
        got = v.get(col)
        if got is None and col in non_null:
            return non_null[col]
        return got

    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        renamed = 0
        for rk in rekeys:
            old, new = rk.get("vol_id"), rk.get("new_vol_id")
            if not old or not new or old == new:
                continue
            cur = conn.execute("UPDATE volunteers SET vol_id = ?, rev = ? WHERE vol_id = ?",
                               (new, db.next_rev(conn), old))
            if cur.rowcount:
                for stmt in _REKEY_SQL:
                    conn.execute(stmt, (new, old))
                renamed += 1
                db.audit(conn, "sync.rekey", new, detail=f"was {old}")

        written = 0
        for v in upserts:
            vol_id = v.get("vol_id")
            if not vol_id:
                continue
            rev = db.next_rev(conn)
            # Update only what the push carries. The scheduler doesn't hold first_name /
            # last_name / nickname (signup does), and must not blank them by omission. A push
            # left with nothing to update (say, only a status the guard dropped) changes
            # nothing on an existing row.
            sent = [c in v for c in cols]
            conn.execute(
                _UPSERT_VOLUNTEER_SQL,
                (vol_id, *(_val(v, c) for c in cols), clock.now_iso(), rev, *sent, any(sent)),
            )
            if "picks" in v:
                conn.execute("DELETE FROM vol_picks WHERE vol_id = ?", (vol_id,))
                conn.executemany(
                    "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO vol_picks (vol_id, day_key, time_key, kind, rank) "
                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    [(vol_id, p.get("day_key"), p.get("time_key"), p.get("kind", "pref"),
                      p.get("rank")) for p in (v.get("picks") or [])],
                )
            written += 1
        result = _record_op(conn, op_id, {"ok": True, "written": written, "renamed": renamed,
                                         "rev": db.current_rev(conn)})
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except Exception:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return result

@router.post("/api/sync/branding")
async def push_branding(body: bytes = Depends(verified_body),
                        conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(db.get_db)):
    """Conference title, the theme logo, its favicon, the header logo, and the public contact.

    The scheduler sends data URLs because that is how it stores them; the portal decodes once
    and keeps bytes, so it can serve them with an ETag instead of inlining megabytes of base64
    into every page load.

    Args:
        body: The raw body, after the signature check (`verified_body`).
        conn: The database connection.
    """
    import base64

    payload = _json_body(body)
    op_id, stored = _idempotent(conn, payload)
    if stored is not None:
        return stored

    incoming_hash = payload.get("content_hash") or ""
    current = conn.execute("SELECT content_hash FROM branding WHERE id = 1").fetchone()
    if incoming_hash and current and current["content_hash"] == incoming_hash:
        return _record_op(conn, op_id, {"ok": True, "unchanged": True})

    def _decode(data_url: Optional[str]) -> tuple[Optional[bytes], Optional[str]]:
        if not data_url:
            return None, None
        if not data_url.startswith("data:"):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="logo/favicon must be a data URL")
        header, _, b64 = data_url.partition(",")
        mime = header[5:].split(";")[0] or "application/octet-stream"
        try:
            return base64.b64decode(b64), mime
        except Exception:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400,
                                detail="logo/favicon base64 is malformed") from None

    contact_email, conference_url, coc_url = _public_contact(payload)
    logo, logo_mime = _decode(payload.get("logo"))
    favicon, _ = _decode(payload.get("favicon"))
    # Absent from a scheduler that predates it: that reads as "no header logo".
    header_logo, header_logo_mime = _decode(payload.get("header_logo"))
    conn.execute(
        "INSERT INTO branding (id, app_title, portal_title, logo, logo_mime, favicon, "
        "header_logo, header_logo_mime, contact_email, conference_url, code_of_conduct_url, "
        "content_hash, pushed_at) "
        "VALUES (1, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?) "
        "ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET app_title = excluded.app_title, "
        "portal_title = excluded.portal_title, logo = excluded.logo, "
        "logo_mime = excluded.logo_mime, favicon = excluded.favicon, "
        "header_logo = excluded.header_logo, header_logo_mime = excluded.header_logo_mime, "
        "contact_email = excluded.contact_email, conference_url = excluded.conference_url, "
        "code_of_conduct_url = excluded.code_of_conduct_url, "
        "content_hash = excluded.content_hash, pushed_at = excluded.pushed_at",
        (payload.get("app_title"), payload.get("portal_title"), logo, logo_mime, favicon,
         header_logo, header_logo_mime, contact_email, conference_url, coc_url,
         incoming_hash, clock.now_iso()),

@router.post("/api/sync/signup_invites")
async def push_signup_invites(body: bytes = Depends(verified_body),
                              conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(db.get_db)):
    """The scheduler's early-access invites, replacing the portal's list wholesale.

    Each is {invite_id, token_hash, expires_at, revoked_at}: a hash, never the link. An invite
    the scheduler no longer lists is dropped. `used_at` is the portal's (set at signup submit)
    and survives every push; the scheduler learns of a use from the volunteers pull, which
    carries the volunteer's `invite_id`.

    Args:
        body: The raw body, after the signature check (`verified_body`).
        conn: The database connection.
    """
    payload = _json_body(body)
    op_id, stored = _idempotent(conn, payload)
    if stored is not None:
        return stored
    invites = payload.get("invites")
    if not isinstance(invites, list):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="invites must be a list")
    rows = []
    for inv in invites:
        if not isinstance(inv, dict):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="each invite must be an object")
        invite_id, token_hash = inv.get("invite_id"), inv.get("token_hash")
        if not (isinstance(invite_id, str) and invite_id and isinstance(token_hash, str)
                and len(token_hash) == 64):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="invite_id and a SHA-256 token_hash "
                                "are required")
        expires = _iso_or_none(inv.get("expires_at"), "expires_at")
        if expires is None:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="expires_at is required")
        rows.append((invite_id, token_hash, expires, _iso_or_none(inv.get("revoked_at"),
                                                                    "revoked_at")))
    keep = [r[0] for r in rows]
    conn.execute("DELETE FROM signup_invites WHERE invite_id NOT IN "
                 "(SELECT value FROM json_each(?))", (json.dumps(keep),))
    conn.executemany(
        "INSERT INTO signup_invites (invite_id, token_hash, expires_at, revoked_at) "
        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT(invite_id) DO UPDATE SET "
        "token_hash = excluded.token_hash, expires_at = excluded.expires_at, "
        "revoked_at = excluded.revoked_at", rows)
    db.kv_set(conn, "signup_invites_hash", payload.get("content_hash") or "")
    return _record_op(conn, op_id, {"ok": True, "invites": len(rows)})

@router.post("/api/sync/purge_volunteers")
async def purge_volunteers(body: bytes = Depends(verified_body),
                           conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(db.get_db)):
    """Delete volunteers outright, so the same address can sign up again from scratch.

    For clearing test volunteers. Takes {op_id, vol_ids}; removes each row, its picks, every
    session and sign-in link for its id or its address hash, and that address's rate-limit
    counters, in one transaction. An id the portal doesn't have is skipped. The audit line
    records the id. The scheduler calls this before deleting its own copy, so a pull can't
    bring the volunteer back.

    Args:
        body: The raw body, after the signature check (`verified_body`).
        conn: The database connection.
    """
    payload = _json_body(body)
    op_id, stored = _idempotent(conn, payload)
    if stored is not None:
        return stored
    vol_ids = payload.get("vol_ids")
    if (not isinstance(vol_ids, list) or len(vol_ids) > PURGE_MAX
            or not all(isinstance(v, str) and v for v in vol_ids)):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400,
                            detail=f"vol_ids must be a list of up to {PURGE_MAX} ids")
    ids = json.dumps(sorted(set(vol_ids)))
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        hmacs = json.dumps([r["email_hmac"] for r in conn.execute(_PURGE_HMACS_SQL, (ids,))])
        for stmt in _PURGE_SQL:
            conn.execute(stmt, (ids, hmacs))
        for stmt in _PURGE_BY_ID_SQL:
            conn.execute(stmt, (ids,))
        conn.execute(_PURGE_RATE_SQL, (hmacs,))
        purged = []
        for vol_id in sorted(set(vol_ids)):
            if conn.execute(_PURGE_VOL_SQL, (vol_id,)).rowcount:
                purged.append(vol_id)
                db.audit(conn, "volunteer.purged", vol_id)
        result = _record_op(conn, op_id, {"ok": True, "purged": purged})
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except Exception:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return result

def alert_text(value: Any, limit: int) -> str:
    """One line of alert text that's safe to put in a plain-text email.

    An alert's details can come from whoever set it off (a username typed at sign-in, a
    user agent), so this assumes the worst: control and format characters (newlines, NUL,
    bidi overrides) become spaces, runs of space collapse, `{{` can't reach the template
    filler, and anything a mail app would turn into a link is broken (`https[:]//`,
    `www[.]`). Then it's cut to `limit`.

    Args:
        value: Anything; it's turned into text first.
        limit: The most characters to keep.

    Returns:
        The cleaned text, possibly empty.
    """
    text = "".join(" " if unicodedata.category(c)[0] in ("C", "Z") else c for c in str(value))
    text = " ".join(text.split())
    text = text.replace("{{", "{ {").replace("}}", "} }")
    text = re.sub(r"://", "[:]//", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?i)\bwww\.", lambda m: m.group(0)[:-1] + "[.]", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?i)\b(mailto|javascript|data):", r"\1[:]", text)
    return text[:limit].rstrip()

An alert's text fields are checked and defanged by _alert_values. Admin mail is at most ADMIN_MAIL_PER_HOUR, signup invites SIGNUP_INVITE_MAIL_PER_HOUR, alerts ALERT_MAIL_PER_HOUR, each its own allowance. Neither the address nor the link is stored; the audit line records the kind. op_id makes a retried request a replay, not a second email.

@router.post("/api/sync/send_admin_mail")
async def send_admin_mail(body: bytes = Depends(verified_body),
                          conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(db.get_db)):
    """Mail an admin invite, password reset, volunteer signup invite or security alert for
    the scheduler.

    The one exception to "the portal only mails an address someone has just proved they
    know" (CLAUDE.md), and so kept narrow: a signed request, one of four fixed templates, and
    a link that must be this deployment's own — the organizer site's (ADMIN_PUBLIC_URL)
    /admin/invite or /admin/reset, exactly /admin/audit for an alert, or the portal's own
    (PORTAL_PUBLIC_URL) /apply/signup?invite=. An alert's text fields are checked and
    defanged by `_alert_values`. Admin mail is at most ADMIN_MAIL_PER_HOUR, signup invites
    SIGNUP_INVITE_MAIL_PER_HOUR, alerts ALERT_MAIL_PER_HOUR, each its own allowance.
    Neither the address nor the link is stored; the audit line records the kind. op_id makes a
    retried request a replay, not a second email.

    Args:
        body: The raw body, after the signature check (`verified_body`).
        conn: The database connection.
    """
    payload = _json_body(body)
    op_id, stored = _idempotent(conn, payload)
    if stored is not None:
        return stored
    kind, to, link = payload.get("kind"), payload.get("to"), payload.get("link")
    if kind not in _ADMIN_PATHS:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Unknown kind")
    if not isinstance(to, str) or len(to) > 254 or not _ADDR.match(to):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Bad address")
    base = settings.base_url if kind == "signup_invite" else settings.admin_url
    if not isinstance(link, str) or not link.startswith(base + _ADMIN_PATHS[kind]) \
            or any(c.isspace() for c in link):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="That link isn't this site's")
    if kind == "alert" and link != base + _ADMIN_PATHS["alert"]:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="That link isn't this site's")
    values = _alert_values(payload) if kind == "alert" else None
    since = clock.iso(clock.now() - timedelta(hours=1))
    if kind == "signup_invite":
        sql, cap, what = _INVITE_MAIL_COUNT_SQL, SIGNUP_INVITE_MAIL_PER_HOUR, "invite"
    elif kind == "alert":
        sql, cap, what = _ALERT_MAIL_COUNT_SQL, ALERT_MAIL_PER_HOUR, "alert"
    else:
        sql, cap, what = _ADMIN_MAIL_COUNT_SQL, ADMIN_MAIL_PER_HOUR, "admin"
    if conn.execute(sql, (since,)).fetchone()[0] >= cap:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail=f"Too much {what} mail this hour")
    try:
        if kind == "signup_invite":
            # The organizers' own template (Volunteer Portal → Invite email), else the default.
            subject, text = content.render_invite(_invite_template(conn),
                                                  _invite_values(conn, link, payload))
            Mailer(settings).send(to, subject, text)
        elif kind == "alert":
            Mailer(settings).send_admin(kind, to, link, values)
        else:
            Mailer(settings).send_admin(kind, to, link, payload)
    except Exception as exc:                                    # noqa: BLE001
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail=f"Mail failed: {exc}") from exc
    db.audit(conn, "admin_mail.sent", detail=kind)
    return _record_op(conn, op_id, {"ok": True, "kind": kind})

@router.post("/api/sync/email_index")
async def push_email_index(body: bytes = Depends(verified_body),
                           conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(db.get_db)):
    """Backfill {vol_id, email_hmac} pairs produced offline by vol_mail.py index.

    Existing volunteers have ciphertext but no HMAC, and nothing on a server can read the
    ciphertext — so this is the only way they can ever sign in, and it necessarily comes from
    the machine holding the private key.

    Args:
        body: The raw body, after the signature check (`verified_body`).
        conn: The database connection.
    """
    payload = _json_body(body)
    op_id, stored = _idempotent(conn, payload)
    if stored is not None:
        return stored
    pairs = payload.get("pairs") or []
    updated, conflicts = 0, []
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        for pair in pairs:
            vol_id, addr_hash = pair.get("vol_id"), pair.get("email_hmac")
            if not vol_id or not addr_hash:
                continue
            try:
                cur = conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE volunteers SET email_hmac = ?, rev = ? WHERE vol_id = ?",
                    (addr_hash, db.next_rev(conn), vol_id),
                )
                updated += cur.rowcount
            except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
                # Two vol_ids resolving to one address is a real duplicate for an organizer
                # to merge, not something to paper over here.
                conflicts.append(vol_id)
        result = _record_op(conn, op_id, {"ok": True, "updated": updated,
                                         "conflicts": conflicts})
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except Exception:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    return result

docs.title: tools.vol_mail.vol_mail
docs.text:
vol_mail — send volunteers their schedule, with a check-in QR code for each shift.

Run on an organizer's own machine, once or twice before the conference (a draft, then a final after adjustments). It is not part of the website: no container copies it, and the site never sends this mail itself.

vol_mail.py fetch   --url https://<site> --key-file api_key.txt --out box.json
vol_mail.py preview --package schedule-email.zip --box box.json --vol 1042 --out preview/
vol_mail.py send    --package schedule-email.zip --box box.json --key private.pem --round draft --dry-run
vol_mail.py send    --package schedule-email.zip --box box.json --key private.pem --round draft
vol_mail.py send    ... --round final --only-changed-since draft --dry-run   (then without --dry-run)

Inputs: - The package — Call for Volunteers → Schedule Email → Download package. Markdown is already HTML in it; this tool only fills in placeholders, by the same rules as the site's preview (backend/email_render.py fill / render_message, copied below; the test suite checks the two agree). - The box — fetch saves the export API's volunteers, with each address still encrypted and each shift's check-in code. Needs an API key with volunteers:read, volunteers:email and checkin:codes (Admin → API Keys). fetch is the only command that talks to the scheduler. - private.pem — the organizers' key, which decrypts addresses in memory, one at a time.

Sending is Microsoft Graph, the same way the mail relay does it (mailrelay/relay.py): a delegated device-code sign-in as VOL_MAIL_MAILBOX, which has Send As on the From address (MAIL_SENDER, or --from). The sign-in is kept in memory only; nothing is saved, so each send run signs in afresh.

Safety rails: - send needs a --dry-run of the same round first. The dry run checks every address decrypts, renders every message, and writes the round's plan; the real run sends exactly that plan, and refuses if the package or box changed since. - At most --per-minute sends (20; Graph allows 30 a minute per mailbox). Interrupted? Run the same command again: anyone already sent in that round is skipped. - State and output record vol_ids only, never an address.

def sign_in(self) -> str:
    """Device-code sign-in as `mailbox`. Tokens stay in this object, never on disk.

    Returns:
        The account that signed in.

    Raises:
        Fail: When sign-in fails, times out, or signs in as another account.
    """
    try:
        dc = _post_form(f"{self.base}/devicecode", {"client_id": self.client_id, "scope": SCOPES})
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        raise Fail(f"device code request failed: "
                   f"{_describe(exc.code, _error_body(exc))}") from exc
    self.out(dc["message"])
    interval = int(dc.get("interval", 5))
    deadline = time.time() + int(dc.get("expires_in", 900))
    while time.time() < deadline:
        _sleep(interval)
        try:
            tok = _post_form(f"{self.base}/token", {"client_id": self.client_id,
                                                    "grant_type": DEVICE_CODE_GRANT,
                                                    "device_code": dc["device_code"]})
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            err = _error_body(exc)
            if err.get("error") == "authorization_pending":
                continue
            if err.get("error") == "slow_down":
                interval += 5
                continue
            raise Fail(f"sign-in failed: {_describe(exc.code, err)}") from exc
        user = _id_token_user(tok.get("id_token"))
        if user.lower() != self.mailbox.lower():
            raise Fail(f"signed in as {user or 'an unknown account'}, but VOL_MAIL_MAILBOX is "
                       f"{self.mailbox}")
        self._keep(tok)
        return user
    raise Fail("the device code expired before sign-in finished; run the command again")

def send(self, msg: dict, to: str) -> None:
    """Send one message, waiting out a 429 (up to three times). Raises Fail otherwise.

    Args:
        msg: The message from `build_message`.
        to: The recipient.
    """
    data = json.dumps(graph_payload(msg, to, self.sender)).encode()
    if len(data) > MAX_GRAPH_REQUEST:
        raise Fail(f"message is {len(data) // 1024} KB, over Graph's limit; use smaller images")
    for attempt in range(4):
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{GRAPH_API}/me/sendMail", data=data, method="POST",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self._access_token()}",
                     "Content-Type": "application/json"})
        try:
            with _urlopen(req, timeout=60):
                return
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            if exc.code == 429 and attempt < 3:
                wait = int(exc.headers.get("Retry-After") or 30)
                self.out(f"  Graph asked to slow down; waiting {wait}s")
                _sleep(wait)
                continue
            if exc.code == 401 and attempt < 3:
                self.token = None
                continue
            raise Fail(f"Graph sendMail failed: "
                       f"{_describe(exc.code, _error_body(exc))}") from exc

def fill(template: str, values: dict, as_html: bool) -> str:
    """Replace each `{{field}}` with its value. A copy of `backend/email_render.fill`.

    Args:
        template: Text containing `{{field}}` placeholders.
        values: Field name to value. An unknown field is left as it was.
        as_html: Escape values for HTML, except the fields in `RAW_HTML_FIELDS`.

    Returns:
        The filled-in text.
    """
    def sub(m):
        key = m.group(1)
        if key not in values:
            return m.group(0)
        val = str(values[key])
        return val if (not as_html or key in RAW_HTML_FIELDS) else html.escape(val)
    return PLACEHOLDER.sub(sub, template)

def human_date(iso):

def render_message(parts: dict, vol: dict, event_title: str, qr_src) -> dict:
    """One volunteer's subject, HTML and text. A copy of the backend's, so the site's
    preview and the sent message match.

    Args:
        parts: The package's template parts.
        vol: The volunteer, from the box.
        event_title: The value for `{{event_title}}`.
        qr_src: A callable `(index, shift) -> str` giving each QR image's source.

    Returns:
        `{"subject", "html", "text"}`.
    """
    who = {"name": vol["name"], "first_name": vol["first_name"], "handle": vol["handle"],
           "vol_id": vol["vol_id"], "event_title": event_title}
    blocks_html, blocks_txt = [], []
    for i, s in enumerate(vol["shifts"]):
        sv = {"day": s["day"], "date": human_date(s.get("date")), "time": s["time"],
              "position": s["position"], "category": s["category"]}
        blocks_html.append(fill(parts["shift_html"], {**sv, "qr": qr_img(qr_src(i, s), s)}, True))
        blocks_txt.append(fill(parts["shift_txt"], {**sv, "qr": f"Check-in code: {s['checkin_code']}"},
                               False))
    return {
        "subject": fill(parts["subject"], who, False),
        "html": fill(parts["body_html"], {**who, "shifts": "\n".join(blocks_html)}, True),
        "text": fill(parts["body_txt"], {**who, "shifts": "\n".join(blocks_txt).strip()}, False),
    }

def load_box(path: str) -> dict:
    """Read a box written by `fetch`, and check it has what sending needs.

    Args:
        path: The box file.

    Returns:
        The box: the export API's volunteers response.

    Raises:
        Fail: Not a box, or the API key lacked the `checkin:codes` or `volunteers:email` scope.
    """
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            box = json.load(f)
        box["volunteers"]
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError) as exc:
        raise Fail(f"{path} isn't a box from `vol_mail.py fetch` ({exc})") from exc
    for v in box["volunteers"]:
        for s in v["shifts"]:
            if "checkin_code" not in s:
                raise Fail(f"{path} has no check-in codes: the API key needs the checkin:codes scope")
        if "email_enc" not in v:
            raise Fail(f"{path} has no encrypted emails: the API key needs the volunteers:email scope")
    return box

def load_private_key(path: str):
    """Load the organizers' private key, asking for its passphrase if it has one.

    Args:
        path: The PEM file (`private.pem`).

    Returns:
        The key object.

    Raises:
        Fail: When the file isn't a PEM private key.
    """
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        pem = f.read()
    try:
        return serialization.load_pem_private_key(pem, password=None)
    except TypeError:     # encrypted key
        pw = getpass.getpass(f"Passphrase for {path}: ").encode()
        return serialization.load_pem_private_key(pem, password=pw)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise Fail(f"{path} isn't a PEM private key ({exc})") from exc

def decrypt_email(key, email_enc: str) -> str:
    """Decrypt one volunteer's address. It stays in memory only.

    Args:
        key: The private key from `load_private_key`.
        email_enc: The base64 RSA-OAEP ciphertext from the box.

    Returns:
        The address.
    """
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
    from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import padding
    pt = key.decrypt(base64.b64decode(email_enc),
                     padding.OAEP(mgf=padding.MGF1(algorithm=hashes.SHA256()),
                                  algorithm=hashes.SHA256(), label=None))
    return pt.decode().strip()

def build_message(pkg: dict, box: dict, vol: dict) -> dict:
    """Subject, HTML (with cid: images), text, and the inline attachments it needs.

    Args:
        pkg: The package from `load_package`.
        box: The box from `load_box`, for the event title.
        vol: The volunteer.
    """
    msg = render_message(pkg["parts"], vol, box.get("event_title", ""), lambda i, s: f"cid:qr-{i}")
    attachments = [{"cid": f"qr-{i}", "name": f"checkin-{i + 1}.png", "content_type": "image/png",
                    "data": qr_png(s["checkin_code"])} for i, s in enumerate(vol["shifts"])]
    used = sorted({m.group(1) for m in ASSET_REF.finditer(msg["html"])})
    for name in used:
        ctype, data = pkg["assets"][name]
        attachments.append({"cid": f"asset-{name}", "name": name, "content_type": ctype, "data": data})
    msg["html"] = ASSET_REF.sub(lambda m: f"cid:asset-{m.group(1)}", msg["html"])
    msg["attachments"] = attachments
    return msg

def message_digest(msg: dict) -> str:
    """A hash of one finished message, recorded in the plan so `send` can tell whether it changed.

    Args:
        msg: The message from `build_message`.

    Returns:
        The SHA-256 hex digest over the subject, both bodies and every attachment.
    """
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for part in (msg["subject"], msg["html"], msg["text"]):
        h.update(part.encode() + b"\0")
    for a in msg["attachments"]:
        h.update(a["cid"].encode() + hashlib.sha256(a["data"]).digest())
    return h.hexdigest()

def write_eml(msg: dict, path: str, to: str = "preview@example.invalid",
              sender: str = "") -> None:
    """A .eml to open in a mail app: text and HTML alternatives, images inline.

    Args:
        msg: The message from `build_message`.
        path: Where to write it.
        to: The To header. A placeholder by default, since previews aren't sent.
        sender: The From header. Blank uses MAIL_SENDER, or a placeholder for a preview.
    """
    from email.message import EmailMessage
    m = EmailMessage()
    m["From"], m["To"], m["Subject"] = sender or SENDER or PREVIEW_SENDER, to, msg["subject"]
    m.set_content(msg["text"])
    m.add_alternative(msg["html"], subtype="html")
    html_part = m.get_payload()[1]
    for a in msg["attachments"]:
        maintype, subtype = a["content_type"].split("/")
        html_part.add_related(a["data"], maintype=maintype, subtype=subtype,
                              cid=f"<{a['cid']}>", filename=a["name"])
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(bytes(m))

def read_sent(path: str) -> dict:

    sent = {}

    with open(args.key_file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        api_key = f.read().strip()
    url = args.url.rstrip("/") + "/api/export/volunteers?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(
        {"status": args.status, "assigned": "1"})
    if not url.startswith("https://") and not args.insecure_http:
        raise Fail("the URL must be https:// (the API key and addresses travel with it)")
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {api_key}"})
    try:
        with _urlopen(req, timeout=60) as resp:
            box = json.loads(resp.read())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        hint = {401: " (wrong, expired or revoked key, missing scope, or not an allowed IP)",
                429: " (too many failed attempts from this address; wait 15 minutes)"}.get(exc.code, "")
        raise Fail(f"the scheduler said HTTP {exc.code}{hint}") from exc
    except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
        raise Fail(f"couldn't reach {args.url}: {exc.reason}") from exc
    box["fetched_from"] = args.url
    _write_private(args.out, json.dumps(box, indent=1) + "\n")
    vols = box["volunteers"]
    no_email = sum(1 for v in vols if not v.get("email_enc"))
    out(f"Saved {len(vols)} volunteer(s) with shifts to {args.out} "
        f"({no_email} without an email). Generated {box.get('generated_at')}.")
    load_box(args.out)    # say now, not at send time, if the key lacked a scope
    return 0

def cmd_preview(args, out=print) -> int:
    """`preview`: write messages as `.eml`, `.html` and `.txt` files, sending nothing.

    Args:
        args: The parsed command line: `package`, `box`, `vol`, `out`.
        out: Where to print progress.

    Returns:
        The exit status.

    Raises:
        Fail: When the package or box is bad, or the volunteer isn't in the box.
    """
    pkg, box = load_package(args.package), load_box(args.box)
    vols = [v for v in box["volunteers"] if v["vol_id"] == args.vol] if args.vol else box["volunteers"][:1]
    if not vols:
        raise Fail(f"no volunteer {args.vol} in {args.box}")
    os.makedirs(args.out, exist_ok=True)
    for v in vols:
        msg = build_message(pkg, box, v)
        eml = os.path.join(args.out, f"{v['vol_id']}.eml")
        write_eml(msg, eml)
        # The same HTML with images inlined, for a browser.
        page = msg["html"]
        for a in msg["attachments"]:
            page = page.replace(f"cid:{a['cid']}",
                                f"data:{a['content_type']};base64,{base64.b64encode(a['data']).decode()}")
        with open(os.path.join(args.out, f"{v['vol_id']}.html"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(page)
        with open(os.path.join(args.out, f"{v['vol_id']}.txt"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(f"Subject: {msg['subject']}\n\n{msg['text']}")
        out(f"{v['vol_id']}: {eml} (.html and .txt beside it)")
    return 0

def cmd_send(args, graph_factory=None, out=print, confirm=input) -> int:
    """`send`: plan a round with `--dry-run`, then send it.

    The dry run builds every message and writes a plan. A real run sends the plan, skipping
    anyone the round's log already shows as sent, so an interrupted round can be resumed. It
    refuses if the package or box changed since the plan was made.

    Args:
        args: The parsed command line (see `main`).
        graph_factory: Builds the Graph client. Tests pass a fake.
        out: Where to print progress.
        confirm: Asks before sending. Skipped with `--yes`.

    Returns:
        0 when everything went, 1 when anything failed or the operator declined.

    Raises:
        Fail: No plan for the round, or the inputs changed since it was made.
    """
    os.makedirs(args.state, mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
    plan_path, sent_path = _state_paths(args.state, args.round)
    pkg, box = load_package(args.package), load_box(args.box)
    fingerprint = {"package_sha256": sha256_file(args.package), "box_sha256": sha256_file(args.box)}
    key = load_private_key(args.key)

    if args.dry_run:
        to_send, skipped = _select(box, args, out)
        recipients, bad = [], []
        for v in to_send:
            try:
                addr = decrypt_email(key, v["email_enc"])
            # Deliberately broad: whatever stops one address decrypting skips that volunteer
            # (reported below), not the whole run.
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
                bad.append((v["vol_id"], "address doesn't decrypt with this key"))
                continue
            if not _ADDR.match(addr):
                bad.append((v["vol_id"], "decrypted address isn't a plain address"))
                continue
            msg = build_message(pkg, box, v)
            recipients.append({"vol_id": v["vol_id"], "shifts": len(v["shifts"]),
                               "shifts_hash": shifts_hash(v), "message_sha256": message_digest(msg)})
        skipped += bad
        plan = {"round": args.round, "created_at": _now(), **fingerprint,
                "box_generated_at": box.get("generated_at"), "subject": pkg["parts"]["subject"],
                "only_changed_since": args.only_changed_since,
                "recipients": recipients, "skipped": [{"vol_id": a, "reason": b} for a, b in skipped]}
        _write_private(plan_path, json.dumps(plan, indent=1) + "\n")
        already = read_sent(sent_path)
        out(f"Round {args.round!r}: {len(recipients)} to send"
            + (f" ({sum(1 for r in recipients if r['vol_id'] in already)} already sent in this round)"
               if already else "") + f", {len(skipped)} skipped. Box generated {box.get('generated_at')}.")
        for vid, why in skipped:
            out(f"  skip {vid}: {why}")
        out(f"Plan written to {plan_path}. Run the same command without --dry-run to send.")
        return 1 if bad else 0

    if not os.path.exists(plan_path):
        raise Fail(f"no plan for round {args.round!r}; run it with --dry-run first")
    with open(plan_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        plan = json.load(f)
    for k, label in (("package_sha256", "package"), ("box_sha256", "box")):
        if plan[k] != fingerprint[k]:
            raise Fail(f"the {label} changed since the dry run; run --dry-run again")
    already = read_sent(sent_path)
    todo = [r for r in plan["recipients"] if r["vol_id"] not in already]
    if not todo:
        out(f"Round {args.round!r}: everyone in the plan has been sent. Nothing to do.")
        return 0
    by_id = {v["vol_id"]: v for v in box["volunteers"]}

    graph = (graph_factory or _graph_from_env)(args, out)
    out(f"Round {args.round!r}: about to send {len(todo)} email(s) as {graph.sender}"
        + (f" ({len(already)} already sent)" if already else "") + ".")
    if not args.yes and confirm("Type send to continue: ").strip().lower() != "send":
        out("Cancelled; nothing sent.")
        return 1
    who = graph.sign_in()
    out(f"Signed in as {who}.")

    gap = 60.0 / max(1, args.per_minute)
    failed = 0
    for n, r in enumerate(todo, 1):
        v = by_id[r["vol_id"]]
        msg = build_message(pkg, box, v)
        if message_digest(msg) != r["message_sha256"]:
            raise Fail(f"{r['vol_id']}: the message differs from the dry run; run --dry-run again")
        rec = {"vol_id": r["vol_id"], "at": _now(), "shifts_hash": r["shifts_hash"]}
        try:
            graph.send(msg, decrypt_email(key, v["email_enc"]))
            rec["ok"] = True
            out(f"  [{n}/{len(todo)}] sent {r['vol_id']}")
        except Fail as exc:
            rec.update(ok=False, error=str(exc))
            failed += 1
            out(f"  [{n}/{len(todo)}] FAILED {r['vol_id']}: {exc}")
        _append(sent_path, rec)
        if n < len(todo):
            _sleep(gap)
    out(f"Done: {len(todo) - failed} sent, {failed} failed."
        + (" Run the same command again to retry the failures." if failed else ""))
    return 1 if failed else 0

def main(argv=None) -> int:
    """Parse the command line and run `fetch`, `preview` or `send`.

    Args:
        argv: The arguments, without the program name. `None` reads `sys.argv`.

    Returns:
        The exit status.
    """
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="vol_mail.py", description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    f = sub.add_parser("fetch", help="download the volunteer box from the export API")
    f.add_argument("--url", required=True, help="the admin site, e.g. https://<admin hostname>")
    f.add_argument("--key-file", required=True, help="file holding the API key (bsc_…)")
    f.add_argument("--out", default="box.json")
    f.add_argument("--status", default="active", choices=("active", "all"))
    f.add_argument("--insecure-http", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)

    v = sub.add_parser("preview", help="write one volunteer's email as .eml/.html/.txt")
    v.add_argument("--package", required=True)
    v.add_argument("--box", required=True)
    v.add_argument("--vol", help="vol_id (default: the first in the box)")
    v.add_argument("--out", default="preview")

    s = sub.add_parser("send", help="send a round (--dry-run first)")
    s.add_argument("--package", required=True)
    s.add_argument("--box", required=True)
    s.add_argument("--key", required=True, help="the organizers' private key (PKCS#8 PEM)")
    s.add_argument("--round", required=True, help="a name per send, e.g. draft or final")
    s.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    s.add_argument("--only", help="file of vol_ids, one per line: send to these only")
    s.add_argument("--only-changed-since", metavar="ROUND",
                   help="only volunteers whose shifts differ from what ROUND sent them")
    s.add_argument("--state", default="vol_mail_state", help="where round plans and logs live")
    s.add_argument("--per-minute", type=int, default=20)
    s.add_argument("--from", dest="sender", default=SENDER,
                   help="the From address (default: MAIL_SENDER from the environment)")
    s.add_argument("--yes", action="store_true", help="don't ask before sending")

    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return {"fetch": cmd_fetch, "preview": cmd_preview, "send": cmd_send}[args.cmd](args)
    except Fail as exc:
        print(f"vol_mail: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

docs.title: Keeping it current
docs.text:
The bandit results are rebuilt whenever the docs are. The SBOM describes built images, so it's made by a script rather than at build time:

podman-compose build     # the images the SBOM describes
tools/sbom.sh            # one CycloneDX file per artifact, with vulnerabilities, into docs/security/sbom/
mkdocs build --strict    # or ./run_lint.sh; renders them here

Commit docs/security/sbom/ afterwards. Run it before each release, and whenever you want a fresh vulnerability check: trivy's database changes daily, so the same images can show new vulnerabilities a week later.

The Python libraries are pinned to their current major version (>= the release tested, < the next major), so a rebuild picks up fixes but not breaking changes. The JavaScript libraries are pinned exactly by frontend/package-lock.json.

docs.title: How this is made

Bandit runs over the same files, with the same bandit.yaml, as ./run_lint.sh: each app's code, then its tests with B101 (assert) skipped, since asserts are how pytest works. The lint fails on anything at medium severity and medium confidence or above. This page shows every level, so the low findings the lint lets through are visible too.

An accepted finding is marked # nosec Bxxx on its own line, with the reason beside it. There are no global skips. The reasoning behind each tier is in Quality & security.

docs.title: How this is made
docs.text:
tools/sbom.sh runs trivy over each artifact, with its vulnerability scanner on, and writes one CycloneDX file per artifact to docs/security/sbom/, plus meta.json with the date and trivy's version. This page is rendered from those files on every docs build; the files themselves are linked above, for tools that read CycloneDX.

  • Images are scanned as built, so the SBOM lists the Alpine packages and every installed Python package, at the versions actually in the image. Python itself isn't listed: the official image builds it from source rather than installing it as a package, so trivy can't see it. Its version is the image's tag (python:3.14…).
  • Frontend JavaScript comes from package-lock.json, production dependencies only: the build tools (Vite and the like) don't ship.
  • vol_mail isn't in any image. Its requirements are installed into a throwaway virtual environment and scanned there, with pip removed first, as it is from the app images. That leaves the tool's own libraries. The organizer's own environment still has pip, which is installer tooling the tool never runs. Scan that environment if you want it counted.
  • Severity is the rating from the vulnerability's own source (the Alpine, GitHub or Python advisory), falling back to the highest rating any source gives.

The PostgreSQL image is used as published (postgres:18-alpine), so its findings wait on the image's maintainers. Most are in gosu, a small Go program the image's entrypoint runs once at start to drop root before PostgreSQL starts. It's built with an old Go, and none of the network-facing Go code it's flagged for runs in this stack. The app images, by contrast, are built here with apk upgrade, so a rebuild takes every Alpine fix.

A listed vulnerability isn't necessarily reachable. Many are in code paths this project never calls, such as a library feature it doesn't use. Fix what has a fix by rebuilding the images (the pinned ranges take patch and minor releases), and look at the rest before deciding.

docs.title: Backend: the scheduler API
docs.text:
The backend is the organizers' system of record: the schedule, the volunteer roster, notes, ratings, check-ins, radios, organizer accounts and export API keys. It's a FastAPI app on PostgreSQL 18, and it's reachable only through the admin hostname, behind an access gate at the edge.

Code: backend/. Reference: backend.main and the modules beside it.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Module What it does main The app: routers, session middleware, and startup (SSE loop, portal sync). db The connection pool, PgClient, migrations, get_session_data and RoleChecker. Imports nothing from the app. portal_sync The sync loop that keeps the portal up to date, and pulls signups back. checkin_codes Shift check-in codes (HMAC) and the early/late rule. api_auth Export API keys: scopes, IP allow-lists, the failure limiter. email_render The schedule email: Markdown to HTML and text, placeholders, QR codes, the package zip. names Splitting a stored name, and the export API's name format. routers/ One module per area of the API.

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
The schema is scheduler.sql, the whole current schema, for a fresh database. 1.0 is the baseline. Each later release that changes the schema adds one file, migrations/<release>.sql, which an existing database gets once, in order, when the backend starts. The list is SCHEMA_RELEASES in db.py. See Releasing.

The main tables:

  • Schedule. days_table, times_table, positions and categories define the structure. day_times says which times each day runs. schedule has one row per slot (a position at a timeslot), holding the assigned vol_id.
  • Volunteers. volunteers (name, status, encrypted email, picks and answers from the portal), vol_picks (timeslot preferences), vol_notes (notes, check-ins and ratings) and shift_flags.
  • Radios. radios and radio_checkouts.
  • Accounts. users, sessions, user_passkeys, user_invites, password_resets and api_tokens.
  • Settings. app_kv: the site title and logos, the event timezone, the email public key, the check-in key and the cookie secret.

Every query is a complete literal with ? placeholders, which PgClient rewrites for psycopg2. Rows come back as dicts.

docs.title: A volunteer's state
docs.text:
Three fields, each with one owner:

Field Owner Values status organizers pending (signed up), then active (approved, i.e. through orientation) cancelled_at the volunteer, through the portal set when they cancel, cleared when they rejoin inactive_at organizers Make inactive and Reinstate

Three generated columns turn those into the rules everything else uses: is_assignable (approved, and neither cancelled nor inactive) for the assignment pickers, is_counted for capacity and demand, and is_live for the pending queue. A slot whose volunteer is no longer live needs a replacement, and the Schedule tab's banner lists it.

docs.title: Organizer accounts
docs.text:
Three roles:

Role Can do organizer everything checkin check volunteers in, rate them, issue and return radios view read only

Organizers sign in with a password (Argon2) or a passkey. New organizers can be invited with a 72-hour single-use link, and a forgotten password can be reset by email. Both kinds of mail go out through the portal, because the backend has no mail path of its own.

docs.title: Sync with the portal
docs.text:
The backend is always the client. Every PORTAL_SYNC_INTERVAL seconds, and shortly after any change, one pass runs in this order:

  1. Heartbeat. Checks the portal is up and that both sides hold the same keys.
  2. Pull volunteers changed since the last cursor, with their picks.
  3. Push pending decisions (approvals, inactive, re-keys), then any settings that differ (signup open, the email public key).
  4. Push the schedule snapshot, the branding, and the early-access invite list.

Each push replaces the portal's copy wholesale, and a content_hash makes an unchanged push free. Each volunteer column has one owner, so a push can't overwrite an edit the volunteer just made in the portal. A decision waits in portal_dirty until the portal accepts it. Interaction diagrams shows the whole pass.

Volunteer Portal in the admin site shows the last pass, any error, and whether the keys match.

docs.title: Purging volunteers
docs.text: Purge deletes inactive volunteers outright, here and on the portal. It's for clearing test volunteers, so their addresses can sign up again from scratch. The portal goes first. If it can't be reached, nothing is deleted. Picks, notes, check-ins and ratings go with the volunteer, their slots become empty, and radio history keeps the name.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
logs/audit.jsonl records every write, sign-in, sign-out and refusal, one JSON object per line: the time in UTC, an event code such as auth.login.fail, its severity, who did it, the client address, the request path, a message, and structured details. Read it with jq:

jq -c 'select(.event == "auth.login.fail")' logs/audit.jsonl          # failed sign-ins
jq -c 'select(.severity == "high" or .severity == "medium")' logs/audit.jsonl
jq -r '.ip' logs/audit.jsonl | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head        # busiest addresses

Each event is also a row in the audit_events table, which the admin site's Audit Log reads. The table keeps AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (365 by default); the file keeps everything.

The list of event codes and their severities is EVENTS in backend/audit.py.

Security alerts (backend/alerts.py) watch those events: bursts of failed sign-ins, a password spray, account and role changes, credential changes made by someone else, a new email key or export key, refused export calls, and sign-ins or key use from a new network. Requests to both the backend and the portal are also watched for attack patterns (SQL or script injection, path traversal, scanner tools, the paths scanners try) and for clients piling up refused or malformed requests. The portal's findings come to the backend's audit log over the sync API. Nothing is blocked; a request carrying a NUL character is the one refused, as no browser sends one.

A fired alert is recorded as alert.fired and emailed, through the portal, to organizers ticked for Security alerts in Admin → Users who have an address on their account. Every organizer can read the log itself (Admin → Audit Log). Each kind fires at most once an hour for the same cause, and at most 15 alerts are mailed an hour in all. The old free-text logs/audit.log (before release 1.1) is left as it was and no longer written.

Successful healthchecks are left out of the access log, and a healthy, idle backend logs nothing. A sync problem is logged once as a warning, and recovery as one portal sync healthy line.

docs.title: Frontend: the website
docs.text:
One Vue 3 build serves three areas. nginx serves it, and sends API calls on to the backend and the portal.

Path What it is Talks to / The public call for volunteers the portal (branding) /apply/* The volunteer portal: sign up, sign in, manage a registration the portal only /admin The organizer app the backend /admin/invite, /admin/reset Accepting an organizer invite; resetting a password the backend

Code: frontend/. Vue 3 with <script setup>, PrimeVue 4 components, Vite and vue-router. Design notes for each component are in frontend/CLAUDE.md.

docs.title: Two sites from one build
docs.text:
nginx (frontend/default.conf) runs two servers on the same files:

  • Port 8082, the public hostname serves /, /apply/*, the assets and /api/portal/*. Everything else, /admin and the organizer API included, is a 404 from nginx, so nothing public can reach the backend.
  • Port 8080, the admin hostname serves everything. A fresh load of / there redirects to /admin, so organizers land on the sign-in page.

Both take the client address from the edge's client-IP header, and pass it on as a single X-Forwarded-For value.

docs.title: How the pages work
docs.text:
• The admin app loads lazily. The landing page is the only view in the main bundle, so a volunteer on conference wifi never downloads the organizer editors or the barcode scanner.
  • The /apply/ pages call /api/portal/* only, never a scheduler endpoint.
  • API paths are absolute (fetch('/api/...')), because pages live at nested paths. Request bodies are FormData, not JSON.
  • Link pages do nothing on load. /apply/verify, /admin/invite and /admin/reset spend their token only when the button is pressed, then remove it from the browser history.
  • Volunteer email addresses are encrypted and decrypted in the browser. Adding a volunteer by hand encrypts the address to the public key before it's sent. Showing addresses in Admin → Volunteers decrypts them locally with private.pem, which never leaves the organizer's machine.
  • Open organizer pages refresh themselves. The backend sends a server-sent event after each change, and the page refetches what it shows.

docs.title: Look
docs.text: The organizer app uses PrimeVue's Aura theme with a custom dark preset. The volunteer pages use bsidescharm.org's light look (assets/portal-theme.css), with the title and logos the organizers set in App Settings.

docs.title: Developing
docs.text:
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev        # Vite with hot reload; proxies /api/portal to the portal, /api to the backend
npm run build      # what the container builds

The dev server expects the backend and the portal to be running, for example with the compose stack up. See Getting started.

docs.title: Mail relay
docs.text:
The relay is the only container that holds a Microsoft Graph credential. The portal hands it one plain-text message at a time, and it sends that message as MAIL_SENDER, the conference's volunteer address, set in .env. It does nothing else.

Code: mailrelay/relay.py, standard library only. Reference: mailrelay.relay. Setting it up: Graph mail setup.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text: Sending through Graph needs a credential for a real person's Microsoft account. Keeping it out of the internet-facing portal means a compromised portal can, at most, ask for plain-text mail from the one address the operator set, at a limited rate. It can't read mail, choose the sender, or take the credential.

docs.title: What it accepts
docs.text:
POST /send, with Authorization: Bearer $MAIL_RELAY_TOKEN and a JSON body of exactly to, subject and body:

  • One recipient, a plain address: no lists, no display names.
  • A one-line subject, and a plain-text body.
  • Any other field is refused with a 400. A caller that sends html or from finds out at once that it doesn't work.
Status Meaning 202 Sent. The body has an id, which is what the logs record. 400 The message failed validation. 401 Wrong or missing token. 411, 413, 415 No length, too large, or not JSON. 429 Over the rate limit: 20 a minute and 300 an hour. Graph's own cap is 30 a minute. 502 Graph or the network failed. The error carries Graph's code, never the address. 503 Not signed in, or the sign-in expired. Run relay.py login.

GET /health reports whether it's signed in.

docs.title: How it sends
docs.text:
• The sender is usually a Microsoft 365 group, and Graph can't send from a group directly. So the relay signs in as RELAY_MAILBOX and sends with From set to MAIL_SENDER. Exchange checks that the account has Send As on the group.
  • Graph receives structured JSON, not MIME. Microsoft builds the headers, so there's nothing for a caller to inject into.
  • The sign-in is delegated: a device-code sign-in once, then a refresh token on the mailrelay_state volume (mode 0600). Microsoft issues a new refresh token on every use, and the relay replaces the file atomically. It re-reads the file on each refresh, so a new login takes effect without a restart.

docs.title: Hardening
docs.text:
• The container's filesystem is read-only except /state, with every capability dropped and no-new-privileges.
  • It publishes no ports. It's on mail_internal, which only the portal shares and which has no route out, and on mail_egress, its way to Microsoft.
  • Logs carry a message id, never an address. Tests check this.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
podman-compose exec mailrelay python relay.py login     # sign in as RELAY_MAILBOX
podman-compose exec portal python mailer.py --test you@example.com   # one message, end to end
(cd mailrelay && python3 -m pytest)                     # tests, no network

docs.title: Portal: the volunteer side
docs.text:
The portal is where volunteers sign up, sign in and manage their own registration. It's a separate application from the scheduler: its own SQLite database, its own sessions, and no shared code. The only link between the two is the signed sync API, and traffic on it flows one way, from the scheduler to the portal.

Code: portal/. Reference: portal.main and the modules beside it.

docs.title: Why it's separate
docs.text: The portal faces the internet; the scheduler sits behind an access gate. If the portal's host were fully compromised, the attacker would get volunteer names, email ciphertext and a copy of the schedule. They wouldn't get organizer accounts, notes, ratings, radio history, the scheduler's cookie secret, or a single readable email address. The portal can't decrypt addresses, and it has no way to call the scheduler.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Module What it does main The app and its startup. Runs one worker, since SQLite has one writer. config Settings from the environment. Refuses to start without the shared keys. db SQLite connections, migrations, the revision counter, portal_kv and the audit log. security Email HMAC and encryption, token hashing, request signing. ratelimit Per-address and per-client buckets in the database. mailer Sends through the relay, SMTP, or .eml files. routers/auth Sign-in links, sessions, and GET /api/portal/me. routers/signup The signup form, and changing, cancelling and rejoining. routers/sync The API the scheduler calls. routers/branding The title, logos and contact details (email, website, code of conduct) the scheduler pushed. signup_fields The questionnaire in force, and checking answers against it. content The organizer-editable landing page, questionnaire and invite email: defaults, checks, the sandboxed templates and the safe Markdown.

The volunteer pages themselves are routes in the frontend under /apply/, and nginx sends /api/portal/* here.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
Volunteers have no passwords. They sign in with a magic link mailed to their address:

  1. request_link mails a single-use link, valid for 15 minutes, to a registered address.
  2. The link opens /apply/verify, which does nothing until the volunteer presses the button. Mail scanners fetch links, so a GET never spends a token.
  3. The button's POST spends the token in one conditional UPDATE, so two clicks can't both win, and starts a session: 12 hours, or 90 days with Remember this browser.

Only SHA-256 hashes of tokens and session ids are stored. A copy of portal.db isn't enough to sign in as anyone.

Link requests are rate-limited per address and per client, where an IPv6 client counts by its /64. Each request also takes at least 250 ms, so timing doesn't reveal whether an address is registered.

docs.title: What organizers can change
docs.text:
The landing page, the questionnaire and the early-access invite email are edited in the scheduler's Volunteer Portal dialog and pushed here, where each push is checked again before anything is stored:

  • Templates (the landing page's Markdown and the invite) are Jinja, rendered in the sandbox and cut down further: variables from a fixed list, {% if %}, comparisons and a few text filters. No loops, set, includes, calls or attribute access.
  • Markdown is rendered with raw HTML and images off, and links only to web pages, email addresses and this site.
  • The questionnaire must be a shape the form and the server's validation understand.

Until a part is saved, the portal uses its default, which is what the site said before this was editable.

docs.title: Signing up
docs.text:
Signup is email first:

  1. Email. A registered address is told to sign in instead. Any other gets a signup link.
  2. The link gives a signup session, which can do exactly one thing: submit the form.
  3. About you, shifts, questions, review. The form submits the name, two preferred timeslots in order, any extra timeslots, and the questionnaire answers.
  4. The portal creates a pending volunteer with a p-… id and upgrades the session in place. An organizer approves them in the scheduler.

Signup is open only when an organizer has opened it, the email public key is on the portal, and there are two non-overlapping timeslots with space. Otherwise the page shows it as closed or full. An early-access invite link gets one person past "closed", but never past "full". The invite is spent at submit, not when the email is typed.

The two preferred timeslots can't overlap. Space is checked again inside the submit's transaction, so two people can't take the last place at once. remaining comes from the scheduler's snapshot, which includes any overbooking allowance, and the portal counts down from it until the next push.

docs.title: A volunteer's own page
docs.text:
/apply/me shows the volunteer's status, their assigned shifts, their picks and their answers. While pending or approved, they can:

  • Change their shifts. The same rules as signup. A shift they already hold can be kept even when it reads as full. Dropping a shift they're assigned to is allowed: the page warns them, and the scheduler flags it for an organizer.
  • Change the answers marked editable (T-shirt size, dinner, flexibility).
  • Cancel. Their places go back at once. The picks are kept, so they can rejoin later.
  • Rejoin after cancelling, choosing shifts again. Their approval was never touched.
  • Sign out, here or everywhere.

docs.title: Email addresses
docs.text:
Value What it is Who can reverse it email_hmac HMAC-SHA256 of the lowercased address, with EMAIL_HMAC_KEY nobody (but an address can be checked against it, with the key) email_enc RSA-OAEP ciphertext under the organizers' public key only private.pem, which never comes here

A unique index on email_hmac is what prevents two signups for one address, even within the same second.

Since the portal can't decrypt addresses, it only ever mails an address someone has just typed: a sign-in link, during their own request. The one exception is admin mail the scheduler asks for (organizer invites, password resets and early-access invites). Each is a fixed template whose link must point at this deployment's own site, and each is rate-limited. Every other message to volunteers is sent offline, by vol_mail.

docs.title: The sync API
docs.text:
The scheduler signs every request with SYNC_SECRET: method, path, timestamp, nonce and a hash of the body. A timestamp more than 300 seconds off, or a nonce seen before, is refused. Every failure is the same bare 401. Every POST carries an op_id, and a repeat gets the stored result back, so a retry can't apply twice.

Call What it does GET heartbeat, GET config Health, cursors, key fingerprints, settings GET volunteers?since= Volunteers changed since a cursor, with their picks POST schedule Replace the schedule snapshot POST volunteers Apply organizer decisions, and re-keys to a badge number POST branding, settings, signup_invites, announcements Replace each POST send_admin_mail Send one admin message POST content Replace the landing page, questionnaire and invite email, each checked here first POST purge_volunteers Delete volunteers outright, with their sessions and rate-limit counters POST email_index Fill in email_hmac for volunteers who have only ciphertext, from values made offline with the private key

docs.title: Data
docs.text: SQLite at /data/portal.db on the portal_data volume, with WAL and foreign keys on. The schema version is PRAGMA user_version, separate from the scheduler's, and the portal migrates itself on startup. Back it up with sqlite3 .backup, never cp. See Deployment → Backups.

docs.title: vol_mail: schedule emails
docs.text:
vol_mail sends each volunteer their shifts, with a QR code per shift for the check-in desk to scan. It runs on an organizer's own machine, usually twice before the conference: a draft, then a final after adjustments.

It isn't part of the website. No container copies it, and the site never sends this mail:

  • The site provides the template, as a package downloaded from Call for Volunteers → Schedule Email.
  • The site provides the data, through the read-only Export API.
  • The tool decrypts the addresses with the organizers' private.pem, and sends through Microsoft Graph with the same app registration as the mail relay.

Code: tools/vol_mail/vol_mail.py. Step-by-step instructions are in tools/vol_mail/README.md, beside the tool. Reference: tools.vol_mail.vol_mail.

docs.title: The commands
docs.text: Command What it does fetch Downloads the volunteers, with their shifts, check-in codes and encrypted addresses, into box.json. The only step that talks to the site. preview Writes one volunteer's message as .eml, .html and .txt files. Sends nothing. send --dry-run Decrypts every address, builds every message, and writes the round's plan. send Sends exactly the plan, after you type send.

docs.title: What it needs
docs.text: What Where it comes from An API key with volunteers:read, volunteers:email and checkin:codes Admin → API Keys. Save it to a file named api_key*. The template package Call for Volunteers → Schedule Email → Download package private.pem The organizers' private key GRAPH_TENANT_ID, GRAPH_CLIENT_ID, VOL_MAIL_MAILBOX The relay's app registration, and an account with Send As on the sender MAIL_SENDER (or --from) The From address, the same as the relay's

docs.title: Rules it enforces
docs.text:
• A dry run first. The real run refuses if the package or the box changed since the plan was made.
  • Resumable. If a round is interrupted, or some messages fail, run the same command again. Anyone already sent in that round is skipped.
  • Only the changes. --only-changed-since draft sends the final only to volunteers whose shifts changed since the draft.
  • At most 20 a minute, and a 429 from Graph is waited out.
  • No addresses on disk. The round's state holds vol_ids and hashes only. box.json holds ciphertext and check-in codes, is written owner-only, and should be deleted afterwards.
  • The sign-in stays in memory. There's no token file to protect afterwards.

docs.title: Check-in codes
docs.text:
A shift's code depends only on the volunteer and the slot, so a draft's code still works if that shift didn't change. A code stops working when its slot is reassigned, or when an organizer uses App Settings → Rotate key, which voids every code. Send again afterwards.

The text version of each shift carries the code as text too, which the desk can type into the scanner's manual entry if a code won't scan.
